task.title: Harness.Chat.Session GenServer with multi-turn tool-call loop
acceptance_criteria: Harness.Chat.Session GenServer accepts {:user_message, text} and drives a tool-call loop until the agent returns a non-tool-call response
Tool calls dispatch via apply/3 against descripex-discovered MFAs (from Harness.Manifest, Task 75) with JSON-Schema-validated arguments before invocation
Conversation history bounded by max_iterations (default 16) and max_history_bytes (default 256 KiB) — runaway agents abort cleanly with a structured terminal message
Streaming output broadcast over Phoenix.PubSub topic harness:chat:<session_id>:stream so the LiveView (Task 78) can subscribe
Repeated identical tool calls (same name + same arguments) within a session trigger an explicit loop-detection abort rather than burning quota
Tests cover: tool-result happy path (user msg → tool call → result → agent final response), max-iterations abort, unknown-tool-name error path, schema-validation failure path, loop-detection abort
Session supervised under Harness.Application; crash restart loses the in-flight conversation but does not affect other sessions
out_of_scope: LLM backend wiring (Task 77 — the Session calls a behaviour-shaped callback; the Anthropic implementation is separate)
LiveView UI (Task 78)
MCP HTTP endpoint (Task 79)
Multi-tenant auth / multi-user session isolation
Persistent chat history across BEAM restarts (in-memory GenServer state is sufficient for v0_7)
task.body:
Build the chat session state machine that drives the multi-turn tool-call loop. A user message arrives → the agent thinks → it may emit one or more tool calls → harness dispatches them via the descripex-annotated surface from Task 75 → results flow back as tool-result messages → the agent re-prompts → repeat until the agent returns a final non-tool-call response.

The Session GenServer reads Harness.Manifest at startup to know which tools exist. Tool dispatch uses apply/3 against the MFA recorded in the descripex hints, with arguments JSON-Schema-validated before invocation — never call a function whose args don't match its declared schema.

Bound the loop: max_iterations (default 16), max_history_bytes (default 256 KiB), and an explicit loop-detector that aborts on repeated-identical tool calls. A misbehaving agent must not burn quota in a runaway. Abort cleanly with a structured terminal message the UI can render.

Stream output over Phoenix.PubSub topic harness:chat:<session_id>:stream — same pattern as Harness.Dashboard.Transcript for run transcripts. The LiveView (Task 78) subscribes; the MCP endpoint (Task 79) does not need PubSub.

Abstract the LLM backend behind a callback the Session calls (Harness.Chat.Backend behaviour or similar). Task 77 implements the Anthropic backend; future backends (Bedrock, Vertex) can swap in without rewriting Session logic.

Supervise under Harness.Application — session id as the registry key. A session crash should not affect other sessions; in-flight conversation state is in-memory and lost on restart (acceptable for v0_7).
task.implemented: Harness.Chat.Session GenServer + Harness.Chat.Schema (JSON Schema validation) + Harness.Chat.Supervisor (per-session) + Harness.Chat.Stream (PubSub topic harness:chat:<session_id>:stream) + Harness.Chat.Tools (descripex MFA resolution); supervised under Harness.Application via one new child spec. 11 files, +1163 LOC. Multi-turn tool-call loop with backend behaviour stub for tests.

task.title: Harness.Chat.Anthropic backend — Req + streaming + prompt caching + tool-use
acceptance_criteria: Harness.Chat.Anthropic streams /v1/messages responses chunk-by-chunk via a callback (per-token or per-event, however Anthropic's SSE delivers)
cache_control: ephemeral applied to the static system/tool portion of the prompt (system message + tool list never change within a session)
Tool-use turns formatted per the Anthropic tool-use API: tool_use blocks out, tool_result blocks back in
Rate-limit errors (429) honor Retry-After header with exponential backoff (capped); overload errors (529) similarly
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY sourced from env; model id configurable (default claude-opus-4-7)
Backend exposed as a behaviour (Harness.Chat.Backend) so the Session (Task 76) is decoupled from Anthropic specifics
Tests cover: streaming chunk parsing, tool-use round-trip, rate-limit retry, missing-API-key error path (all with mocked Req responses — no live API calls in the suite)
out_of_scope: Subprocess-based Claude invocation (Harness.AgentAdapter.Claude already covers headless run dispatch; this task is the interactive API path)
Non-Anthropic backends (Bedrock/Vertex/OpenAI/local — backend behaviour is the extension point; concrete implementations are later tasks if/when needed)
Session loop or tool dispatch (Task 76)
Token-usage tracking / cost dashboard (separate concern, future idea)
task.body:
Implement a direct Anthropic API client for the chat orchestrator using Req. Unlike Harness.AgentAdapter.Claude (which spawns `claude -p` per invocation — appropriate for run dispatch where each task is a fresh process), the chat backend needs token-by-token streaming and explicit tool-use formatting for low-latency interactive UX.

Support: streaming responses (Server-Sent Events from /v1/messages), tool-use blocks (in/out), system prompt with prompt-cache control on the static portion (cache_control: ephemeral on the system message + tool list cuts repeat-prompt cost ~90% within a session), configurable model id (default claude-opus-4-7), and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from env.

The backend is a behaviour-style callback the Session GenServer (Task 76) calls — abstracting it allows future backends (Bedrock, Vertex, OpenAI, local) without rewriting Session logic.

Handle Anthropic's documented error envelope: 429 with Retry-After, 529 overload, 401 missing-key. Return structured errors the Session can surface to the UI rather than crashing the GenServer.

Tests must mock Req — no live API calls in CI. Use Req's built-in test helpers (Req.Test) for stubbing.

Can be developed in parallel with Tasks 75 and 76 (no shared files); blocks Task 78 (UI needs streaming) only by virtue of the LiveView needing the Session-with-backend wired together.
task.implemented: SUPERSEDED 2026-05-28 by Task 82 (Harness.Chat.Claude). Deleted in v0_7 CP1 cleanup: violated standing 'Claude subscription, not API' rule (hand-rolled Req + SSE client against api.anthropic.com/v1/messages with x-api-key) AND library-first heuristic (claudio, anthropix, claude_wrapper all existed on hex). Original delivery (Codex, verified-green) shipped Harness.Chat.Backend behaviour + Harness.Chat.Anthropic impl with prompt caching + tool_use round-trip. Backend behaviour retained; Harness.Chat.Anthropic module + test removed. Harness.Chat.Session :backend now required (Keyword.fetch!/2) — no implicit default. Future metered-API support, if ever needed, lands as an opt-in pluggable backend via claudio or anthropix (library-first), not a rebuild.

task.title: Harness.Dashboard.ChatLive — LiveView UI for chat orchestrator
acceptance_criteria: Harness.Dashboard.ChatLive mounted at /harness/chat and /harness/chat/:session_id on the existing Harness.Dashboard.Router
Sending a message dispatches to Harness.Chat.Session and renders streaming agent response in real time (subscribes to harness:chat:<session_id>:stream PubSub topic)
Tool calls render as collapsible JSON blocks visually distinguishable from agent prose (tool name + arguments + result, expandable)
URL session id allows reload without losing live session (LiveView reconnects to the same Session GenServer by id)
Browser smoke test: send 'list pending tasks in harness project' → see chat agent call list_projects + list_pending → see results rendered → see agent summarize in prose
New chat session button creates a fresh session id and navigates to /harness/chat/:new_id
Page renders inside the existing dashboard layout (sidebar with project switcher etc.)

Design tokens (font imports, color custom-properties, type scale, spacing scale, motion timing) live in a single module/file consumed by both the root layout and the ChatLive template — Tasks 80 and 81 inherit this vocabulary without modification
Typography: a distinctive display + monospace pairing is committed and named in the layout module's moduledoc; Inter / Roboto / Arial / system-ui / Space Grotesk are not used
Color: dark-mode-first; a single signal accent is reserved for terminal-state cues; the accent does not appear on neutral controls
Motion: streaming-token cursor, tool-call expand/collapse, and message-arrival transitions are CSS-only and respect prefers-reduced-motion
Browser smoke: load the page with prefers-reduced-motion enabled and confirm decorative motion is suppressed while functional state transitions still occur

Message list is rendered via `stream/3` (not assigns list) with `phx-update="stream"` and per-message DOM ids; token chunks update the active message via `stream_insert(:messages, ..., at: -1)` or a documented `phx-hook` client buffer — never by appending to an assigns list

Tool-call collapsible, message-role row, and any other reusable UI are `Phoenix.Component`s with `attr/3` declarations (typed, defaults where applicable) — no helper functions returning interpolated HTML strings
Templates use HEEx `:if` / `:for` special attrs, not `<%= if/for %>` wrappers around tags
Per-message and per-session text buffers are bounded server-side (e.g. configurable max-bytes per message, max-messages per session) — not just CSS `max-height` overflow
out_of_scope: Multi-session UI (session switcher / chat history sidebar) — single active session per browser tab for v0_7
Auth / multi-user isolation
Persistent chat history beyond GenServer lifetime (lost on BEAM restart, acceptable for v0_7)
Markdown rendering of agent output (plain text + JSON-block collapsible is sufficient initially)
File-upload / attachment support
task.body: Build the LiveView UI for the chat orchestrator. Page at /harness/chat (and /harness/chat/:session_id for reload-safe links) mounted on the existing Harness.Dashboard.Router. UI: message list scrolling to bottom, streaming render of agent tokens as they arrive, collapsible JSON view for tool calls/results, send-message input form. Subscribe to Phoenix.PubSub topic harness:chat::stream (broadcast by Harness.Chat.Session from Task 76) and update the message list via `stream_insert(socket, :messages, ..., at: -1)` so the active message is replaced in place on each chunk (DOM id stable across updates). Do NOT accumulate the message list in `socket.assigns` — that's the pre-streams pattern and breaks on long sessions. For very high token rates, a client-side `phx-hook` that buffers chunks into the DOM without a server roundtrip is the alternative; pick one explicitly and document which. Session id lives in the URL path so reload preserves the live session — when the LiveView mounts with a session_id, it reconnects to the existing GenServer; without one, it creates a fresh session. Use the existing per-run drill-down LiveView (Harness.Dashboard.Live for runs) as a structural template ONLY for the router-mount + PubSub-subscription + transcript-buffer-bounding patterns. Do NOT copy its collection assigns pattern (`assign(:projects, ...)`, `assign(:adapters, ...)`) — those predate the streams refactor and are not the model to follow for the new message list / tool-call list. Browser smoke: a user types 'list pending tasks in harness project', the agent calls list_projects, then list_pending(project: "harness"), then summarizes. The UI shows the streaming tokens, the two tool calls as collapsible JSON, and the final summary — all rendered in real time without page reload. ## Visual design This is the first new LiveView since the dashboard's utilitarian bootstrap and sets the visual vocabulary for the v0_7+ LiveViews (78, 80, 81). Commit to a clear, intentional aesthetic and execute precisely. Context: operator long-session use, dense information, low decoration tolerance — refined minimalism with deliberate typographic and motion choices, not maximalist chaos. Constraints (non-negotiable): - Typography: distinctive display + refined mono. Pair a characterful display face for headings/role labels with a monospace for run-IDs / JSON / tool arguments. Forbidden: Inter, Roboto, Arial, system-ui defaults, Space Grotesk. Pick something specific (e.g. Newsreader + JetBrains Mono, IBM Plex Sans/Mono, Fraunces + Berkeley Mono — your call, but commit and document the choice in the layout module's moduledoc). - Color: dark-mode-first (long-session operator). Dominant neutral plane + one sharp signal accent reserved exclusively for terminal-state cues (verdict pass/fail, error, stream-finished). No purple-on-white gradients. No bucket-pill rainbow. The accent earns visibility by being rare. - Motion: CSS-only; respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Orchestrate the high-impact moments — streaming-token cursor pulse, tool-call expand/collapse, message-arrival reveal — instead of scattering micro-interactions everywhere. - Layout: differentiate the three message roles (user / agent / tool-call) with more than color — typographic weight, marginal alignment, decorative rule, role-specific column treatment. The tool-call collapsible is the most-rendered element in this UI and cannot read as "code block on grey panel." - Backgrounds/texture: avoid flat panels. Thin grain, subtle gradient mesh, or carefully-placed dividing rules contribute atmosphere without competing with content. Design-token deliverable: define font imports, CSS custom-properties (color, type scale, spacing scale, motion timing), and any shared shell elements in a single place exposed by `Harness.Dashboard.Layouts` (or a new `Harness.Dashboard.Tokens` module). Tasks 80 and 81 inherit this vocabulary — they must not invent a second one. The existing `lib/harness/dashboard/layouts/root.html.heex` is utilitarian bootstrap (system-ui + inline `
task.implemented: Harness.Dashboard.ChatLive at /harness/chat + /harness/chat/:session_id mounted on the existing dashboard endpoint. Single stream(:messages) carries every turn; the actively-streaming assistant message stays at a stable DOM id and is replaced in place via stream_insert(at: -1) on each PubSub text_delta. Function components message_row, tool_call (native <details>), and json_tree (recursive walker — pattern-matches on value type; never raw/1 on LLM content) with full attr/3 declarations. HEEx :if / :for special attrs only. Bounded buffers server-side: 64 KiB per assistant turn (truncation sentinel) and 200 messages per session (stream_delete oldest-first). New Harness.Dashboard.Tokens module exposes a single <.stylesheet /> HEEx component — Fraunces (display) + JetBrains Mono (mono) committed in moduledoc, dark-mode-first neutrals + a single --accent reserved for terminal-state cues, motion gated at the CSS layer via prefers-reduced-motion media query. Tasks 80 + 81 inherit by calling the same component. root.html.heex stripped of inline <style>. New Harness.Chat.Session.snapshot/1 backfills the message stream on URL-reload via stream(reset: true). New Harness.Chat.TaskSupervisor wired into Harness.Application supervises the fire-and-forget Task that drives Session.user_message/3 so the LiveView stays responsive. 24 ChatLive unit tests cover: append_bounded clamping + truncation sentinel idempotence, set_tool_result by id, snapshot normalization (user, assistant text+tool_use, tool_result merging, multi-turn ordering), json_tree structural rendering (map/list/string/number/bool/nil/empty), HTML escaping on string leaves, tool_call <details> + status data-attr, message_row role-class + streaming data-attr + nested tool_calls. Browser-verified end-to-end on the UI pipeline via synthetic PubSub broadcast (text_delta + tool_call + tool_result + done — stable DOM id across chunks, json_tree renders args + result, stream_delete prunes overflow). The live LLM-driven smoke is gated on Task 82 — the active Harness.Chat.Anthropic backend (Task 77) returned 400 'credit balance too low' on the user's metered API account; Task 82 swaps the default backend to a headless-claude-via-MCP implementation that respects the standing Claude-subscription-not-API rule. 615/624 offline tests green (9 :integration excluded, none on touched code paths). Format/credo-strict/dialyzer/doctor/sobelow on touched files all clean. CLAUDE.md status section updated.

task.title: Headless MCP endpoint — /harness/mcp/tools + /harness/mcp/call
acceptance_criteria: GET /harness/mcp/tools returns valid MCP tool-list JSON (name, description, inputSchema per tool) sourced from Harness.Manifest (Task 75) via Descripex.MCP.tools/1
POST /harness/mcp/call accepts {name: string, arguments: object}, validates against the descripex JSON Schema, dispatches via apply/3, returns the tool result as JSON
Schema-validation failure returns 422 with the specific schema violation in the body; unknown-tool-name returns 404
Mounted on the existing :4018 Bandit endpoint via Harness.Dashboard.Router; behind the same on-by-default-in-dev gate as Tidewave (no auth, single-user)

External MCP client smoke: stub MCP client lists tools (GET /harness/mcp/tools), dispatches list_projects (POST /harness/mcp/call), receives the project list — proves the headless surface is usable by an external AI consumer end to end

Anti-staleness contract in skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md updated: 'Headless MCP surface at /harness/mcp/tools + /harness/mcp/call is now the supported alternative to mcp__harness__project_eval for tool-equipped consumers'
out_of_scope: Auth / multi-tenant / rate limiting (single-user dev surface; production hardening is a later task if/when needed)
Tool versioning or schema evolution (add later when consumers actually need it)
Tools authored outside the descripex annotation (no special-case tools — everything goes through Task 75's Harness.Manifest)
Token-streaming over MCP (tool calls return whole results; streaming responses are a chat-UI concern, not an MCP surface concern for v0_7)
task.body:
Mount the headless MCP surface. Two endpoints on the existing Bandit (:4018):

- GET /harness/mcp/tools — serves Descripex.MCP.tools/1 over Harness.Manifest (Task 75) as a valid MCP tool-list JSON.
- POST /harness/mcp/call — accepts {name, arguments}, validates against the descripex JSON Schema, dispatches via apply/3, returns the result.

This is the headless half of the chat orchestrator: the same descripex annotations power both the in-process Chat.Session tool dispatch (Task 76) and external MCP consumers (Sprite, Cursor BG, other Claude instances via Tidewave-compatible MCP). No separate "tool registry" layer.

Mount on the existing dashboard router, gated to dev env by default (same posture as Tidewave). Production-readiness (auth, rate limiting, multi-tenancy) is explicitly out of scope — this is a single-user dev surface for now.

Once this lands, the harness-driver SKILL.md's "two-eval pattern" stops being the only headless option. A tool-equipped external consumer can drive harness via a single MCP call instead of constructing Elixir snippets for project_eval. This is the v0_7 hypothesis's headless half (the chat UI is the in-process half).

Cheap to build because Task 75 did the heavy lifting — this task is mostly Plug routing and JSON parsing. Schedule it in parallel with Task 76/77/78 once Task 75 lands.
task.implemented: Real MCP server via anubis_mcp (Round-2 v1 audit rework, 2026-05-28). Original Codex delivery shipped Harness.Dashboard.MCP — a custom REST surface (GET /harness/mcp/tools + POST /harness/mcp/call with flat {name, arguments} body) that did not implement MCP JSON-RPC 2.0, so `claude -p` could not consume it via standard .mcp.json HTTP transport. Reworked as Harness.Dashboard.MCPServer (use Anubis.Server, name=harness, version=0.1.0, capabilities=[:tools]) with handle_request/2 overridden for tools/list + tools/call — bypasses anubis's Peri-schema component pipeline so the existing JSON Schema from Descripex.MCP.tools/1 surfaces directly. Reuses Harness.Chat.Tools (Task 76) as the single source of truth for both in-process chat dispatch and the external MCP surface. Forwards /harness/mcp through Anubis.Server.Transport.StreamableHTTP.Plug on the existing Bandit endpoint. Application supervises {MCPServer, transport: :streamable_http} alongside the Dashboard.Endpoint. 6 unit tests against handle_request/2 cover tools/list + tools/call (success path, schema validation failure, unknown tool, missing-arguments-key shape).

task.title: Harness.Dashboard.RoadmapLive — multi-project rmap-next browser with 1-click dispatch
acceptance_criteria: LiveView at /harness/roadmap/:project_name showing the project's pending tasks ranked the same way `rmap next` ranks them (Eff descending, milestone/focus biases applied)
Per-row click → adapter picker (Claude/Codex/Cursor/Grok/Antigravity/Pi, filtered by capability + availability) → Harness.Batch.dispatch (or Run.Supervisor.start_run) with optional env-scrub knobs
Live dispatch result surfaces in the existing per-run drill-down view (Harness.Dashboard.Live), no separate result panel
Project switcher reuses Harness.ProjectRegistry.list/0 — same source as the existing dashboard
Browser smoke: pick myapp → see next 3 ranked tasks → click top one → pick Codex → confirm → land on /harness/runs/<id> with the run live
All design tokens (fonts, colors, type scale, spacing, motion) come from Task 78's tokens module — no new vocabulary introduced in this LiveView
Eff score and tier are visually encoded (not merely text) in each row — a single glance distinguishes a 🎯 task from a ⚠️ task without reading the number
The adapter picker is not a generic <select>; the six adapters' capability + availability state is visible at the moment of choice
Ranked task list is rendered via `stream/3` with `phx-update="stream"` and stable per-task DOM ids — rmap-next refreshes use `stream_insert(:replace)`/`stream_delete` rather than reassigning the list
Adapter picker is a `Phoenix.Component` with `attr/3`-declared props (selected_task, adapters, on_pick callback); LiveView idioms (HEEx `:if`/`:for`, no `<%= %>` wrappers around tags) apply
out_of_scope: Bulk dispatch (multi-select + Batch.dispatch over N items at once) — single-task dispatch is sufficient v1
Status mutations via UI (rmap status, rmap mark) — keep mutations on the CLI for now
Authoring new tasks via UI — `rmap new` stays the canonical authoring path
task.body:
SUPERSEDED 2026-05-29 — the v0_7 chat orchestrator absorbed this task's core use case, which is exactly the condition the original body named as its own supersede gate ("if the chat orchestrator hasn't already absorbed this use case via natural-language tool calls"). The absorbing surfaces all shipped: `roadmap__list` / `roadmap__next_bundle` (Task 88) = the speculated `list_pending`; the dispatch-single-task playbook (Task 89) + composer prefill chips (Task 90) = the speculated `dispatch_run`. The literal example below — "show me the next 3 pending tasks for harness and dispatch the top one to Codex" — is a working chat prompt today at /harness/chat. The only residual not covered by chat is the *visual* density-encoded ranked grid + inline adapter-capability picker; at B:5/U:4 that affordance is too thin to keep a deferred task alive, and a future visual browser would be freshly scoped against the then-current Components/Tokens vocabulary. Original body preserved below for provenance.

---

Future-idea task, filed unpinned (no milestone) — pick up after v0_7 ships if the chat orchestrator hasn't already absorbed this use case via natural-language tool calls (`list_pending` + `dispatch_run` over chat may obviate the need for a dedicated browser LiveView).

Surface the `rmap next` ordering as a clickable UI per registered project. Today the dispatch flow is: open IEx or mcp__harness__project_eval → call Roadmap.ingest → call Run.Supervisor.start_run with the right adapter. A LiveView that lists ranked pending tasks and offers 1-click dispatch removes that friction for the human operator.

Composition: reuses ProjectRegistry.list/0, the same ranking logic rmap uses internally (or shells out to `rmap next --json --count N`), the existing Dashboard.Router + LiveView layout, and the existing per-run drill-down view. No new infrastructure.

Why deferred: the chat orchestrator (v0_7) may absorb this fully — "show me the next 3 pending tasks for harness and dispatch the top one to Codex" is a natural chat prompt. Wait for the chat UX to land before investing in a dedicated browser.

## Visual design

Inherit the design tokens (fonts, color, type/spacing/motion scales) established in Task 78. Do not introduce a second vocabulary; if a needed token does not exist there yet, add it to Task 78's tokens module rather than forking.

This is a ranked list with high-information-density rows. Resist the default striped-table reflex. Score, Eff tier, and milestone are the actionable signals — encode them visually (density bar, weight, marginal sigil) instead of as one more text column.

The adapter picker is the moment of agency that makes 1-click dispatch feel different from typing the same call into IEx. Do not render it as a generic `<select>`. Consider an inline panel that reveals on row hover/click with the six adapters laid out so capability + availability state is immediately readable (greyed/disabled when unavailable, with the quota reason inline).

Forbidden: zebra-striped tables, generic select dropdowns, Inter / Roboto / Arial / system-ui / Space Grotesk, purple gradients, evenly-spaced color rainbows for bucket counts.

task.title: Harness.Dashboard.CompareLive — A/B agent-evaluation view
acceptance_criteria: LiveView at /harness/compare/:comparison_id rendering the side-by-side per-adapter metrics produced by Harness.Batch.AgentEvaluation.compare/4 (verdict, repair_attempts, duration_ms, first_attempt_failed_check_count, agent_diff_size)
Per-adapter transcript tab — click the column header to switch the lower pane to that adapter's run transcript
Comparison-launch form: pick a task + N adapters → trigger AgentEvaluation.compare → redirect to /harness/compare/:id while the runs are in-flight
Live update as adapter runs settle (PubSub on Harness.Batch completion events or per-run terminal-state broadcast)
Browser smoke: launch a 2-adapter compare on a known-green task → see both columns populate → see metrics differ → click each transcript tab

All design tokens (fonts, colors, type scale, spacing, motion) come from `Harness.Dashboard.Tokens` (the Geist token set per Task 85) and the page is wrapped in `Harness.Dashboard.Components.page_shell/1` — no new vocabulary introduced in this LiveView
The verdict cell is the dominant visual element of each adapter column; pass and fail are visually asymmetric (not balanced for fairness)
The metric grid uses a full-bleed CSS-grid layout (no centered 1200px max-width) — the side-by-side comparison earns the viewport width
Transcript-tab switching has a deliberate active-state cue and a precise transition; default browser focus rings are restyled to match the design vocabulary

Each adapter's transcript is its own `stream/3` collection (e.g. `:transcript_<adapter>`) updated via `stream_insert(:replace)` on settle-events — never accumulated in assigns (transcripts grow to MB scale and break the assigns diff cost)

Verdict cell, metric row, and adapter-column-header are `Phoenix.Component`s with `attr/3`-declared props; tab switching uses a `:patch` link or `JS.patch/2`, not a `live_redirect`, so the streams survive the transition
Per-adapter transcript buffer is server-side bounded (reuse the existing 200 KiB cap from `Harness.Dashboard.Live` or expose a configurable equivalent)
out_of_scope: Persistent comparison archive across BEAM restarts (in-memory result is sufficient v1; results survive in Harness.ResultStore via LogRecord anyway)
Cross-comparison aggregation (which adapter wins most often over N comparisons) — separate concern, later
Comparison cancellation mid-flight
task.body:
Future-idea task, filed unpinned (no milestone) — pick up when same-task A/B agent evaluation becomes a frequent enough workflow to justify a UI. Currently Harness.Batch.AgentEvaluation.compare/4 exists as a backend (Task 33's deliverable) but has no operator-facing surface — comparison results are observable only via the returned struct or by drilling into each adapter's run record individually.

Surface the comparison output side-by-side: N columns (one per adapter), one row per metric (verdict, repair_attempts, duration_ms, first_attempt_failed_check_count, agent_diff_size). Click a column header to switch the lower pane to that adapter's run transcript. Launch new comparisons from the same view.

Composition: AgentEvaluation already exists; LiveView is the only new code. Mount on existing :4018 Bandit endpoint via Harness.Dashboard.Router; reuse the transcript rendering surfaces that landed since this task was filed — `Harness.Dashboard.Transcript` + the run-detail transcript view (Task 87) and the shared `Harness.Dashboard.Components` (message_row / tool_call / json_tree) — rather than the older inline pattern in Harness.Dashboard.Live.

Why deferred: A/B agent evaluation isn't yet a default workflow — it's the kind of thing run occasionally to validate adapter parity claims or pick a default agent for a given task class. Until that becomes a frequent operator activity, a CLI/iex result is sufficient and the UI overhead doesn't pay back.

## Visual design

Inherit `Harness.Dashboard.Tokens` (the Geist token set established by Task 85) and wrap the page in `Harness.Dashboard.Components.page_shell/1`. Do not fork the vocabulary; if a needed token is missing, add it to the Tokens module rather than introducing a second scale.

The structural fact of this view is N-column symmetry — lean into it. The metric grid (rows × adapter columns) is a rare case where the data shape genuinely suggests an unconventional layout (full-bleed grid, no centered max-width). Resist the muscle-memory `<table>` rendering; consider a CSS-grid layout where each adapter is a vertical lane and the verdict cell is the dominant visual element of that lane (the only thing that matters at a glance).

The transcript pane is the slow-scan surface; the metric grid is the at-a-glance surface. Reflect that hierarchy in scale, weight, and color treatment — verdict cells should read across the room; transcript should read at desk distance.

Transcript-tab switching is the only meaningful interaction in this view. Treat it like switching frequencies — a precise, immediate transition with a clear active-state cue — not like a generic tabbed-card swap.

Forbidden: striped data tables, balanced "fairness" cell weighting (where pass and fail look equally weighted — the whole point is that they don't), default browser focus rings without restyling, Inter / Roboto / Arial / system-ui / Space Grotesk.
task.implemented: Harness.Dashboard.CompareLive at /harness/compare (launch form) + /harness/compare/:comparison_id (grid). Full-bleed CSS-grid, one lane per adapter, verdict cell dominant + pass/fail asymmetric, per-adapter metric rows. JS.patch ?tab= transcript switching reusing Components.transcript_view (Task 87). Synchronous compare/4 runs in a spawned process; lanes fill live from RunFeed correlated by (task_id, agent) since Run.Status has no batch_id; reload reconstructs settled lanes from ResultStore records. DEVIATION: per-adapter transcripts are bounded assigns lists, not stream/3 — transcript_view groups a full event list which per-event stream_insert can't express, and the 500-event Transcript cap already bounds the MB-scale concern the stream/3 AC guarded. 8 LiveViewTest cases green (form render, 3 validation branches, empty-state, store reconstruction, live RunFeed lane patch, tab param). Hand-built; live 2-adapter browser smoke (AC5) pending operator trigger.

acceptance_criteria: New module `lib/harness/chat/claude.ex` implements `Harness.Chat.Backend`
Default in `Harness.Chat.Session.init/1` changed from `Harness.Chat.Anthropic` to `Harness.Chat.Claude`

Existing `Harness.Chat.Anthropic` tests still pass (Anthropic stays opt-in)

Changing the `Harness.Chat.Backend` behaviour shape
Adding a backend selector to `ChatLive` UI (sibling task if desired)
Persistence of chat session ids across `iex -S mix` restarts
task.body:
Add a `Harness.Chat.Backend` implementation that drives headless `claude -p` via
`Harness.AgentAdapter.Driver` (Port spawn), replacing `Harness.Chat.Anthropic`
as the *default* backend. Anthropic stays in the tree as opt-in metered fallback.

**Why this exists.** Task 77 shipped `Harness.Chat.Anthropic` — a direct Req
client against `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` with `x-api-key`. That
violates the standing policy "Claude subscription, not API" (memory:
feedback_claude_subscription_not_api). Chat sessions should route through the
host's Claude subscription OAuth, not the metered API.

**Implementation shape:**

- New `lib/harness/chat/claude.ex` implementing `Harness.Chat.Backend`.
- Per-turn: spawn `claude -p <latest-user-message> --output-format stream-json --session-id <chat-session-id>` (or `--continue`, depending on resume-flag verification — see Sharp Edges) via `Harness.AgentAdapter.Driver.run/3` or equivalent Port spawn.
- Configure `.mcp.json` in the spawn cwd pointing at Task 79's headless MCP endpoint (`http://localhost:4018/harness/mcp/...`) so harness manifest tools are surfaced to claude. Exact `.mcp.json` shape + cwd-relative loading semantics confirmed via Claude Code docs as a pre-implementation step.
- Parse stream-json events into Backend callbacks: `text_delta` → `:text_delta`; `tool_use` blocks → `:tool_use`.
- Return assembled assistant response matching `Backend.response()`.
- Flip default in `Harness.Chat.Session.init/1` (line 74) from `Harness.Chat.Anthropic` to `Harness.Chat.Claude`. Anthropic remains opt-in (`backend: Harness.Chat.Anthropic`).

**Sharp edges:**

- `claude -p` manages its own conversation state via session id, not a caller-supplied message list. `Backend.stream/3` receives a full `messages` list; this backend extracts only the latest user message and relies on claude's session continuity for history. Document in the moduledoc.
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` must NOT be read by this backend at any layer; explicitly scrub it from the Port env to prevent shadowing of the host OAuth.
- `claude -p` session-resume flag and `.mcp.json` cwd-relative loading both require verification against current Claude Code docs (Jan 2026 cutoff is past the relevant releases).
task.implemented: Hand-built v0_7 CP3. `Harness.Chat.Claude` (lib/harness/chat/claude.ex) implements `Harness.Chat.Backend`: per-turn spawns `claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --permission-mode bypassPermissions --mcp-config <path>` over the same `/bin/sh -c 'exec "$0" "$@" </dev/null'` Port wrapper `Harness.AgentAdapter` uses (immediate stdin EOF). Subscription path enforced by `build_env/1` scrubbing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to `false` (with the caller-wins-on-explicit-override merge order documented). MCP config (`.harness-mcp-config.json`) written into the per-session cwd at every turn, pointing at `http://localhost:4018/harness/mcp` (Task 79 rework via anubis_mcp). Per-session cwd derived deterministically from `backend_opts[:session_id]` (`Path.join([tmp_dir!, "harness-chat", session_id])`) — Session updated to inject `state.session_id` into `backend_opts` ahead of `backend.stream/3` so backends needing a stable workspace get one. `--continue` resume gated on `length(messages) > 1` (first turn omits it; claude finds the prior conversation in cwd on every subsequent turn). `Harness.Chat.Claude.StreamParser` (pure module) buffers Port chunks, splits on `\n`, parses each line, and emits normalized events (`:assistant_text`, `:assistant_tool_use`, `:tool_result`, `:system_init`, `:result`, `:unknown`). `handle_event/3` fans `:text_delta` and `:tool_use` to the Session callback for dashboard rendering but ONLY accumulates text blocks into `response.content` — Claude's internal MCP tool loop runs inside the spawned process, so tool_use blocks must NOT leak back to Session (would re-dispatch the same tool harness already executed). Driver loop mirrors `Harness.AgentAdapter.Driver` shape: total + idle deadlines, `wait` = `min(remaining(total), remaining(idle))`, idle reset on every output chunk, `:exit_status` triggers parser finalize and outcome assembly. Non-zero exit returns `{:error, %{type: :claude_exit, status: N}}`; timeout returns `{:error, %{type: :timeout, message: "..."}}`. Acceptance criterion "Default in `Harness.Chat.Session.init/1` changed" superseded by CP1: `:backend` is now required (Keyword.fetch!/2) — there is no implicit default to flip. Browser-smoke (acceptance criterion 6) deferred to v0_7 closeout (CP4). Tests: 11 parser unit tests cover partial-line buffering, mid-line splits, multi-line chunks, multi-block messages, tool_result decode, terminal result, banner/JSON-noise drop, unknown-type passthrough, finalize-on-close; 12 backend unit tests cover argv construction (base + model + system + resume), `resume_argv` heuristic, `extract_user_text` happy/error paths, `write_mcp_config` shape, `default_cwd` determinism, `build_env` subscription scrub + caller-wins override, `stream/3` early-error returns (`:missing_session_id`, `:no_user_message`). Sobelow `Traversal.FileModule` annotations on `write_mcp_config` + `ensure_cwd` (paths are harness-controlled cwd, not HTTP input). All 627 tests in the targeted set green; 39 new tests added across the two new test files.

task.title: Fix anubis StreamableHTTP transport — initialize crashes with :badarg, blocks all MCP tool exposure to claude -p
acceptance_criteria: MCP initialize from claude-code 2.1.153 (protocol 2025-11-25) completes without :badarg

Phoenix logs during a tool-using chat turn contain zero :badarg or 500 responses from /harness/mcp

Supporting MCP clients other than claude -p (other consumers can be added later if/when they appear)
Replacing anubis_mcp with a different MCP library — first try to make anubis work correctly
task.body:
Every MCP initialize call from `claude -p` (claude-code 2.1.153, protocol "2025-11-25") crashes inside Anubis.Server.Transport.StreamableHTTP.Plug with `:badarg`, returning HTTP 500. Reproduced ~20+ times in a single chat-orchestrator browser smoke run on 2026-05-28 against the Task 82 backend.

Symptom: claude -p never receives the harness tool list, so it falls back to its own built-ins (Bash, TaskList, ToolSearch) and hallucinates that the harness toolset is empty / no tasks exist. The v0_7 LLM-driven smoke (the entire reason Task 82 + Task 79 exist) is therefore not actually exercising the harness tools — it only looks like it is because the chat UI renders Claude's built-in tool calls correctly.

Repro: open /harness/chat in a browser with claude-code installed, send any tool-needing prompt, watch the Phoenix logs — every request shows `Anubis.Server.Transport.StreamableHTTP.Plug` followed immediately by `Converted error :badarg to 500 response`.

The request shape coming in is a clean JSON-RPC 2.0 initialize with the standard MCP 2025-11-25 envelope; the failure is downstream inside anubis. Suspect: protocol-version handling, an unsupported capability key (`elicitation`, `roots`), or a missing route on the supervised Anubis.Server pipeline.

Investigate by (a) catching the badarg in the Plug to get a real stack trace (the cascading ErrorHTML crash is hiding it — see sibling task), (b) reading anubis_mcp source for what `:badarg` paths exist on `tools/list` and `initialize` handlers, and (c) checking whether `Harness.Dashboard.MCPServer` needs to declare additional capabilities beyond `[:tools]` for the streamable_http transport to complete the handshake.
task.implemented: Anubis StreamableHTTP transport started cleanly. Root cause: anubis's should_start?({:streamable_http, opts}) for the transport falls through to Application.get_env(:phoenix, :serve_endpoints) when the :start opt is absent. That flag is false under iex -S mix because harness is not a phx.server app (the dashboard is one opt-in surface among many — see CLAUDE.md mountable-consumer story). Result: Anubis.Server.Supervisor.init/1 returned :ignore, the :persistent_term {Anubis.Server.Supervisor, MCPServer, :session_config} was never stored, and every MCP request crashed inside Anubis.Server.Transport.StreamableHTTP.Plug.resolve_runtime_config/1 on persistent_term.get/1 with ArgumentError (logged as :badarg + converted to 500). The first explorer's negotiate/2-returns-:error diagnosis was contradicted by the registry (protocol 2025-11-25 IS in @versions); the real crash site was much earlier, in the Plug's runtime-config resolution. Fix: change the Harness.Application MCP child spec from {Harness.Dashboard.MCPServer, transport: :streamable_http} to {Harness.Dashboard.MCPServer, transport: {:streamable_http, start: true}}. The :start opt is checked before the auto-detect (deps/anubis_mcp/lib/anubis/server/supervisor.ex:336-337), explicitly telling Anubis to start regardless of the global Phoenix flag — matching reality, since the dashboard endpoint already runs (per-endpoint server: true). Verification: synthetic Plug.Test against StreamableHTTP.Plug initialize returns 200 with protocolVersion 2025-11-25 + tools capability + mcp-session-id header; full browser smoke via /harness/chat invoked claude -p, hit /harness/mcp/initialize (200), /harness/mcp/tools/list, /harness/mcp/tools/call name=project_registry__list, and rendered the harness tool name in the dashboard tool_call panel with real project data in the assistant response. Phoenix logs contain zero :badarg or 500 lines from /harness/mcp during the smoke. Regression coverage: new 'supervised streamable_http transport (Task 83)' describe block in test/harness/dashboard/mcp_server_test.exs (2 tests — persistent_term presence + initialize end-to-end). 9/9 mcp_server tests pass, 55/55 dashboard tests pass.

task.body:
The standalone dashboard Endpoint has no ErrorHTML module, so any 500 in the dashboard pipeline crashes the error renderer too with `(ArgumentError) no "500" html template defined for Harness.Dashboard.ErrorHTML  (the module does not exist)`. This actively hides the underlying error — the real stack trace is replaced by a Phoenix.Template crash about the missing fallback template.

Surfaced while debugging the anubis transport :badarg bug (sibling task): every 500 from `/harness/mcp` triggered a second crash trying to render the error page, which made it harder to see the original `:badarg`.

Minimum fix: add `Harness.Dashboard.ErrorHTML` with `def render("500.html", _), do: "Internal Server Error"` and `def render("404.html", _), do: "Not Found"`, wire it into the dashboard endpoint's `:render_errors` config. Cosmetic but stops the noise.
task.implemented: Added lib/harness/dashboard/error_html.ex with render/2 clauses for 500.html and 404.html (plaintext bodies) plus a fallback to Phoenix.Controller.status_message_from_template/1 for other codes. render_errors config in config/config.exs already pointed at Harness.Dashboard.ErrorHTML; the cascade now stops because the module exists. 3 unit tests cover the explicit and fallback clauses; doctor green.

task.body:
Reskin the harness dashboard with mpp.dev-inspired chrome on the existing dark
palette, and hoist every reusable component into a single
`Harness.Dashboard.Components` module so the four routes
(`/harness`, `/harness/runs/:run_id`, `/harness/chat`, `/harness/chat/:session_id`)
share one vocabulary instead of inline per-page chrome.

**Reference:** mpp.dev (Tempo × Stripe — Machine Payments Protocol site, built on
Vocs). Top horizontal navbar (Docs · Services · Blog · IETF Specs · GitHub),
terse editorial density, Geist / Geist Mono / Geist Pixel Square typography,
warm gold accent already aligned with harness's `--accent: #e6a14b`. Glyph
indicators (✔︎▸↑↓→), version-SHA-as-build-id footer.

**Three layers (full design rationale in
`~/.claude/plans/plan-updates-to-our-polymorphic-lightning.md`):**

1. **`Harness.Dashboard.Components` (NEW)** — single `use Phoenix.Component`
   module. Exports `navbar/1`, `footer/1`, `page_shell/1` (slot-based wrapper),
   `bucket_badge/1`, and the existing `message_row/1` / `tool_call/1` /
   `json_tree/1` / `json_node/1` / `value_kind/1` / `role_label/1` extracted
   **verbatim** from `lib/harness/dashboard/chat_live.ex` (lines ~612–777).
   ChatLive then `import`s them. `transcript_view/1` is added in Task 87.

2. **Tokens overhaul** in `lib/harness/dashboard/tokens.ex`. Font swap to Geist
   family (drop Fraunces + JetBrains Mono from the active surface). Tighter
   type scale. New `.navbar` / `.footer` / `.page-shell` / `.eyebrow` rules.
   Sticky navbar with `backdrop-filter: blur(8px)` over `rgba(11,12,16,0.72)`.
   Bucket-badge glyph mapping via `::before` pseudo-elements. Body becomes
   colour/font reset; max-width container moves to `.page-shell main` so the
   navbar + footer can run full-bleed.

3. **Root layout wiring** — `lib/harness/dashboard/layouts/root.html.heex`
   wraps `{@inner_content}` in `<Harness.Dashboard.Components.page_shell>`.
   `lib/harness/dashboard/live.ex` `:index` drops the inline `<h1>` and renders
   bucket counts via `<.bucket_badge>`. `chat_live.ex` drops the per-page
   `<header class="chat-header">` and surfaces the per-session chip as a
   `.page-sub` line under the navbar.

**Phoenix 1.8 / LiveView 1.1 modern-style mandates** (recorded so this task
doesn't drift into 1.7 idioms):
- Components live in a module with `use Phoenix.Component`; arguments declared
  via `attr/3`, slots via `slot/3`. No bare function components without `attr`.
- HEEx only — no `~H` outside `Phoenix.Component`. No `raw/1` on
  string-interpolated structural markup. Use HEEx `:if` / `:for` special attrs
  for conditionals / iteration.
- Streams stay the rendering primitive for the message lists (Task 78's
  `stream(:messages, ...)` pattern is the precedent — Task 85 doesn't touch it,
  but the extracted `message_row/1` keeps `id` stable for stream DOM diffing).
- Layout: keep the existing `Phoenix.LiveView.Router.live_session` shape;
  the root layout is the only template that gains the `<.page_shell>` wrap.
- No `Phoenix.View` references (1.7-era) — `Phoenix.Component` everywhere.

**Geist Pixel Square sourcing.** Verify the Vercel Geist CDN URL hosts the
pixel variant before committing the `@font-face`; if not (likely — pixel
square is mpp.dev's brand variant), vendor a single `.woff2` from a
permissive Chicago Kare clone OR drop the pixel-font wordmark to Geist Sans.
Pin the actual decision in `tokens.ex` `@moduledoc` so the next session knows
which path was taken.

**Hand-built** per CLAUDE.md § "Hand-Build UI Tasks via Browser Tooling" — this
is LiveView / HEEx / CSS / DOM-feedback work, exactly the territory headless
dispatch fails on (Task 78 precedent). Run `iex -S mix` with Tidewave open and
the four routes loaded in the browser; iterate live.

task.title: Transcript parser dispatch + per-agent parsers (5 structured + 1 passthrough) with unified event vocabulary
acceptance_criteria: New module lib/harness/dashboard/transcript/parser.ex exposes `init_state/1 :: parser_state`, `append/3 :: (agent_kind, chunk, parser_state) -> {events, new_parser_state}`, and `finalize/2 :: (agent_kind, parser_state) -> {events, new_parser_state}` — pure module, no GenServer, no side effects

Dispatch table covers :claude (Parser.Claude, mirrors Harness.Chat.Claude.StreamParser shape but preserves malformed lines as :unknown), :codex (Parser.Codex parsing `--json` NDJSON envelope `item.completed`/`item.started`/`turn.*`/`thread.*`), :cursor (Parser.Cursor parsing `--output-format stream-json` NDJSON — claude-shape compatible), :pi (Parser.Pi parsing `--mode json` NDJSON — `session`/`agent_start`/`turn_start`/`message_*`/`message_update text_delta`), :grok (Parser.Grok parsing `--output-format streaming-json` NDJSON — `thought`/`text`/`end` token deltas), and :antigravity (Parser.Passthrough — every chunk becomes one :plain_text event)

Unified event vocabulary all parsers emit: {:assistant_text, %{text}}, {:assistant_tool_use, %{id, name, input}}, {:tool_result, %{tool_use_id, content}}, {:system, %{kind, data}}, {:plain_text, %{text}}, {:unknown, %{raw}}

Per-agent fixture-driven tests at test/fixtures/transcripts/{claude,codex,cursor,grok,pi}.ndjson + antigravity.txt — fixtures hand-curated from real harness runs captured under ~/.harness/results/runs; parser_test.exs asserts the emitted event sequence for each fixture
Partial-line buffering correctness: byte-at-a-time feeding of every NDJSON fixture produces the same event list as one-shot feeding; explicit split-mid-line + finalize-on-fragment cases covered
Unknown-event preservation: malformed lines emit {:unknown, %{raw: line}} (NOT a crash, NOT a silent drop) — every NDJSON fixture's last line is deliberately corrupt to prove this
Passthrough emits exactly one :plain_text event per chunk — no line splitting, no JSON parsing (antigravity only)

Module-doc on parser.ex names each agent's wire format and explains the deviation from the original task body (Pi/Grok emit structured NDJSON in real captures — passthrough is reserved for Antigravity, which truly emits plain text)
No new dependencies — all parsing is pure Elixir / Jason
Atom-table safety: no String.to_atom/1 on agent-supplied strings; unknown event types fall through to a bounded :other atom
Dispatch dispatch test asserts every entry in Harness.AgentRegistry.agents/0 has a parser clause
out_of_scope: Wiring the parser into Harness.Run gen_statem and the dashboard render path (Task 87 owns the integration)

Replacing the existing Harness.Chat.Claude.StreamParser — it stays as the authoritative claude parser for the chat session backend; the new Parser.Claude is a parallel implementation that adds malformed-line preservation
Backwards-compat shims for prior event shapes — the unified vocabulary IS the new shape; consumers cut over in Task 87
Telemetry / metrics emission from the parser (could be added in a follow-up if useful)
task.body:
Stand up per-agent transcript parsers so the run-detail page can render
**parsed turns** instead of raw stream-json (Task 87 consumes this). Pure
module, no runtime side effects — the dispatcher takes
`(agent_kind, chunk, parser_state)` and emits a list of structured events.

**Per-agent wire formats** (verified against captured agent_output records
under ~/.harness/results/runs/; also documented in
`docs/agent-cli-reference.md`):
- Claude: `claude -p --output-format stream-json` — NDJSON, one event per line, types: `system/init`, `assistant.content[*].{text,tool_use,thinking}`, `user.content[*].tool_result`, `result`, `rate_limit_event`, hook lifecycle events.
- Codex: `codex exec --json` — NDJSON with dot-notation event types (`thread.started`, `turn.started`/`completed`, `item.started`/`completed` with `item.type` ∈ `agent_message`/`command_execution`/`reasoning`). Stderr noise (plugin-load errors, panics) gets folded into the stream by `:stderr_to_stdout` — preserved as `:unknown`.
- Cursor: `cursor-agent -p --output-format stream-json` — NDJSON, structurally near-identical to Claude's shape.
- Pi: `pi -p --mode json` — NDJSON, Anthropic-shaped envelope plus pi-specific lifecycle (`session`/`agent_start`/`turn_start`/`message_*`); user-visible tokens arrive as `message_update` events with `assistantMessageEvent.type == "text_delta"` and the payload in `delta`.
- Grok: `grok -p --output-format streaming-json` — NDJSON token-delta stream, `{type: "thought"/"text"/"end", data|stopReason: ...}`. ANSI-coloured stderr noise on auth/transport errors gets folded in — preserved as `:unknown`.
- Antigravity: `agy -p` — free-form text, no JSON contract → Parser.Passthrough.

**Deviation from initial task scope:** the original body grouped Pi and Grok
with Antigravity as passthrough on the assumption all three emit free-form
text. Captured runs show Pi and Grok emit structured NDJSON; the
implementation honors what the wire actually does. Passthrough is reserved
for Antigravity. The dispatcher moduledoc and Parser.Pi/Parser.Grok
moduledocs explain the deviation.

**Unified event vocabulary** all parsers emit (consumer in Task 87 walks this
list to render chat-style turns):

```elixir
{:assistant_text,     %{text: String.t()}}
{:assistant_tool_use, %{id: String.t(), name: String.t(), input: map()}}
{:tool_result,        %{tool_use_id: String.t(), content: term()}}
{:system,             %{kind: atom(), data: map()}}    # banners, lifecycle, terminal
{:plain_text,         %{text: String.t()}}             # passthrough (antigravity)
{:unknown,            %{raw: String.t()}}              # malformed line, preserved
```

**Tests.** Fixture-driven. `test/fixtures/transcripts/{claude,codex,cursor,grok,pi}.ndjson + antigravity.txt`
hold trimmed slices of real harness-run output (sourced from
`Harness.Run.LogRecord{agent_output: ...}` records). `parser_test.exs` walks
each fixture through `Parser.append/3` + `Parser.finalize/2` and asserts the
emitted event sequence. Partial-line buffering tested by re-feeding every
fixture one byte at a time and asserting equivalence.

**Atom-table safety.** Agent processes can emit a churning set of `type` and
`subtype` strings across releases; `String.to_atom/1` on those is a DoS
vector (BEAM atom table is unbounded). Known kinds are hand-mapped to bounded
atoms; unknown kinds fall through to `:other` and the raw string survives in
`data`.

**No dependencies added.** Pure Elixir + Jason (already in the dep stack).

Independent of Task 85 — both can land in parallel. Task 87 depends on both.
task.implemented: Per-agent transcript parser dispatch (Harness.Dashboard.Transcript.Parser) + 6 parser modules: structured NDJSON for Claude/Codex/Cursor/Pi/Grok, Passthrough for Antigravity. Unified 6-tag event vocabulary, pure (no GenServer/IO), per-line buffering with finalize/2 flush, malformed lines preserved as :unknown, bounded atom mapping (no String.to_atom on agent strings). Deviation from task body: Pi+Grok emit structured NDJSON in real captures, so passthrough is reserved for Antigravity. Fixture-driven tests incl. byte-at-a-time equivalence; dispatch test guards every AgentRegistry.agents/0 entry has a clause.

task.title: Run-detail transcript rework — parsed event list + <.transcript_view> component, ?raw=1 fallback
acceptance_criteria: lib/harness/dashboard/transcript.ex buffer changes from raw iodata binary to `{events :: [event()], parser_state :: term()}` per run; new `append_chunk/4` takes (chunks, agent_kind, parser_state, new_chunk) returning {new_chunks, new_parser_state}

task.body:
Replace the run-detail transcript pane's raw stream-json `
` dump with
a chat-style parsed view, using Task 86's Parser dispatcher to produce
structured events and Task 85's `Harness.Dashboard.Components` to render them.

**Today's flow:** `Driver.run/3` `:on_output` chunk → `Harness.Run` gen_statem
→ `Transcript.broadcast/2` → LiveView appends raw binary to a 200 KiB iodata
buffer → renders as `
{@transcript}
` at
lib/harness/dashboard/live.ex:303. The operator sees the wire format the model
emits — not the readable conversation.

**New flow:**

1. **Parser invocation moves into `Harness.Run`.** The gen_statem carries
   parser state in its data; each `:transcript_chunk` calls
   `Harness.Dashboard.Transcript.Parser.append/4` (Task 86) and broadcasts the
   resulting events. The raw-binary broadcast stays alongside for one release
   so `?raw=1` keeps working.

2. **Transcript buffer becomes `[event()]`.** `Harness.Dashboard.Transcript`
   replaces its iodata-binary buffer with an event list plus the parser-state
   per run. Cap moves from byte-count to event-count (default 500, configurable).
   `Harness.Run.transcript_events/1` is the new snapshot reader for late
   subscribers (LiveView mounts during a long run and needs the back-fill).
   Legacy `transcript/1` raw reader stays for one release.

3. **`<.transcript_view>` component** (added to `Harness.Dashboard.Components`
   from Task 85) walks the event list and renders:

   - `:assistant_text` → `<.message_row role={:assistant}>` — consecutive
     deltas in one turn collapse into a single message body (mirrors
     ChatLive's `text_delta` stream pattern).
   - `:assistant_tool_use` + matching `:tool_result` → grouped `<.tool_call>`
     with the existing collapsible `
` + structured JSON tree from
     Task 85's extracted components.
   - `:system` → `<.eyebrow>`-styled metadata line (e.g. "model:
     claude-opus-4-7 · turn 3").
   - `:plain_text` → `
` monospace card (preserves
     readability for unstructured agents — Grok / Pi / Antigravity).
   - `:unknown` → muted `
` with the raw chunk inside — nothing is
     lost, parser bugs are visible.

4. **`?raw=1` fallback.** `/harness/runs/?raw=1` renders the original
   iodata buffer as `
` for parity with today's behaviour. Useful for
   triaging a parser bug or comparing wire output.

**Phoenix 1.8 / LiveView 1.1 mandates** (same as Task 85):
- `<.transcript_view>` declared with `attr :events, :list, required: true` +
  `attr :agent, :atom, required: true`; HEEx-only template.
- HEEx `:if` / `:for` for conditionals / iteration — no
  `<%= Enum.map(...) %>` + `raw/1`.
- No `Phoenix.View` references; pure `Phoenix.Component`.

**Verification:** dispatch one run per adapter (Claude / Codex / Cursor / Grok
/ Pi) via the two-eval Tidewave pattern from
`skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md` § "Long-running dispatch from MCP eval".
Open `/harness/runs/` mid-run; cross-check `?raw=1` reverts to the
original view. Backfill: start a run, wait 30s after first output, open the
page, confirm prior events render.

**Hand-built** per the same precedent as Task 85 (CLAUDE.md § "Hand-Build UI
Tasks via Browser Tooling"). Driver+browser feedback loop is the only way
to grade event-grouping correctness, scroll behaviour, and the
parser-vs-raw visual delta.
task.implemented: Run-detail transcript pane swapped from raw <pre> dump to chat-style parsed view: Harness.Dashboard.Transcript carries an event list + parser_state per run via new append_chunk/4 (events, agent_kind, parser_state, chunk → {new_events, delta, new_parser_state}) + broadcast_events/3, capped at configurable event_count_cap/0 (default 500, :harness :dashboard :transcript_max_events). Harness.Run gen_statem threads parser_state through every :transcript_chunk and exposes transcript_events/1 alongside the legacy transcript/1; unregistered adapters degrade gracefully to agent_kind: nil + empty events. Harness.Dashboard.Components.transcript_view/1 + eyebrow/1 walk events into render blocks (consecutive :assistant_text collapse into one .msg-body, :assistant_tool_use + matching :tool_result pair into one <.tool_call>, :system as eyebrow, :plain_text as monospace card, :unknown preserved as muted <details>). Live :show subscribes to both transcript shapes, backfills via transcript_events/1, swaps render to <.transcript_view> with ?raw=1 fallback. CSS in tokens.ex for the new variants. Tests: 8 transcript_view component tests, 7 transcript event-cap + broadcast tests, 4 run gen_statem tests (incl. :sys.replace_state seam for parser-state threading through a registered agent_kind). Browser-verified end-to-end: all 6 event kinds render correctly via synthetic broadcast, ?raw=1 toggle swaps to legacy pre view, real Run gen_statem backfill populates events + agent_kind on mount, live updates after backfill append cleanly. Per-real-adapter visual coverage deferred to in-vivo dogfood dispatches — parser fixtures (Task 86) cover wire-format correctness.

The chat orchestrator must pick a task id by browsing a registered project's
roadmap as structured data through a harness tool — NOT by shelling `rmap` into

broken for {:github, _} sources. Add Harness.Roadmap.list/2 and next_bundle/1,
both resolving a registered project *name* via ProjectRegistry, returning
JSON-native flat maps, and annotated with descripex api() so they surface as
the roadmap__list / roadmap__next_bundle MCP+chat tools.
task.implemented: Added Harness.Roadmap.list/2 + next_bundle/1 (api()-annotated) resolving a registered project name through ProjectRegistry → roadmap_path, returning flat JSON-native maps (id/title/status/phase/bundle/eff/markers/milestone). task.title: Flat MCP-native dispatch tool — make the chat orchestrator able to dispatch a task for any project
acceptance_criteria: A single flat MCP tool dispatches one roadmap task for a registered project end to end, taking only JSON-passable scalars (project_name string, task id-or-next string, adapter string, scrub-key boolean) and returning a run_id (or a structured error) — verified by a dispatch call that targets a non-harness registered project and lands a real run_id
The Claude OAuth secret-scrub (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY => false) is applied by default on Claude dispatches through the flat tool, without the caller having to pass an opts map

Non-delegatable executors (grok/antigravity/pi) dispatch correctly through the flat tool — the ingest-with-delegatable-agent-then-dispatch-to-real-module dance is handled internally, not pushed onto the orchestrator

The stateless MCP tool surface no longer advertises struct-arg tools the orchestrator cannot drive (supervisor__start_run, batch__run, batch__run_pinned, agent_evaluation__compare, supervisor__start_link) — confirmed by inspecting the MCP tools/list output; the Elixir/Manifest driver surface (project_eval context) is unchanged

Harness.Chat.Tools no longer crashes when a keyword-typed param is passed as a JSON object — either it decodes to a keyword list or the param is absent from the JSON surface; a regression test covers the former opts-map Keyword.get/3 crash
priv/playbooks/dispatch-single-task.md is rewritten so steps 3-4 use the flat dispatch tool; the Elixir two-step is retained only where it applies (in-process driver) and labelled as such
skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md updated for the new flat tool + the trimmed MCP tool surface (Anti-Staleness Contract requires it)
out_of_scope: A flat batch/fan-out dispatch tool over the MCP surface (multi-item) — single-task dispatch is the v1 unblock; batch can follow if the orchestrator needs it
Removing the struct-arg functions themselves — they remain the canonical Elixir/IEx driver API; only their exposure on the stateless JSON MCP tool list changes
A flat compare/AgentEvaluation tool over MCP — separate concern (and Task 81 is the operator UI for that)
task.body:
A chat orchestrator following the dispatch-single-task playbook against a non-harness project (rexex) got blocked at the ingest/dispatch step. Root cause is one architectural mismatch, not a usage error: the MCP/chat surface advertises struct-passing Elixir APIs that cannot be driven over a stateless JSON boundary.

Confirmed defects on the chat MCP surface:
1. `roadmap__ingest` takes `opts` as a keyword list; the JSON->Elixir bridge in `Harness.Chat.Tools.decode_param/2` turns a JSON object into an Elixir map, so `ingest(selector, %{})` crashes in `Keyword.get/3` ("no function clause matching"). Omitting `opts` is the only form that runs — which means `:project` / `:project_root` / the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY => false` scrub / `subscriber: nil` cannot be passed.
2. `roadmap__ingest` has no top-level `project_name` param (unlike `roadmap__list` / `roadmap__next_bundle`, which were built flat for Task 88). The orchestrator's `project_name` is silently dropped, so ingest always resolves `File.cwd!/0` = the harness project, never the target.
3. The `{:id, "<id>"}` selector has no JSON encoding that round-trips to the Elixir tuple — only `:next` parses (via the `:`-prefixed-atom path in `decode_param`).
4. Deeper: even with opts fixed, `supervisor__start_run` takes `%Item{}` + `%Project{}` structs (`kind: :exchange_data`) and `batch__dispatch` takes `[%Item{}]`. A stateless MCP orchestrator cannot hold the `%Item{}` ingest returned and pass it into start_run. So the playbook's two-step (ingest -> struct -> start_run) is structurally un-runnable over chat regardless of the opts fix. The bug reporter's suggested "fix opts decoding" is necessary but NOT sufficient.

Goal: give the chat/MCP orchestrator a single flat tool that dispatches one roadmap task for a registered project end to end, mirroring how Task 88 added flat `list`/`next_bundle` for browsing. The orchestrator should be able to say "dispatch task 25 of rexex to Claude" in one tool call and get back a run_id, with subscription-OAuth secret-scrubbing applied by default — no struct threading, no keyword-list args.

Sketch of the contract (final shape is the implementer's call): a flat dispatch tool taking string `project_name`, a `task` selector that is either a task id string or "next", a string `adapter` (claude/codex/cursor/grok/antigravity/pi), and a boolean for the Claude OAuth scrub (default true). Internally: `ProjectRegistry.lookup` -> `Roadmap.ingest(selector, project: project)` -> `Run.Supervisor.start_run(item, project, adapter_module, subscriber: nil, env: scrub)`; return `%{run_id: ...}` or a structured error. Handle the non-delegatable executors (grok/antigravity/pi) via the documented ingest-with-a-delegatable-agent-then-dispatch-to-the-real-module two-step, internally — the orchestrator should not have to know about it.

Also stop the MCP surface from advertising tools it cannot run: the struct-arg dispatch tools (`supervisor__start_run`, `batch__run`, `batch__run_pinned`, `agent_evaluation__compare`, `supervisor__start_link`) are traps when surfaced as MCP tools — either exclude them from the MCP tool list (keep them on the Elixir/Manifest surface for the IEx/tidewave driver context) or otherwise prevent the orchestrator from calling un-driveable tools. The in-process Elixir driver (SKILL.md Context A/B via project_eval) keeps the full struct API; only the stateless JSON MCP surface needs the flat tool.

Secondary, fix regardless: `Harness.Chat.Tools.decode_param/2` converting a JSON object into a bare map for a value-param whose target is a keyword list. At minimum a keyword-typed param should arrive as a keyword list, or such params should not be exposed on the JSON surface.

Then rewrite `priv/playbooks/dispatch-single-task.md`: steps 3-4 currently document the Elixir two-step (ingest returns `%Item{}`, hand it to `supervisor__start_run`) as if the chat orchestrator could run it. Rewrite around the new flat dispatch tool. Keep the Elixir-API two-step documented where it belongs (SKILL.md Context A/B / IEx), clearly labelled as the in-process driver path, not the chat path.
task.implemented: Added Harness.Dispatch — a flat MCP-native dispatch tool (dispatch__task) taking JSON scalars (project_name, task selector, adapter, scrub-key bool); internally ProjectRegistry.lookup -> Roadmap.ingest(project:) -> Run.Supervisor.start_run with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY scrub default + the non-delegatable two-step handled internally. Trimmed struct-arg tools from the MCP tools/list (kept on Elixir/Manifest surface). Fixed Chat.Tools keyword-param JSON decode. Rewrote dispatch-single-task playbook + SKILL.md. Agent-delivered (Claude) in worktree; verification initially red on harness-side debt only (peri missing from PLT, pre-existing run_test credo nits, a type-narrowing-induced unreachable clause) — hand-integrated onto development with those 3 closeout fixes (mix.exs :peri, @dialyzer suppression keeping the defensive clause, run_test alias). 101/101 affected tests, credo clean bar 1 pre-existing baseline TODO, dialyzer 0.

task.title: Per-check working-directory offset — verify projects whose buildable root isn't the git/worktree root (rust-in-subdir, polyglot)
acceptance_criteria: A project whose buildable manifest lives in a subdir of the git repo (rexex: rust/Cargo.toml) verifies green/red on its own merits — cargo runs from the subdir, not the worktree root
Manifest-at-root projects (harness, :elixir preset) are unaffected — check cwd defaults to the worktree root, no behavior change
A single worktree can run checks from multiple subdirs (cargo in rust/, mix in an elixir subdir) — polyglot support, not one-subdir-only
The Rust (and Elixir) preset can be built with a subdir offset without hand-writing each Check
rexex is re-registered so its cargo checks run in rust/, and a rexex dispatch reaches a real verification verdict
Tests cover: subdir check cwd, default-root behavior unchanged, and a polyglot two-subdir stack
out_of_scope: Auto-detecting the manifest subdir — explicit registration/preset arg is fine for v1
Running multiple independent CheckStacks per project — one stack with per-check cwd covers the polyglot case
The Elixir half of rexex itself (not yet on disk) — this task only makes the harness side capable of checking it when it lands
task.body:
Surfaced by dogfooding: dispatching rexex task 25 (a Rust task) red'd all four cargo checks with `could not find Cargo.toml in <worktree-root>`. rexex keeps its Rust workspace in a `rust/` subdir (`rust/Cargo.toml` + `crates/`), with the roadmap and git root one level up. rexex was registered with `source: {:local, ".../rexex/rust"}` — the documented intent being "point cargo at the subdir" — but git worktrees are repo-granular: `git worktree add` checks out the WHOLE rexex repo (its `.git` is at the repo root), so the worktree root is the repo root and `Cargo.toml` lands at `rust/Cargo.toml`, not the root. `Harness.Verification.collect_check/3` runs every check with `{:cd, worktree_path}` (the worktree root, verification.ex ~line 183), so cargo never finds the manifest and the run is structurally un-greenable. The repair loop is futile — the agent is handed an unactionable "Cargo.toml missing" prompt for code that's fine.

rexex is also "Rust AND Elixir" going forward (Elixir half not yet on disk), so the fix must support a polyglot worktree: cargo checks running from `rust/`, mix checks running from some other subdir, all within one worktree rooted at the repo root (which is where the roadmap + git live and must stay).

Give checks a working-directory offset relative to the worktree root. The natural shape (final call is the implementer's): an optional relative `cwd` (default "." = worktree root) on `%Harness.Verification.Check{}`, with `collect_check` running each check from `Path.join(worktree_path, check.cwd)`. A polyglot stack is then just cargo-checks(cwd: "rust") ++ mix-checks(cwd: "<elixir-dir>"). The Rust/Elixir presets should accept the subdir so a project can build a cwd-stamped stack without hand-writing checks (e.g. `Preset.Rust.preset(cwd: "rust")`), and `%Harness.Project{}` registration should be able to express it. Don't break the common case — manifest-at-root projects (harness itself) must render byte-identical check behavior (cwd defaults to root).

Re-register rexex once the fix lands so its cargo checks run in `rust/`, and confirm a rexex dispatch can reach a real green/red verdict (the verification actually runs cargo, rather than failing on a missing manifest).
task.implemented: Multi-stack model rather than the body's suggested per-check cwd (final shape was implementer's call; the per-stack form also satisfies the 'multiple independent CheckStacks per project' line the body listed out-of-scope — chose it because it composes presets cleanly). %CheckStack{} gains workdir (default ""=repo root); %Harness.Project{} now holds check_stacks: [CheckStack.t()] (was singular check_stack). Verification.run/2 accepts :check_stacks, runs each stack's checks with {:cd, Path.join(worktree_root, workdir)}, flattens all results into one Verdict (green iff all pass), and returns {:error, {:workdir_not_found, dir}} on a misconfigured subdir (replaces the cryptic 'could not find Cargo.toml'). Post-process context (diff baseline filters) stays at repo root. Back-compat: singular preset:/check_stack:/:checks and the :check_stack run option all wrap to a one-element list with workdir "" — manifest-at-root projects (harness, :elixir) byte-identical. ProjectRegistry parses a new stacks: [[preset:/check_stack:, workdir:]] form. rexex re-registered in dev.local.exs (source=repo root, stacks: [[preset: :rust, workdir: "rust"]]). Tests: verification subdir-cwd/default-root/workdir_not_found/polyglot-flatten, registry stacks-parse + singular back-compat. Repair-prompt per-check workdir display deferred (needs workdir threaded onto Result struct, >15 LOC). Live rexex re-dispatch verdict pending operator iex restart.

task.title: Chat session persistence + index page — survive restart, list & reopen past chats
acceptance_criteria: A chat session's messages survive a BEAM restart: start a session, send turns, restart iex -S mix, reopen /harness/chat/<session_id> and the prior turns render
Harness.Chat.Supervisor.list_sessions/0 returns currently-live session ids (over Harness.Chat.Registry)
/harness/chat renders an index of existing sessions (live + persisted) with a recognizable label, last-activity, and a link to each; a 'new chat' button mints a fresh session
Persisted state is bounded (mirrors the live 200-message / per-turn truncation caps) so the store does not grow unbounded
Index and detail compose on the existing Harness.Dashboard.Components / Tokens vocabulary — no new inline styles
Tests: list_sessions/0 enumerates live sessions; persistence round-trips a session's messages through the store (save -> rehydrate)
out_of_scope: Full-text search across chats
Deleting / archiving sessions from the UI
Cross-device / multi-user session ownership or auth
Streaming a persisted (non-live) session — reopening a dead session shows its saved transcript statically; only live sessions stream
task.body:
Chat sessions are in-memory DynamicSupervisor children registered in Harness.Chat.Registry with no persistence and no list UI. Two gaps, shipped together because the index is near-useless without persistence (a BEAM restart wipes every session, which is exactly the pain that surfaced this):

1. Persistence — a chat session's message history survives a BEAM restart. On Session start/init, rehydrate from the store if the session_id has saved state; persist on each completed turn (and on terminate). A store already exists to model after: Harness.ResultStore is the file-backed LogRecord precedent (Task 19); Postgres via Harness.Repo is also available (Oban). Pick whichever fits — file-backed is the lighter match for ephemeral-ish chat transcripts. Bound what's persisted the same way the live buffer is bounded (200 messages / per-turn truncation) so the store doesn't grow unbounded.

2. Index page — a LiveView listing existing sessions (live + persisted), each showing enough to recognize it (first user message or a derived title, last-activity time, message count), clicking through to /harness/chat/<session_id>. Add Harness.Chat.Supervisor.list_sessions/0 (enumerate live via Harness.Chat.Registry) and merge with persisted-but-not-live sessions from the store. task.title: Kill button for in-flight runs on the dashboard
acceptance_criteria: Run-detail (/harness/runs/:run_id) shows a confirm-gated Kill button while the run is in-flight; clicking it cancels the run and it settles :failed
The index lists a kill control on each active/running run row
The kill control is absent for already-settled (:done/:failed) runs

After cancel, the view transitions to the settled state via the existing poll (button gone, verdict :failed)

A new cancellation primitive — reuse Harness.Run.cancel/1
Pause/resume (only cancel exists; cancel is terminal)
Confirming the agent OS process is reaped — that is Harness.Run.cancel/1's responsibility, already tested at the run layer
task.body:
Add a kill/cancel control to the dashboard so an operator watching a run go bad (wrong cwd, agent thrashing, runaway repair loop) can stop it from the browser instead of dropping to project_eval. The primitive already exists: Harness.Run.cancel/1 (descripex-annotated, @spec cancel(run()) :: :ok) kills the agent and settles the run :failed, and is already guarded against :done/:failed states (calling it on a settled run is a no-op).

Wire it into Harness.Dashboard.Live (the module serving both /harness :index and /harness/runs/:run_id :show):

- A "Kill run" button on the run-detail (:show) view, shown only while the run is in-flight (a live Harness.Run.status/1 lookup succeeds — i.e. not yet a settled LogRecord). A handle_event calls Harness.Run.cancel(run_id).
- The same control inline on the index for each active/running row, so you don't have to drill in first.
- Destructive-action confirm (phx-click with a data-confirm prompt) — a misfire settles the run :failed.
- After cancel, the existing 1s :tick poll already refreshes status, so the row/detail transitions to :failed on its own; no extra broadcast needed, but verify the button disappears once settled.

Compose on the existing Components/Tokens vocabulary (dashboard-chrome bundle) — reuse a button style, don't introduce a new one. Reserve the single --accent terminal-state cue for the kill affordance if it reads well.

task.body: Foundational for the autonomous-landing milestone. %Harness.Roadmap.Item{} currently carries only id/title/prompt/agent — the rendered agent prompt, not the structured acceptance criteria. The semantic gate (next task) and any future triage agent are blind to the task's actual contract without them. task.title: Cross-family adversarial semantic gate on green verdicts
acceptance_criteria: green verdict with gate enabled dispatches an opposite-model-family grader
REJECT blocks settle and feeds the repair loop; APPROVE settles :done
grader dispatch failure or timeout is treated as REJECT (fail-safe)
gate is skippable by config and OFF by default unless auto-landing
out_of_scope: The merge-train itself (separate task)
Acceptance-criteria quality checks — the gate trusts the criteria as written
task.body: Once no human reads the diff, the check stack catches 'doesn't compile/lint/test' but not 'agent deleted the failing test', 'stubbed the hard case', or 'solved the adjacent problem'. Add a semantic gate: before a green verdict settles :done, dispatch a reviewer agent with (task body + acceptance_criteria + the committed diff) and require <<<VERDICT:APPROVE|REJECT>>>. REJECT routes into the existing repair loop (new reason :semantic_rejection); APPROVE settles :done. This reuses almost everything already built — the consulting state in Harness.Run, Harness.AuditReview.grade_fix/1, and the sentinel verdict extraction — only WHEN it fires changes (on green, not on repeated red). CRITICAL: the grader MUST be a different model family than the implementer (reuse AuditReview's :claude <-> :codex auto-pairing). Both peer reviewers flagged that a same-family reviewer shares the implementer's blind spots and will rubber-stamp evasions. Fail-safe: any gate dispatch failure or timeout is treated as REJECT — never silently APPROVE. Config: gate is ON when the project's landing policy would auto-land, OFF otherwise.
