task.title: Model/agent availability — block unavailable {agent,model} at dispatch + surface available models over MCP
acceptance_criteria: New module Harness.ModelAvailability owns a mechanical query: available?(agent, model) :: boolean (catalog-member AND not blocked-now), blocked_until(agent, model) :: DateTime|nil, list_available(agent) :: [%{id, label, blocked_until}]. No scoring/weights/percentile/keyword-classifier — only set membership and now<until comparisons (the mantra: count facts, do not judge them).

Operator-declared blocks persist via Harness.SettingsStore under key :model_blocks, keyed on the PAIR {agent, model} (model may be :all to block a whole agent). Survives restart (unlike AgentRegistry's transient state). Shape: %{{:cursor, "claude-opus-4-8-thinking-high"} => %{until: DateTime|nil, reason: String, source: :operator}}.

Catalog source: probe `cursor-agent --list-models` and `grok models` via System.cmd, parse `id - label` lines (strip (current)/(default)/(NO ZDR) annotations into metadata), cached with a TTL plus a refresh_catalog/1 MCP tool. For codex/claude/antigravity/pi (no CLI list command): operator-maintained static list from settings, else an explicit :catalog_unavailable marker — never a silent [].

Five api()-annotated MCP tools on Harness.ModelAvailability, added to Harness.Manifest.@driver_surface so they auto-expose as model_availability-<fn>: list_available_models(agent, opts), block_model(agent, model, opts) (opts: until ISO8601, reason), unblock_model(agent, model), list_blocks(), refresh_catalog(agent). ALL params MUST be MCP-JSON-expressible — agent as plain string coerced to atom, model as string, until as ISO8601 string; NO atom/struct/tuple params (this repo has an active param-boundary bug, Task 259 — do not advertise an uncallable shape).

Dispatch gate (a): in Harness.Dispatch.resolve_and_ingest/3, after {project,item,adapter_module} resolves and before RunWorker.enqueue, resolve the effective model (item.model -> Config.agent_model/1 -> CLI default) and reject a blocked pair with {:unavailable, agent, model, available: list_available(agent)}. Add {:unavailable, atom(), String.t()|nil, keyword()} to the Dispatch error union. When the model falls through to the CLI default (unknown), apply only the agent-level (:all) block; a pinned/configured model checks the exact pair. No run starts on a blocked pair.

Reviewer-model gate: Run.reviewer_model/1 resolves the reviewer model from {:agent_model, reviewer_agent}; apply the same available?/2 check before spawning the reviewer Port so a blocked reviewer model fails fast with the same {:unavailable, ...} shape rather than mid-run.

Failure-capture (Source 3) is structured-signal-ONLY and mantra-bounded: hook the existing failed-run settle path that calls AgentRegistry.mark_unavailable/2; when the failure carries an UNAMBIGUOUS STRUCTURED quota signal (HTTP 429 / retry-after in a JSON error envelope, or a documented quota exit signal the adapter already surfaces as a fact), also record_block(agent, model, until: now + retry_after, source: :failure). When the signal is NOT structured, NO-OP — do NOT regex/keyword-classify free-text transcript (that classification is an agent's job, deferred). The reviewer must confirm no ~r/rate.limit|quota|429/-style classifier on raw output was added to harness code.

Tests in test/harness/model_availability_test.exs: catalog line-parse, block/unblock round-trip, expiry (a block with until in the past makes available?/2 true again with no manual unblock), the dispatch gate hard-rejects a blocked pair AND returns the available list, the reviewer-model gate, and failure-capture records on a synthesized structured-429 settle but adds NO block on an unstructured failure.

Changing the model/assignee/delegate --to precedence (the three-axis adapter contract) — this gates the RESOLVED model, it does not change resolution.
rmap-side validation of model pins — rmap is a generic substrate with no runtime availability knowledge; bad pins are caught at harness dispatch, not at file-time.
Per-model token/quota accounting or predictive burn (Task 89 territory).
task.body:
Why now (2026-06-12): a single roadmap task (259) burned FOUR routing attempts (claude -> cursor-opus -> codex -> composer) because harness has no notion of which {agent, model} pairs are usable right now. cursor-opus was token-blocked; nothing in harness knew, so the orchestrator guessed repeatedly and the operator hand-corrected each time. This task closes that gap: (a) block dispatching to an unavailable {agent, model}; (b) surface over MCP which models are available per agent so the orchestrator routes right the first time.

Empirical CLI findings (probed this session — these correct the original premise that "cursor tells us until which date opus/gpt are blocked", which is FALSE):
- `cursor-agent --list-models` and `cursor-agent models` return an IDENTICAL flat catalog (`id - label`). No quota, no "blocked until", no reset date. `cursor-agent about` only adds Subscription Tier + current model. So there is NO queryable block schedule anywhere.
- `grok models` exists (same shape). codex/claude have NO list command (only -m/--model; claude has --fallback-model). agy/pi minimal.
- A block is observable only by (1) the operator declaring it, or (2) a dispatch FAILING with a rate-limit error whose response may carry retry-after. Hence the two locked sources: operator-declared + structured-failure-capture.

Locked decisions (operator): block source = operator-declared + failure-capture; block action = HARD-REJECT with {:unavailable, agent, model, available: [...]} (no silent fallback — the orchestrator re-routes from the returned set). Fire a witness notification on a blocked dispatch (read-only, never a gate).

Relationship to prior work: extends the AGENT axis (Task 16 Harness.AgentRegistry — transient, restart-clearing, agent-level quota fail-over within a batch) with a NEW MODEL axis: per-{agent,model} pair, operator-declared, PERSISTENT (SettingsStore), MCP-surfaced. The two compose at query time: dispatch allowed only if AgentRegistry says the adapter is up AND ModelAvailability says the pair is not blocked. Sibling store to AgentRegistry, not a field on it (different persistence semantics).

Mantra check (reviewer will verify): catalog membership + now<blocked_until = counting/comparing facts -> code; operator block = an operator-supplied fact persisted verbatim; failure-capture restricted to a structured signal (a fact the adapter surfaces) and explicitly NOT a free-text classifier. No magic weights, no percentile gates.

Full plan (approved): /Users/efries/.claude/plans/melodic-prancing-reef.md. Reuse SettingsStore (persistence), Config.agent_model/1 (model precedence), AgentRegistry (compose gates), AgentAdapter.model_args/1 pattern, Manifest->Chat.Tools registration. Route: non-frontier (composer-2.5 / codex) — mechanical OTP+MCP wiring, fully specced.

Parser handles grok's bullet format: leading `- `/`* ` bullets and trailing `(default)`/`(current)` annotations stripped; id captured
list_available_models("codex") returns the codex catalog slugs (e.g. gpt-5.5, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.3-codex-spark) — codex IS probeable via `codex debug models`, not catalog_unavailable

task.body:
`Harness.ModelAvailability` lists grok as a CLI-probeable catalog source (`@probeable_agents %{cursor: "cursor-agent", grok: "grok"}`, `@catalog_commands grok: ["models"]`), but `model_availability-list_available_models` / `refresh_catalog` return `{:ok, %{catalog_unavailable: true, models: []}}` for grok even though the `grok` binary is present and authenticated.

Root cause: `grok models` does NOT emit the `id - label` shape `parse_id_label_line/1` (lib/harness/model_availability.ex ~line 430) expects. Observed live output (grok 2026-06-12, exit 0):

```
You are logged in with grok.com.

Default model: grok-build

Available models:
  - grok-composer-2.5-fast
  * grok-build (default)
```

`catalog_lines_to_entries/1` splits each line on `" - "`; grok's bullet lines (`  - <id>`, `* <id> (default)`) and the header lines yield no `id - label` pair, so `models == []` → `{:error, :catalog_unavailable}`. The whole grok catalog is silently empty.

Fix: teach the grok probe (or a grok-specific parse branch) to read the bullet format — collect lines after the `Available models:` header, strip the leading `- ` / `* ` bullet and a trailing ` (default)`/`(current)` annotation, and take the token as the model id (label = id when grok gives no separate label). Keep cursor's `id - label` path unchanged. Confirm `list_available_models("grok")` returns `[%{id: "grok-build", ...}, %{id: "grok-composer-2.5-fast", ...}]`.

Secondary (now in-scope): `{output, 0} = System.cmd(...)` in `default_probe/2` hard-matches exit 0 inside the `with` body — a non-zero exit raises MatchError instead of falling through to `{:error, :catalog_unavailable}`. Match the exit code as a `with` clause so a failed probe degrades gracefully (covers grok AND codex).

## Codex (widened 2026-06-12 — the original out_of_scope premise was wrong)

Codex IS catalog-probeable: `codex debug models` (subcommand nested under `codex debug`, not top-level — easy to miss) renders the raw catalog as JSON, exit 0. Verified live (codex 2026-06-12):

```
{"models":[{"slug":"gpt-5.5","display_name":"GPT-5.5","visibility":"list",...},{"slug":"gpt-5.4",...}]}
```

So wire `@probeable_agents` + `@catalog_commands` for codex (`codex -> ["debug", "models"]`) and add a **JSON-decode** parse branch — `Jason.decode/1` the output, map each `%{"slug" => id, "display_name" => label}` to `%{id: id, label: label, annotations: []}`. This is a DIFFERENT parse strategy than the grok/cursor line parsers (JSON vs text lines), so `default_probe/2` (or a per-agent parse dispatch) must select the parser by agent. Keep the grok bullet branch and cursor `id - label` branch intact.

Claude stays out: `claude model list` is interpreted as a prompt (no such subcommand); anthropics/claude-code#12612 is an open feature request to add it. Its `catalog_unavailable` is by design — no static catalog for it here.

## PARTIAL SHIP 2026-06-12 (commit pending) — grok + exit done, codex re-scoped under Task 265

Shipped this session in `Harness.ModelAvailability`: grok bullet parser (`parse_grok_line`), per-agent parse dispatch (`parse_agent_line/2`), dedupe-by-id, pi table parser + pi wired probeable (bonus), and the graceful non-zero-exit fix in `default_probe/2` (the `{output, 0}=` MatchError). So ACs grok/bullet-format/cursor-regression/non-zero-exit are MET; grok unit test added. DO NOT re-implement the grok parser.

NOT done the 263 way: codex. Instead of the `codex debug models` JSON probe, codex got a UI-only `@builtin_ui_catalogs` static seed (gpt-5.5/gpt-5.4/gpt-5.4-mini/gpt-5.3-codex-spark), and claude got one too (overriding this task's "claude stays out" premise — the operator explicitly asked to seed both). The codex `debug models` JSON-probe branch + its test are the only remaining 263 ACs, and whether codex should probe vs use the operator-editable list is now a design decision folded into **Task 265** (unify the 3 catalog sources, advisory gate, operator-editable lists). Revisit 263's codex half after 265's design is settled.

task.title: Make a run's landed-state a PERSISTED FACT (landed_sha on the run record), written by the lander — kill the fragile rmap+git mergedness recompute
acceptance_criteria: A run's merged/landed status is read from a PERSISTED FACT on the run record (new nullable `landed_sha` column on `run_records` + the field on the `LogRecord` struct and the dashboard `Status` snapshot), never recomputed at render time.

The lander writes `landed_sha` onto the run record at the successful ff-push (the `land_in_worktree`/`writeback` success path, where the pushed SHA and `request.run_id` are both in hand), best-effort and non-blocking — a write failure logs and still lands, mirroring the existing rmap writeback.

The dashboard 'Run history — unmerged only' filter decides mergedness solely from the stored `landed_sha` field — it no longer calls `rmap list` roadmap summaries or git branch-reachability for this decision.

The fragile recompute is DELETED: `RunFeed.branch_landed_cache/3`, `ResultStore.landed_sha/2` + `landed_sha_for_run/2` (the per-row `git fetch`/reachability path), the `landed_cache` assign + its `:refresh_landed_cache`/roadmap-tick refresh, and the roadmap-summary landed JOIN used only for this filter. Roadmap summaries may stay for open-task counts, but are no longer a landing witness.

REGRESSION: with an empty `ProjectRegistry` / no roadmap loaded (the DB-disconnect state observed 2026-06-12 where ALL runs showed as unmerged), a run that landed still renders as merged — it reads the DB fact, not the registry.

Backfill/compat is decided and stated: run records that landed before this column exists have `landed_sha = NULL`. Either a one-shot backfill from the task's `shipped_in` OR they read as unmerged until re-landed — pick one, document it in the migration/moduledoc, and assert no crash on NULL.

Tests (no Process.sleep; assert specific values, not 'any error passes'; @spec on every new def AND defp): lander persists `landed_sha` on a ff-push; dashboard filter hides a run with `landed_sha` set and shows one with NULL; the empty-registry regression above.
out_of_scope: Removing the run-history view or the unmerged/landed toggle entirely (the operator chose to KEEP the filter and make it robust — the rip-it-out option was explicitly rejected).
The model-required reviewer-config blocker (no `{:agent_model,_}`/`{:reviewer_model,_}` set) — separate issue, fixed via the dashboard settings cards, not here.
Changing landing mechanics or the rmap `done --verified --shipped-in` writeback semantics from Task 214 — the rmap-side writeback stays; this adds a run-record-side fact next to it.
The post-merge audit job and any audit-state surfacing.
task.body:
The dashboard 'Run history — unmerged only' view shows ALL runs as unmerged whenever the landing witness is missing, because mergedness is RECOMPUTED on a cold tick instead of stored. Two fragile witnesses, neither a stored fact:

1. `RunFeed.roadmap_landed_sha/2` — joins the run's `task_id` against a `task_id => shipped_in` map built from `rmap list` per registered project. Empty when `ProjectRegistry` is empty — exactly the DB-disconnect / schema-drift state (the registry boots empty, no project to query), so every run reads as unmerged.
2. `RunFeed.branch_landed_cache/3` -> `ResultStore.landed_sha_for_run/2` — git branch-reachability (is the run's commit reachable from origin/<target>). Needs projects + local git; and per the reverted PARTIAL perf task, falling through to this path caused a per-render `git fetch origin` for every history row that HUNG the /harness render.

Named evidence:
- Task 214 (done, phase 17) INTRODUCED the branch-reachability derivation to fix a 'false approved-but-not-landed' signal. This task supersedes that mechanism: replace the recompute with a fact the lander already knows.
- The reverted perf task documents `RunFeed.landed_sha` falling through to `landed_sha_for_run` -> per-row `git fetch` hang.
- Observed 2026-06-12: with the dashboard node degraded and the registry empty, the operator saw EVERY run as 'unmerged only'. Recurring operator-facing bug across multiple sessions.

The mantra fit: 'is this run landed?' is a FACT the lander produces at ff-push (it sets the task's `shipped_in` in the same motion) — it should be COUNTED/stored on the run record, not re-derived by the dashboard from rmap+git every 30s. This is mechanical substrate (a stored SHA + a NULL check), not judgment — correct to make a column.

The fix: add a nullable `landed_sha` to `run_records`; the lander writes it at successful push next to the existing rmap writeback; the dashboard filter reads `status.landed_sha != nil`; delete the rmap-summary + git-reachability recompute used only for this filter. The filter STAYS (operator's choice) — it just reads a robust fact.

task.title: Unify the three model-catalog sources into one operator-editable, advisory resolution (dedupe probe / static / builtin)
acceptance_criteria: A single `catalog(agent)` resolution returns the layered catalog; the settings dropdown and any other consumer read the SAME source — `selectable_models/1` vs `list_available/1` split is removed

Catalog membership is advisory: `catalog_allows?/2` is removed from the dispatch gate; only operator/failure blocks (`blocked_now?`) hard-gate. Regression: a pinned model absent from the catalog still dispatches; a blocked {agent,model} pair still rejects
Operator can edit a per-agent model list in /harness/settings (add/remove ids) persisted to `:model_catalog_static`; the dropdown reflects edits with no restart
A Refresh-from-CLI action probes a probeable agent and merges the result into the editable list; non-probeable agents (claude) keep their builtin/operator entries
`@builtin_ui_catalogs` folds into the single catalog layer once gating is advisory (no UI-only parallel map remains)

Changing block (operator/failure) semantics — blocks stay the hard gate, untouched
Validating model ids against a baked allowlist — ids churn; the whole point is operator-editable + probe-sourced lists
task.body:
Model lists are configured in THREE disjoint places, and the dropdown vs the dispatch gate read different ones — operator complaint: "it can not be that we have to configure/edit this at so many parts." Combine the strong points instead of picking one.

The three sources today (all in `Harness.ModelAvailability`):
1. Live CLI probe — `@probeable_agents` / `@catalog_commands` shell out (`cursor-agent --list-models`, `grok models`, `pi --list-models`; codex via `codex debug models` is Task 263's remaining piece). Authoritative, never rots, but depends on the agent CLI being installed+authed.
2. SettingsStore `:model_catalog_static` — operator-declared, persisted, currently the only override layer. FEEDS THE DISPATCH GATE (`catalog_allows?/2`).
3. `@builtin_ui_catalogs` (added 2026-06-12) — hardcoded claude/codex defaults, UI-only so they don't gate dispatch. Read by `selectable_models/1`; the dropdown uses this, the gate uses `catalog/1`. This split is the smell.

WHY the split exists: `catalog_allows?/2` makes catalog membership a dispatch gate — a pinned model not in the catalog is rejected pre-spawn. Seeding claude/codex into the gating catalog would block any unseeded id from dispatching, so the builtin was kept UI-only. That fork (selectable_models vs list_available) is the duplication.

DIRECTION CONFIRMED (operator, 2026-06-12 — assignee flipped human->codex, advisory gate APPROVED):
- ONE layered resolution `catalog(agent)` = operator-static (SettingsStore, editable in UI) -> live probe (refresh-on-demand, cached) -> code builtin defaults. Both the settings dropdown and every consumer read it — delete the `selectable_models` vs `list_available` split.
- Make catalog membership ADVISORY: drop `catalog_allows?/2` from the dispatch gate so the ONLY hard gate is explicit operator/failure blocks (`blocked_now?`). The agent CLI already rejects a bad `--model`; harness deciding a model id is "valid" is judgment-in-code the MANTRA says belongs to the agent. With gating gone, the builtin folds into the single catalog layer (no UI-only parallel map).
- Operator-editable per-agent list in /harness/settings (add/remove ids), persisted to `:model_catalog_static`. "Refresh from CLI" probes (where probeable) and merges into the editable list. This is the operator's stated want: "set my models, not rely on agents" — probe becomes a convenience to populate the list, not a dependency.
- Builtins seed the initial editable list (claude, which has NO list CLI, lives here permanently; cursor/grok/pi/codex seed from probe).

SHIPPED THIS SESSION (2026-06-12, commit pending) toward Task 263 + this one:
- grok bullet-format parser (`parse_grok_line`) + pi table parser (`parse_pi_line`); per-agent parse dispatch (`parse_agent_line/2`); dedupe by id.
- pi wired as probeable.
- graceful non-zero-exit in `default_probe/2` (was a `{output, 0}=` MatchError that would 500 the settings page on an unauthed CLI).
- claude + codex `@builtin_ui_catalogs` (UI-only) + `selectable_models/1`; settings dropdowns for claude/codex/cursor/grok/pi.
Remaining from 263: codex via `codex debug models` JSON probe (this task may instead route codex through the operator-editable list — design decision).

task.title: Routing-brief: one MCP surface joining roster+availability+capability+KPI per {agent,model} (raw facts, no fused score) so the task-writer routes without reading lib/
acceptance_criteria: New Harness.Routing (use Descripex, dedicated curated read-surface like Harness.Agents/262) exposes routing-brief/0 returning, per currently-available {agent, model} pair, a JSON-safe map JOINING the four existing fact-legs: roster facts (installed/enabled/reviewer_eligible/capabilities/cost_tier from Harness.Agents), availability (from ModelAvailability — only un-blocked pairs surface, blocked pairs annotated with reason not silently dropped), capability scores by domain (ResultStore.list_capability_scores), and KPI rollups (ResultStore.aggregate_by_agent: success_rate, first_attempt_pass, duration_p90, cost_to_approved). It is a JOIN of existing accessors — no new aggregation logic, no re-counting.

Every capability/KPI cell carries its SAMPLE COUNT n (runs behind the number); unmeasured cells surface as n=0 / explore-candidate, never a fabricated score. The writer reads n to decide explore vs exploit. (dispatch-recommend already encodes explore/exploit; the brief exposes the raw n it keys off.)

routing-brief/1 accepts an optional domains filter (e.g. domains=["otp"]) that scopes/annotates the capability+KPI legs to the relevant domain(s); omitted => all domains. The optional-param boundary resolves the configured store (the Task 248/251-class bug: an omitted arg must NOT short-circuit to a disabled/empty value).

MANTRA GATE: the brief computes NO verdict, ranking, weighted score, or route — it returns raw joined facts and the writer-AI picks. A reviewer can confirm no api()-returned value fuses facts into a single best-{agent,model} number (reuse Task 262's 'no JUDGMENT value' check). dispatch-recommend stays the advisory pick layer ON TOP; the brief is the raw facts UNDER it (cross-ref, do not duplicate or replace it).
Added to Harness.Manifest @driver_surface; routing-brief listed by mcp_tools/0 with a valid JSON Schema, not dropped by struct_arg_tool?/1; reachable via BOTH Harness.Chat.Tools and the MCP server.

WRITER CONTRACT documented: skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md + docs/orchestrator-surface-inventory.md state that the task-writer/orchestrator resolves assignee+model from routing-brief (MCP facts) and NEVER reads lib/harness/*.ex to make a routing decision; routing-brief is named THE single routing source. scripts/sync-harness-skills.sh run to propagate the skill.

Tests (no Process.sleep; assert specific values not 'any error passes'; @spec on every new def AND defp): join correctness (each of the four legs present per pair, blocked pair annotated not dropped); cold-start (an unmeasured {agent,domain} surfaces n=0/explore, not a fake score); the no-fused-score property (no api() value returns a ranking/best-pick); omitted-arg path returns the configured-store facts not the disabled empty. coverage >= 80% on the new module; mix precommit.full green.
out_of_scope: Computing a recommendation/ranking/weighted route — dispatch-recommend (Tasks 120/121) is the advisory pick; this brief is the RAW facts beneath it. No magic weights, no composite scalar (the v0_13 deletion lesson).

The roster/KPI/capability surfaces THEMSELVES — Harness.Agents (262), aggregate_by_agent (139), reviewer-ratings rollup (177/248) already ship; this only JOINS them, it does not re-implement or re-count.
Changing model block/availability semantics — that is Task 265 (the availability leg this depends on); blocks stay the hard gate.
Per-task / per-project model pinning (Tasks 256/261 — separate axes).
Auto-routing inside the dispatch path / changing dispatch-recommend's algorithm — the brief feeds judgment to the writer-AI, it does not wire a new auto-route.
task.body:
THE 'orchestrator routes without reading code' loop, closed as one cheap MCP fact.

Operator's point (2026-06-12): 'der rmap writer sollte alleine in der Lage sein ... nach Verfuegbarkeitscheck via MCP zu wissen, welche Agents mit welchem Model fuer welche Tasks' — 'es kann nicht sein, dass der Orchestrator den ganzen Code in den Context laedt, nur um zu entscheiden an wen zu dispatchen' — 'und mehr: wir haben KPIs, wir WISSEN wie die Agents performen, das sollte direkt bereitgestellt werden.'

The four routing fact-legs ALREADY exist as SEPARATE MCP surfaces; the gap is the JOIN + the contract, not the data:
1. Roster      -> Harness.Agents agents-list (Task 262, done): installed/enabled/reviewer_eligible/capabilities/cost_tier/model.
2. Availability -> ModelAvailability list_available_models (Task 148; cleaned by Task 265): un-blocked {agent,model} pairs.
3. Capability  -> ResultStore.list_capability_scores / get_capability_score: per-{agent,domain} score (+ the scout/facet work).
4. KPI         -> ResultStore.aggregate_by_agent (Task 139, done; reviewer ratings fed by 177/248): success_rate, first_attempt_pass, duration_p90, cost_to_approved.

Today a writer would call four tools and join them in its head — or worse, grep lib/. routing-brief does the join in ONE call so the writer makes one cheap MCP read and decides. It is a dedicated curated read-surface module (Harness.Routing, mirroring the 262 pattern where short-name == tool prefix), returning plain maps, delegating to the existing accessors.

MANTRA, non-negotiable: the brief returns RAW joined facts + the sample-count n behind each number. It NEVER fuses them into a best-pick score/ranking/route — that is judgment the writer-AI does, and dispatch-recommend already provides the advisory pick on top. We deleted ~1,400 LOC of composite-score arithmetic in v0_13 precisely so harness stops computing 'who is best'; this task must not smuggle it back in. The cold-start caveat is a FACT not a formula: surface n=0 for unmeasured cells so the writer knows when to explore.

Depends on 262 (roster leg, done) and 265 (availability leg — build the join after the catalog is unified/advisory so the brief reads one clean availability source, not the pre-265 three-source mess). Builds on 75 (api annotation) + 79 (MCP server) + 139/177/248 (KPI) + 120/121 (capability routing). Verify state against origin before assuming. The primary harness consumer IS an AI orchestrator over MCP — a one-call routing brief is the product, not a nicety.

task.title: Replace unconditional dwell Process.sleep with deterministic synchronization in the test suite
acceptance_criteria: test/harness/run_test.exs:1914 — the Process.sleep(600) 'held persists' dwell is removed; the test instead asserts :held, drives one more event through the Run gen_statem, and re-asserts :held (no fixed wall-clock dwell)
test/harness/run_test.exs:1084 and :1188 — the two `for _ <- 1..6 do ...Process.sleep(150)` loops are replaced by sending all six chunks then asserting :running once; the per-tick dwell is gone

test/harness/dashboard/roadmap_summary_test.exs:160 and :176 — the Process.sleep(500)/Process.sleep(100) waits become assert_receive/refute_receive on the PubSub/telemetry message the summary already emits
grep -nE 'Process\.sleep\([1-9][0-9]{2,}\)' over the touched non-oban files returns nothing
The full offline suite stays green (mix test.json --exclude integration); record the wall-clock delta vs the pre-change baseline in `implemented`
out_of_scope: Flipping any file from async: false to async: true (that is Tasks 268-271)
Touching the 20ms poll granularity of the existing await_*/wait_until_running helpers in run_test.exs:2430-2490 — they already early-exit on success and are not the cost
Splitting run_test.exs (Task 268)
task.body:
The test suite carries unconditional fixed `Process.sleep` dwell that is paid on **every** green run (these are not retry-loop ceilings that early-exit — they always wait the full duration). Replace them with event-driven synchronization that returns the instant the condition holds.

Targets (verified 2026-06-12):
- `run_test.exs:1914` — `Process.sleep(600)` proving a `:held` run stays held. Replace with: assert `:held`, push one more transcript/event through the gen_statem, re-assert `:held`. The persistence claim is about *surviving an event*, not *surviving wall-clock*.
- `run_test.exs:1084` & `:1188` — `for _ <- 1..6 do send(pid, {:transcript_chunk, "tick"}); Process.sleep(150); assert :running end` (~900ms each). Send all six chunks, then assert `:running` **once**. The interleaved dwell proves nothing the single post-assert doesn't.
- `roadmap_summary_test.exs:160` & `:176` — `Process.sleep(500)` + `Process.sleep(100)` before reading summary state. Use `assert_receive`/`refute_receive` on the PubSub/telemetry message the summary path already broadcasts.

**`oban_dispatch_test.exs` is a judgment call — do NOT blindly shrink its 8× `Process.sleep(100)` helper sleeps.** They live inside spawned helper jobs and simulate in-flight job duration measured against the Lifeline `@lifeline_rescue_after_ms` rescue window; cutting them races the rescue tests. Reduce only where the rescue semantics demonstrably still hold; otherwise leave them and write a one-line rationale in the verdict. (Listed in files_to_modify only so a careful reduction is in-scope if safe.)

Prefer the synchronization primitives already used elsewhere in these files: `assert_receive` with a timeout, `Process.monitor` + `assert_receive {:DOWN, …}`, `start_supervised!` for lifecycle, and the existing `wait_until_running`/`await_*` poll helpers (leave those helpers' internals alone).

This is the Phase-1 quick win from the test-suite-perf plan; Tasks 268-271 do the structural async conversions and depend on this landing first where files overlap.

task.title: Split run_test.exs by describe-group and convert to async: true (per-test state isolation)
acceptance_criteria: run_test.exs (2,509 lines / ~129 tests, currently async: false) is split into focused files grouped by its existing `describe` blocks under test/harness/run/

Each resulting file runs with `async: true`, achieved by isolating the shared state — Run gen_statem / Run.Supervisor global names, FakeAdapter state, and worktree base dir — per test (start_supervised!/unique names/unique tmp dirs), NOT by leaving it serial

The full offline suite stays green across at least three seeds (mix test.json --exclude integration --seed 0, plus two random seeds) — proving no cross-test state bleed was introduced by the async flip
Wall-clock delta vs baseline recorded in `implemented`
out_of_scope: The Phase-1 sleep removals (Task 267 — must land first; this task rebases on the de-slept run_test.exs)
Other async:false files (Tasks 269/270/271)
task.body:
`run_test.exs` is the single biggest wall-clock sink: 2,509 lines, ~129 tests, `async: false`, so the whole file runs one test at a time. Split it by its existing `describe` groups into focused files under `test/harness/run/`, then flip each to `async: true`.

The split is the *means* to async (smaller files + isolated state parallelize), so split-and-convert is one coupled task, not two.

The blocker to async is shared global state — isolate each per test:
- **Run gen_statem / Run.Supervisor** use global/registered names → start a fresh supervised instance per test (`start_supervised!`) or unique via_tuple names; never mutate a singleton.
- **FakeAdapter** state (test/support/fake_adapter.ex) → ensure per-run/per-test scoping, no shared ETS/agent.
- **Worktree base dir** (`/tmp/harness_worktrees_test`) → unique subdir per test to avoid collisions when tests run concurrently.

Verification MUST run the **full** suite under multiple seeds after the flip — a file green in isolation but flaky in the async pool means the isolation is incomplete; fix the shared state, do not revert to serial. If a specific describe-group genuinely cannot be isolated, keep just that group in a small async:false file and document why — don't pin the whole split serial for one holdout.

Changing the shared Dashboard.Endpoint started in test_helper.exs (server: false) — work within it
task.body:
`dashboard/live_test.exs` is 59 Phoenix.LiveViewTest tests running `async: false`. Convert to `async: true` by isolating the shared state these tests touch:
- **PubSub topics** — namespace per test (e.g. unique suffix) so a broadcast from one test isn't observed by another.
- **In-memory result/settings stores** (Harness.ResultStore.Memory, SettingsStoreMemory) — these are suite-shared ETS owned by test_helper; scope reads/writes per test or reset under the test's own ownership so concurrent tests don't cross-contaminate.

The `Dashboard.Endpoint` is started once in test_helper with `server: false` and is safe to share — don't restart it per test. If a genuine blocker (stateful singleton the LiveView reads) makes full async impossible, isolate what you can and document the residual in the verdict rather than silently leaving it serial. Verify the full suite under multiple seeds (state-bleed surfaces only in the async pool, not in isolation).

run_test.exs / dashboard (Tasks 268/269)
task.body:
`oban_dispatch_test.exs` (35 tests, async: false) is the hardest conversion: Oban runs `testing: :inline` (a global app-env setting), queue names are shared, and the Lifeline plugin is a singleton with a rescue timer. Attempt `async: true` by isolating what can be isolated (per-test queue names, scoped helper processes, per-test ownership of the dispatch state), but this task is explicitly allowed to conclude **"stays serial, here's the concrete blocker"** — the value is a *grounded* decision, not a forced flip.

Depends on Task 267 because both touch this file (the helper-sleep judgment lands first). If kept serial, still take any cheap sub-wins and name the exact reason in an inline comment so the next person doesn't re-investigate. If converted, verify the full suite under multiple seeds — Oban inline + shared queues are exactly the kind of state that passes in isolation and races in the async pool.

task.title: Sweep the remaining async: false test files — classify the blocker per file, flip what can flip
acceptance_criteria: Every remaining async: false test file (the long tail after Tasks 268-270) is classified by its real blocker: app-env mutation (e.g. :audit_review config), ProjectRegistry singleton, AgentRegistry.reset, or Ecto Sandbox shared-mode
Files whose blocker can be isolated are flipped to async: true with the isolation applied (per-test instance/name via start_supervised!, or per-test connection ownership for DB tests)

Files that genuinely must stay serial carry an inline `# async: false because …` comment naming the blocker; a global-env test does not get to pin a large file serial if it can be split into a tiny dedicated async:false file
Full offline suite green across three seeds; report the count of files flipped and final async:false count in `implemented`
out_of_scope: run_test.exs (268), dashboard/live_test.exs (269), oban_dispatch_test.exs (270) — handled separately
Rewriting fixtures (git_fixture/process_fixture) beyond what isolation requires
task.body:
After the three named heavyweights are converted (Tasks 268-270), ~60 async:false files remain. Sweep them: for each, identify the *real* reason it's serial and isolate it rather than accepting the flag.

Per-blocker isolation patterns:
- **App-env mutation** (e.g. `:audit_review` config) → thread the override through the function under test, or split the genuinely-global cases into a tiny dedicated async:false file so one global-env test doesn't pin a whole file serial.
- **ProjectRegistry / AgentRegistry** → `start_supervised!` a fresh named instance per test instead of mutating the singleton / calling `reset`.
- **Ecto Sandbox shared-mode** (`{:shared, self()}` forces async:false) → move DB tests to per-test manual checkout/ownership where the test owns its connection, enabling async.

This is a sweep, but keep each file's diff coherent — the reviewer verifies the batch as "every remaining file is either justified-serial or isolated-and-async." Report the before/after async:false count. Verify the full suite under multiple seeds; the whole point is catching state-bleed the isolation was meant to prevent.

task.body:
Discovered 2026-06-12 while dogfooding routing-brief (Task 266): result_store-list_capability_scores returns a bare []. Root cause — v0_13 (Task 6513) deleted the CapabilityScore composite ARITHMETIC but left the .Legacy struct + the save/get/list_capability_score store accessors as a manual MCP import hatch. A surface that holds nothing is noise — mantra-aligned to delete (count facts in code; a leg that counts nothing is not a fact).

task.title: routing-brief: thin dispatchable-only index + agents/fields projection (payload fits context; aggregate_* is the drill-down)
acceptance_criteria: routing-brief/0 DEFAULTS to dispatchable pairs only: a pair surfaces only when its agent roster is installed AND enabled AND the {agent,model} is currently available (un-blocked). The full catalog (e.g. cursor's ~139 selectable slugs, blocked/disabled agents) is EXCLUDED by default. Regression: the live payload drops from ~175 pairs / ~178KB to the handful of actually-dispatchable pairs and fits one MCP read.
An include_all: true opt (brief/1 option) restores the current full-catalog behaviour verbatim — nothing is lost, the verbose view is opt-in. Default false.

brief/1 accepts an agents filter (list of agent-name strings, e.g. ["codex","cursor"]) that further restricts the returned pairs to the named agents; composes with the existing domains filter (domains still scopes/annotates KPI cells only). Unknown agent name => that agent contributes no pairs (not an error).

brief/1 accepts a fields projection (list of top-level pair keys, e.g. ["agent","model","availability","kpi"]) that returns only those keys per pair — token-cheap for an orchestrator that needs a subset, mirroring rmap ready --fields. Unknown field name => ignored or 400-class error, pick one and test it. Omitted => all legs.

WRITER CONTRACT (skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md + docs/orchestrator-surface-inventory.md): routing-brief is THE thin routing index (list); for per-agent depth the writer drills into the EXISTING aggregate_* family (aggregate_by_agent / aggregate_by_facet / aggregate_reviewer_reliability / aggregate_ceremony_cost) — the list->get pattern. State explicitly: do NOT add new KPI tools for detail the aggregate_* lenses already provide. scripts/sync-harness-skills.sh run to propagate.

Tests (no Process.sleep; assert specific values; @spec on every new def AND defp): default returns only dispatchable pairs (seed a blocked + a disabled agent, assert both absent); include_all restores them; agents filter narrows; fields projection returns exactly the named keys; domains still scopes KPI. mix precommit.full green; coverage >= 80% on the changed module.
out_of_scope: Any NEW KPI/aggregate MCP tool — the 6 aggregate_* lenses cover the depth; per-{agent,model} KPI does not exist because runs are logged per-agent not per-model (a data fact, surfaced as n/explore, NOT a tool gap)
dispatch-recommend (the advisory scout pick) — stays the layer ON TOP of the brief, untouched
Re-introducing any capability leg (removed in Task 272) — the brief stays 3 legs: roster + availability + KPI
Changing block (operator/failure) semantics or the availability source
task.body:
Discovered 2026-06-12 dogfooding the landed routing-brief over MCP: brief() returns all 175 {agent,model} pairs = ~178KB, which exceeds a single MCP read and blows the writer's context. Breakdown: cursor 139, pi 25, claude 5, codex 4, grok 2 — cursor alone enumerates its entire multi-model catalog. The irony: the surface built so the writer routes WITHOUT reading lib/ is itself too big to read. The domains filter only scopes KPI cells, it does not reduce the pair count.

Fix = make it a THIN INDEX, not a fatter tool and not a pile of new tools. Default to dispatchable-only (available + enabled), add an agents filter and a fields projection (rmap-ready style), keep the full catalog as include_all opt-in. Depth already exists: the 6 aggregate_* lenses are the drill-down (list->get). We just deleted dead surface in Task 272 — do not recreate the vestige by adding speculative KPI tools; a new tool earns its place only when the routing flow has a concrete question none of the aggregate_* lenses answer.

Routing rationale (dogfooded from routing-brief itself): cursor/Opus blocked until 2026-06-30; codex/gpt-5.5 free; codex mcp 9.0 / descripex 9.0 / truthfulness 8.5, success 0.96 over 82 runs — strongest fit for an MCP/descripex read-surface change. -> codex / gpt-5.5.

No new KPI tools.

task.title: routing-brief default: collapse to the configured model per agent, not the whole available catalog (144 pairs still blows context)
acceptance_criteria: routing-brief/0 DEFAULT collapses to ONE pair per dispatchable agent: the agent's CONFIGURED model (Config.agent_model/1 — the model that agent actually runs without a task pin), not every available catalog slug. Regression: the live default payload drops from 144 pairs to ~one-per-enabled-agent (~5-6), i.e. an order of magnitude, and fits one MCP read comfortably. Measured before/after pair count reported in the implemented note.

An agent with NO configured model (Config.agent_model/1 returns nil) still surfaces ONE row flagged model: nil / model_required: true (so the writer sees the agent exists but must pin a model) — it is NOT silently dropped and NOT expanded to its catalog.

The full per-model catalog stays reachable, unchanged, two ways: include_all: true (every available {agent,model}, today's 144-pair behaviour) AND the agents filter (naming an agent returns ITS full available catalog so the writer can weigh that agent's model options). Only the unfiltered default collapses.
antigravity (model-incapable, model_families: []) surfaces its single model-less row as today — the configured-model collapse must not break the no-model agent.

WRITER CONTRACT updated (SKILL.md + orchestrator-surface-inventory.md): the default brief answers 'which AGENT, at its standing model' (the routing index); to compare model options for one agent, pass agents: [name] or include_all; for KPI depth, the aggregate_* family. scripts/sync-harness-skills.sh run.

Tests (no Process.sleep; assert specific counts/values; @spec on every def AND defp): default yields one row per enabled agent keyed to its configured model; an agent with a configured model != its catalog default still shows the configured one; a no-configured-model agent shows the model_required row; include_all + agents:[x] still expand to the full catalog; antigravity row intact. mix precommit.full green.
out_of_scope: The agents/fields/domains/include_all params themselves (shipped in Task 273 — this only changes what the UNFILTERED default selects)
Re-introducing a capability leg (removed Task 272) — stays 3 legs
Any new KPI/aggregate tool — depth lives in the existing aggregate_* family
Changing Config.agent_model resolution or block/availability semantics — read them as-is
task.body:
Follow-up to Task 273 (landed 4d1ceae). Dogfooding the recompiled node: brief() default returned 144 pairs, down from 175 but still ~146KB — it still blows the writer's context. Root cause: 273 defined dispatchable as available+enabled, but a multi-model frontend (cursor) has its ENTIRE ~139-slug catalog 'available' (only opus-4-8-thinking-high is blocked), so available+enabled barely slims it. 273's ACs were satisfied; the definition was too loose.

Correct slim: the default is a ROUTING INDEX — one row per dispatchable agent at its STANDING model (Config.agent_model/1), the model it runs without a task pin. That collapses cursor's 139 rows to one (its configured model) and the whole default to ~5-6 rows. Model-OPTION exploration for a given agent stays opt-in via agents:[name] or include_all — the writer only reaches for the catalog when deliberately weighing one agent's tiers (e.g. cursor-on-Opus vs codex). An agent with no configured model surfaces a single model_required row so it is visible-but-flagged, never silently dropped or catalog-expanded.

Routing rationale (dogfooded): codex/gpt-5.5 free, mcp 9.0 / descripex 9.0 / truthfulness 8.5, success 0.96/82 — strongest fit for this read-surface refinement. cursor/Opus blocked. -> codex / gpt-5.5.

task.title: Lander prunes the run branch + worktree after a successful land (stop the harness/<run-id> + worktree accumulation)
acceptance_criteria: After a successful ff-push + writeback (the SAME success path that enqueues the audit), the lander deletes the local `harness/<run-id>` branch AND removes the implementer run worktree at `<worktrees_root>/.harness/<project>/<run-id>` (the dir Harness.Run created for the implementer; NOT the lander's own reusable detached `landing/` worktree, which must survive).

Prune is best-effort and ordered AFTER the push succeeds: a prune failure is logged (Logger.warning, same style as persist_landed_sha/writeback) and NEVER un-lands the merge or raises. The push is the point of no return; pruning is cleanup.

Prune fires ONLY on a confirmed successful land. The conflict / blocked / resolver-failure / land-cap paths retain the branch + worktree unchanged (dispatch-reland still needs them) — assert a rebase-conflict run keeps both.

Guard against pruning something a live run still owns: the branch is only deleted when its run is settled/landed (no in-flight Harness.Run for that run_id). Use the existing supervisor/registry check or the post-land invariant; document which in a comment.

Tests (no Process.sleep; assert specific filesystem/branch state; @spec on every new def AND defp): a happy-path land removes branch + run worktree and keeps the lander's reusable worktree; a conflict/blocked land retains both; a prune failure is swallowed (land still reported success). mix precommit.full green; coverage >= 80% on lander.ex.
out_of_scope: Touching the landed_sha record writeback (that is Task 276 — this task is purely git/fs cleanup).
Remote branch deletion (harness only ff-pushes commits to <target>; it never pushes the harness/<run-id> branch to origin, so there is nothing remote to prune).
A periodic sweeper for already-accumulated orphans — this fixes the going-forward leak; a one-off backfill of pre-existing orphans is manual (already done for rmap on 2026-06-13).
task.body:
Discovered 2026-06-13: the dashboard's "unmerged runs" list and the on-disk worktree dir both accumulate because the lander never prunes after a successful land. rmap had 31 stale `harness/run-*` branches and ~18 orphaned implementer worktrees under `~/_DATA/worktrees/.harness/rmap/`, all for runs that had cleanly landed (rebased copy on `development`). The branch is INTENTIONALLY retained after a run *settles* so dispatch-reland can recover an approved-unlanded run — but once the run has actually LANDED, recovery is moot and the branch + its implementer worktree are pure litter.

The fix lives in the lander because the lander is the only component that knows the land succeeded. After the ff-push + writeback (the same success path that calls enqueue_audit/3 in lib/harness/lander.ex ~line 350-399), delete the local `harness/<run-id>` branch and `git worktree remove` the implementer run worktree. Mirror the best-effort discipline already used for persist_landed_sha and the rmap writeback: log on failure, never un-land.

CRITICAL distinction the implementer must get right: there are TWO worktrees per landed run — (1) the implementer run worktree `<root>/.harness/<project>/<run-id>` (created by Harness.Run, this is the one to remove) and (2) the lander's OWN reusable detached worktree (the `landing/` dir it rebases in, which must persist for the next land). Remove only (1).
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1781328687804-3a2ad2d5, 469216bad537e27478e5e91438b09604651c2dac).

task.title: Harden landed_sha persistence: lander verify-after-write + mechanical reconcile so a landed run never shows as phantom-unmerged in the dashboard
acceptance_criteria: Lander verify-after-write: after `ResultStore.mark_landed(run_id, sha)` on the success path, re-read the record and if `landed_sha` is still nil, retry once; a still-failing write is logged (never un-lands). Root cause is a rare lost write — a settle-time full-record persist racing the lander's mark_landed and clobbering landed_sha back to nil (observed as a 1-in-231 singleton: run-1781317513615-1e03e688 landed as e8312bb but recorded landed_sha=nil).

Mechanical reconcile (mantra-clean — a git-ancestry COUNT, not judgment): a pure function that, for a done+approve run record with landed_sha == nil, sets landed_sha when the run's delivery is provably on the project's target_branch — i.e. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` of the run's landed commit (or the task's rmap shipped_in) against origin/<target>. It only fills a fact already true on disk; it never decides whether work is 'good' or 'should land'.

Wire the reconcile into the dashboard history load (lib/harness/dashboard/live.ex, where history_all / landed_entry? is computed) so a phantom-unmerged landed run self-heals on mount/restream without a manual ResultStore.mark_landed call. Cheap: only runs for records with landed_sha == nil, and short-circuits when the project has no local source / target_branch.
landed_entry?/2 semantics are unchanged (landed_sha != nil); this task only makes landed_sha reliably reflect reality, it does NOT change how the dashboard classifies merged vs unmerged.

Tests (no Process.sleep; assert specific values; @spec on every new def AND defp): a simulated lost write (mark_landed clobbered by a later persist) is recovered by verify-after-write; the reconcile fills landed_sha for a record whose commit IS an ancestor of target and leaves it nil when it is NOT (genuinely-unlanded approved run stays unmerged); dashboard history of a phantom-unmerged landed run shows it as merged after reconcile. mix precommit.full green; coverage >= 80% on the changed modules.
out_of_scope: Branch/worktree pruning (Task 275).
Re-landing genuinely-unlanded approved runs — those legitimately show as unmerged and are recovered via dispatch-reland; the reconcile must NOT mark them landed (assert this).
Any new judgment in harness — the reconcile is strictly a mechanical ancestry check that backfills a fact; it does not re-decide approval, success, or land-worthiness.
task.body:
Discovered 2026-06-13: the operator saw run-1781317513615-1e03e688 stuck as "unmerged" in the /harness dashboard even though it had landed (commit e8312bb on development, rmap task 48 done --verified --shipped-in e8312bb). The dashboard classifies unmerged purely off the persisted run-record field `status.landed_sha` (lib/harness/dashboard/live.ex landed_entry?/2 = landed_sha != nil) — NOT off git branches. This run's record had landed_sha = nil despite the lander having ff-pushed it.

The lander DOES call ResultStore.mark_landed/2 on the success path (lib/harness/lander.ex persist_landed_sha/2 ~line 370), but it is best-effort: a failed/clobbered write is only logged. Across 231 done+approve records exactly one had landed_sha=nil, so this is a rare lost write — most likely the run gen_statem's settle-time full-record persist racing the lander's read-modify-write and overwriting landed_sha back to nil. Manually backfilled via ResultStore.mark_landed on the live node on 2026-06-13; this task makes it self-healing.

Two layers: (1) verify-after-write in the lander (re-read, retry once) closes the common race; (2) a mechanical reconcile on the dashboard history load backfills landed_sha whenever the run's landed commit / task shipped_in is provably an ancestor of origin/<target> — so even a write lost for any reason heals on the next dashboard view. Both are mantra-clean: counting whether a commit is on a branch is mechanics, not judgment. The reconcile must be careful NOT to mark genuinely-unlanded approved runs (no ancestor on target) as landed — those stay unmerged and recover via dispatch-reland.
task.implemented: Lander verify-after-write (re-read + retry once on mark_landed) + mechanical git-ancestry reconcile backfilling landed_sha on dashboard history load when the run commit is provably an ancestor of origin/<target>; never marks genuinely-unlanded approved runs. Landed via manual keep-both salvage of lander_test.exs conflict vs task 275.

task.title: dispatch-compare: per-adapter model override (cross-family A/B is structurally broken)
acceptance_criteria: dispatch-compare accepts an optional models map (adapter-name -> model) and passes each adapter its own model.
When an adapter is omitted from the map, its OWN default model is used; the task pinned model is never applied to a non-matching adapter family.
cursor-vs-grok compare on a task pinned to composer-2.5-fast spawns BOTH adapters successfully (grok on grok-build).
Invalid (adapter, model) pairs are rejected up front with a clear error, not a mid-run agent_spawn_failed.
Test covers a two-family compare where the task pinned model is valid for only one of them.
out_of_scope: No change to single-adapter dispatch-task / dispatch-await model resolution.
No change to how tasks pin model at creation in rmap.
task.body:
`dispatch-compare` cannot run a fair cross-family A/B (e.g. cursor vs grok) because it has no per-adapter `model` parameter. It ingests the task once and inherits the task's single pinned `model`, then applies that one model to EVERY adapter. Since `model` is now required at task creation and is always family-specific, the inherited model is valid for at most one adapter family — every other adapter fails at spawn.

Observed (tapakly task 134, pinned assignee=cursor model=composer-2.5-fast, compared cursor vs grok):
- cursor half ran and settled normally;
- grok half failed immediately: agent_spawn_failed {:invalid_model_for_adapter, Harness.AgentAdapter.Grok, "composer-2.5-fast"}.

So the comparison yielded only the adapter whose family matched the task's pinned model — i.e. no comparison at all. This blocks the entire purpose of cross-family agent evaluation (the cold-start problem: we cannot get a grok/codex data point on a task pinned to cursor without this).

NOTE (not a separate bug — don't chase it): the dashboard/result-record `agent` field reads "claude" on BOTH compare runs. That is by design — dispatch-compare renders the prompt ONCE for claude (`rmap delegate --to claude`) so every adapter runs an identical prompt, and that render-agent is what lands in the `agent` column. The REAL executor is the `adapter` field (here AgentAdapter.Cursor vs AgentAdapter.Grok). So the three-way mismatch (agent=claude, model=composer-2.5-fast, adapter=Grok) is exactly two facts: render-agent=claude (fairness) + the actual cross-family-model bug above. Do not add per-adapter `agent`-field rewriting — leave the render-agent semantics alone; fix only the model threading.

Fix: add an optional per-adapter model map to the compare entry point and thread it down to each run's spawn, falling back to each adapter's default model (NOT the task's pinned model) when unspecified.

- Harness.Batch.AgentEvaluation.compare/4 (or its opts): accept models: %{"grok" => "grok-build", "cursor" => "composer-2.5-fast"} (adapter-name-keyed). For any adapter absent from the map, resolve that adapter's OWN default model — never reuse the task's pinned model across families.
- MCP surface dispatch-compare: add an optional models object param (adapter-name -> model string), documented as overriding the inherited task model per adapter. Keep current behaviour when omitted EXCEPT the per-family default fallback above (today's "inherit one pinned model for all" is the bug, not the contract).
- Validate each (adapter, model) pair against the adapter's accepted models BEFORE spawning, so a bad pair is a clear up-front error, not an agent_spawn_failed mid-run.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1781329708657-858e6f13, 45a941e3bdde4d0a5dcac52a44efdd7fa2ada78a).

task.title: Poller double-dispatch guard: skip a pending task that already has a live/queued run (mantra-clean dedup, not a re-dispatch)
acceptance_criteria: Before enqueueing a Run.Worker job for a pending task, the poller skips it when a run for the SAME {project_name, item_id} is already live (Harness.Run.Registry / supervisor-list_runs) OR queued/executing on the project's Oban queue (an available/executing job with that run target). This is a mechanical COUNT-then-skip (mantra-clean: count existing runs, do not start another), never a judgment about run quality.

Root cause to fix (observed 2026-06-13): task 276's land-conflict reverted it to pending; the cron poller ticked twice before roadmap-mark_in_progress wrote back, so it dispatched two fresh implementer runs (run-1781330597715-52cea0a7 + run-1781330694166-6fb36d58, ~97s apart) that re-implemented already-approved work. The mark_in_progress writeback is too slow to be the only guard — the dedup must consult LIVE run/Oban state, not just the rmap status field.

The guard keys on {project_name, item_id} (the dispatch identity), not run_id (each re-dispatch mints a new run_id, so run_id can't dedup). Document which live-state source is authoritative (Registry vs Oban queue introspection) in a comment.

A genuinely failed/cancelled prior run (settled, no live process, task legitimately back to pending) is STILL dispatchable — the guard blocks only concurrent duplicates, never a sequential retry of a settled task. Assert both: two ticks within one in-flight window enqueue exactly once; a tick after the prior run settled enqueues again.

Tests (no Process.sleep; assert specific enqueue counts/Oban job state; @spec on every new def AND defp): simulate two poller ticks for the same pending task with a live run present -> exactly one enqueue; same task with the prior run settled -> enqueues; a different pending task is unaffected. mix precommit.full green; coverage >= 80% on the changed modules.
out_of_scope: Changing how mark_in_progress writes back (that is a latency optimization, not the fix — the guard must not DEPEND on writeback speed).
Any global cross-queue concurrency cap (out of scope; open-source Oban has none and this guard is per-task identity, not a global limiter).
The lander-side resolver regression (separate task) — this task is purely the poller-side duplicate-dispatch guard.
task.body:
Discovered 2026-06-13 during the task 275/276 land. The cron RoadmapPoller gates dispatch on queue-headroom + adapter availability (Task 51) but NOT on 'is this exact task already being worked.' When a task is briefly pending (e.g. a land-conflict reverted it, or a cancelled run settled it back) and two cron ticks fall inside the window before mark_in_progress writes back, BOTH ticks see pending and each enqueues a fresh implementer run. Result: two concurrent runs re-implementing the same approved task = pure token waste (observed: 276 dispatched twice, both cancelled manually).

The fix is a mechanical dedup at enqueue time: count whether a live (Harness.Run.Registry) or queued/executing (Oban) run already targets {project_name, item_id}; if so, skip this tick's enqueue for that task. This is counting facts, not judging them — fully mantra-clean. Keying on {project, item_id} (not run_id) is essential because every re-dispatch mints a new run_id. The guard must NOT rely on the rmap status field alone (that is exactly the slow-writeback signal that failed here) — it consults live runtime/Oban state.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1781333043448-35b934bb, ece1ed422d178e65f87727cab7e5c40197dab2ec).

task.title: Lander resolver regression: rebase conflict returns landing job completed WITHOUT invoking the resolver or landing (silent no-op)
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce + fix the silent no-op: a rebase conflict during land MUST route to the resolver path (Harness.Lander.Resolver, Task 189) OR, on resolver failure/disabled, to the block/re-dispatch resilience path — it must NEVER return the Oban landing job as state=completed with errors=[] while the run stays unlanded and the task stays in_progress. A landing job that did not land is not 'completed'.

Root cause to find (observed 2026-06-13): task 276 approved on branch harness/run-1781328687948-38d9a1d8, conflicted on test/harness/lander_test.exs against the just-landed task 275 (lander.ex auto-merged; the test file had a real keep-both content conflict). BOTH the auto-land job (1081) and a dispatch-reland job (1082) returned state=completed, errors=[], yet 276 never landed (c865fe7 not an ancestor of origin/development) and the resolver was never invoked. It was salvaged manually (keep-both) and ff-pushed as 390c3c6. Determine why the {:conflict,_} -> {:resolve,...} branch in Resilience.plan/2 (or its lander caller) did not fire.

If the resolver fired but failed silently, the fallback to block/re-dispatch must engage and the task must NOT be left in_progress with a stranded approved branch (which then triggers the poller double-dispatch in Task 278).

Tests (no Process.sleep; assert specific job outcome + branch/ancestry state; @spec on every new def AND defp): a land that hits a real rebase conflict either lands via resolver (branch becomes ancestor of target) or routes to blocked/re-dispatch — assert it is NEVER reported completed-but-unlanded; a resolver-disabled conflict routes to the resilience fallback, not a silent completion. mix precommit.full green; coverage >= 80% on lander.ex + resilience.ex.
out_of_scope: Re-implementing the resolver agent itself (Task 189 shipped it; this task fixes why the conflict path bypassed it).
The poller-side duplicate-dispatch guard (Task 278) — although this regression is what stranded 276 and fed the double-dispatch, the poller guard is a separate change.
Changing the keep-both default resolution policy.
task.body:
Discovered 2026-06-13 during the task 275/276 land. Task 189 shipped a lander conflict-resolver: on a rebase conflict the lander is supposed to spawn a cross-family merge-resolver agent in the detached landing worktree, reconcile the markers, git add + rebase --continue, then ff-push; resolver failure falls back to block/re-dispatch. A still-conflicted tree must NEVER be reported as landed.

What actually happened with 276: its approved branch conflicted with the just-landed 275 in test/harness/lander_test.exs (a clean keep-both — two independently-added test cases in the same region). Two landing-queue jobs (auto-land 1081, dispatch-reland 1082) both came back state=completed with errors=[], but 276 was not landed and the resolver agent never ran. The conflict had to be salvaged by hand. So the {:conflict,_} -> resolver branch is being bypassed and the landing job is silently completing as a no-op — the worst outcome (looks landed, isn't, and strands the approved branch so the poller re-dispatches it, see Task 278).

Investigate the lander's conflict detection + Resilience.plan/2 dispatch: does it detect the conflict at all? Does it classify the dirty rebase state as success? Is the resolver gated behind a config/eligibility check that silently no-ops? Fix so a conflict deterministically either resolves-and-lands or routes to the blocked/re-dispatch sink, and a landing job NEVER reports completed without an actual ff-push.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1781333031694-adc102e7, fbab2b0fcdf69b4fd9d29fecfeb2c4b399f48259).

task.title: Lander mis-marks reassigned task ids — run→task_id writeback + concurrent rmap-filing id collision corrupts roadmap status
acceptance_criteria: Lander writeback no longer keys solely on the mutable numeric task id: before flipping a task to done --shipped-in, it verifies the id still resolves to the SAME task it dispatched (immutable dispatch-time snapshot — title/content hash or a stable slug). On drift, the writeback ABORTS and surfaces a drift error rather than marking the reassigned task done.

Concurrent roadmap-filing dispatches cannot both claim the same numeric id range: ids allocated atomically at file/land time (or a per-dispatch id-range reservation), so two parallel `rmap new` passes can't both land 200-204.

Regression test reproducing the 2026-06-14 incident: dispatch run R for task id N; between dispatch and land, reassign id N to a DIFFERENT task (concurrent filing); assert R's land either writes back to the ORIGINAL task or aborts with a drift error — never a silent false-done on the reassigned task.
Mis-mark audit: a `done` task whose `shipped_in` commit diff touches none of its `files_to_modify` is flagged (detects this class of corruption in already-landed history).
out_of_scope: Re-architecting rmap id assignment to UUIDs — numeric ids stay; the fix is collision-safe allocation + drift-checked writeback.
Repairing the specific tapakly T200/T203 false-dones — already corrected manually (commit d67a0be in tapakly).
task.body:
Observed in tapakly on 2026-06-14. Two roadmap-filing passes were dispatched concurrently into
the SAME 200-204 id space: an investor-tour browser pass (200=facet-bug, 202=seeds, 203=tour,
204=LLM-spike) and a T169 persona gap-analysis run. The T169 run landed first and reassigned ids
200-211 to persona tasks. The concurrently-dispatched investor-tour runs then landed, and
`Harness.Lander` marked them done BY run.task_id — flipping the now-reassigned persona tasks
(200=FSBO onboarding, 203=Developer LiveViews) to false-done, with `shipped_in` pointing at the
unrelated facet-bug / tour-reground commits. Net: two tasks marked done that were never built,
their real work shipped under a lost id, and the operator had to repair the ledger by hand.

Root cause is the run→task_id writeback assuming the numeric id is immutable across the
dispatch→land window. It isn't, under concurrent rmap-filing. Fix both legs: collision-safe id
allocation so parallel filings don't overlap, AND a drift-checked writeback so a stale id can
never silently mark the wrong task done. This is the rmap-skill 'tasks.toml is a machine-read
contract' hazard actually manifesting — harness acted on a reassigned id.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1781420466585-4cb4433f, 5b82a9bcd2893b63568f4cbb9ae00735ddd4d885).

task.title: dispatch-reland on rebase-conflict re-dispatches a fresh implementer instead of retaining the branch
acceptance_criteria: A MANUAL, operator-invoked dispatch-reland whose harness/<run-id> branch hits a rebase conflict the merge-resolver cannot reconcile retains the branch, surfaces a conflict outcome via the witness sink, does NOT advance or reset roadmap status, and spawns ZERO fresh implementer runs. This is the operator-invoked reland path ONLY.

Confirm whether the reland enqueue path routes a conflict through the merge-resolver (Harness.Lander.resolve_or_abort / Resolver, Task 189) the way the autonomous lander does. If reland BYPASSES the resolver, that inconsistency is the real defect (a CHANGELOG [Unreleased] union conflict should auto-reconcile, not redispatch) — fix it there. State the finding either way.

Regression test (no Process.sleep; assert specific values, never 'any error passes'; @spec on every new def AND defp): a manual reland of an approved run whose branch conflicts on a since-modified target file leaves task status unchanged, retains the branch, emits a conflict witness event, and creates ZERO new runs. A SECOND test asserts the autonomous merge-train conflict path (resilience.ex plan/2) is UNCHANGED.
out_of_scope: Removing or weakening the autonomous merge-train's {:conflict} -> {:redispatch} resilience action (resilience.ex plan/2, capped) or the merge-resolver -> re-dispatch fallback (CLAUDE.md) — those are deliberate, capped AUTONOMOUS recovery and must stay intact.

The structural CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] always-conflicts root cause (every task appends to the same region) — that belongs in a separate sibling task via a .gitattributes union merge driver, not here.
task.body:
Observed in ccxt_extract dogfooding (2026-06-14). dispatch-reland on an approved-but-unlanded run whose retained harness/<run-id> branch fails to rebase onto the target (here: a CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] conflict — every task appends to the same region, so any branch that lands after a sibling conflicts) does NOT retain the branch for manual repair as the docs promise. Instead harness re-dispatches the task as a fresh implementer run.

Concrete repro: ccxt_extract task 119, dispatch-reland run-1781420962974-a3f1506e (state done / verdict approve). The rebase hit a CHANGELOG.md conflict; instead of a retained-branch + conflict outcome, a brand-new implementer run run-1781423241832-15849dd4 (task 119, fresh agent PID) appeared seconds later. Root cause of an apparent 'rogue dispatcher' loop: every reland of a conflict-prone branch (119, 78c — both touch CHANGELOG) silently spawned a fresh implementer, burning tokens against an explicit operator pause. Autonomy was OFF (master_enabled false, project effective false) and the driving session had no cron, so this is purely the reland-on-conflict path.

Expected (per harness-workflow.md): 'Conflict / push-rejected retains the branch for repair — never lands red.' A rebase conflict during reland must (a) leave the branch retained, (b) surface a conflict outcome via the witness sink, (c) NOT advance or reset roadmap status, and (d) spawn zero implementer runs. Operator resolves manually (the working fix here was a manual ff-land with a CHANGELOG union resolve).

Investigate Harness.Lander.land/1 (or the reland enqueue path) for the branch where a failed rebase falls through to re-dispatch rather than a retain+notify terminal state.

---
2026-06-14 (scope correction, pre-dispatch review): the original unconditional 'zero new runs on ANY conflict' framing contradicts a DELIBERATE design — resilience.ex:94 maps {:conflict,_} -> {:redispatch, attempt+1} (capped), and CLAUDE.md documents the merge-resolver -> re-dispatch fallback as intended autonomous recovery. Implementing the original ACs literally would delete load-bearing autonomous conflict-recovery for ALL projects. The real bug is NARROWER: an operator-invoked (manual) reland under an explicit autonomy pause must not inherit that autonomous redispatch — it should retain+notify. Scope the fix to the manual reland path; leave the autonomous merge-train resilience + resolver fallback intact (see out_of_scope). Also verify reland routes conflicts through the resolver like auto-land does — if it doesn't, the observed CHANGELOG union conflict should have auto-reconciled and never redispatched.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1781427866003-90f9afa9, 01e60019075b4b094fc37c7fcf4177b40518eb96).

task.title: Reviewer-stage git-add fatals on gitignored .harness/ → review_stuck blocks the gate; .harness-retained artifact leaks into commits
acceptance_criteria: Worktree.do_commit/diff_size staging no longer fatals (exit 1) when the worktree contains untracked, gitignored .harness/ content (e.g. the reviewer's .harness/review.json). Repro: in a repo whose .gitignore lists `.harness/`, with `.harness/review.json` present, the current `git add -A -- . :(exclude).harness` exits 1 with 'paths ignored: .harness' — this surfaced as run-1781425518611-74749b75 reason `review_stuck` and bounced task 281 back to pending. The reviewer must be able to stage its source fixes and have its verdict read.

The `.harness-retained` artifact (NOT matched by the `.harness` exclude pathspec and NOT gitignored) is no longer staged/committed into agent work. Exclude the whole `.harness*` artifact family, not just the `.harness/` dir.

The fix is verified across BOTH repo states: a target repo that gitignores `.harness/` (harness itself) AND one that does not — staging must succeed (exit 0) and never commit any `.harness`/`.harness-retained` artifact in either.

Regression test (no Process.sleep; assert specific exit/staged-set, never 'any error passes'; @spec on every new def AND defp): a worktree with untracked `.harness/review.json` + `.harness-retained` stages the source change, excludes both artifacts, and commit/diff_size succeed.
out_of_scope: Changing what the reviewer writes into .harness/ or the verdict-file contract — this is purely the staging/exclude mechanics in Worktree.
The dispatch-reland conflict-handling fix (Task 281) — separate concern; this bug merely blocked 281's reviewer from grading.
task.body:
Observed 2026-06-14 dispatching harness task 281. Run run-1781425518611-74749b75: implementer delivered cleanly to branch harness/run-1781425518611-74749b75 (+173 lines, tests), but the run settled :failed with reason review_stuck: Reviewer failed to run {:git_failed, [add, -A, --, ., :(exclude).harness], 1, "paths ignored by .gitignore: .harness"}. The verdict was never read; task 281 bounced to pending.

Root cause in lib/harness/worktree.ex:69 @stage_pathspec [".", ":(exclude).harness"] (@artifact_dir = ".harness"), used by do_commit/2 (L471) and diff_size/1 (L512). In a repo that gitignores `.harness/` (harness's own .gitignore:27 = `.harness/`), an untracked `.harness/review.json` makes `git add -A -- . :(exclude).harness` exit 1 (git treats the positive `.` matching an ignored path as a fatal use-f error; the exclude pathspec does not suppress the fatal). Confirmed by repro in the survived worktree.

Second, coupled defect: a `.harness-retained` file (82 B) sits in the worktree, is NOT gitignored (the `.harness/` pattern doesn't match `.harness-retained`) and is NOT excluded by `:(exclude).harness`, so `git add -A` stages it — a harness artifact leaking into agent commits. Fix must exclude the whole `.harness*` family.

This is a run-lifecycle mechanical bug (harness substrate, not agent judgment) and it intermittently blocks the reviewer gate — it is why 281 could not land despite good work.
task.implemented: Two-move staging in Worktree.stage_worktree/1: bare 'git add -A' (no pathspec, so a gitignored .harness/ is silently skipped instead of fataling git's ignored-path guard) then 'git reset' unstaging the @artifact_paths family (.harness dir + .harness-active/.harness-retained markers). status/diff filter the same family via @stage_exclude. 4 regression tests across both gitignore states; verified .harness/review.json + .harness-retained never commit and diff_size excludes them. Hand-built (run-lifecycle substrate / catch-22).

task.title: ProjectRegistry.upsert/1 — replace-or-insert with live Oban queue scaling (foundational)
acceptance_criteria: Public Harness.ProjectRegistry.upsert/1 (accepts a %Harness.Project{} or attrs keyword/map via build_project/1, like register/1) added with an api() annotation. Unlike register/1 (which returns {:error, {:duplicate, name}} on an existing name), upsert REPLACES an existing registration and INSERTS a new one — idempotent.

On upsert: the in-memory state map entry is replaced, Harness.ProjectRegistry.Persistence.upsert/1 writes the row (on_conflict: :replace_all), the project's Oban queue is ensured, AND when concurrency_cap changed the queue limit is updated live via Oban.scale_queue (today Harness.Oban.ensure_project_queue only START_QUEUEs — extend it or scale within upsert). A cap change takes effect with no BEAM restart.

Test: upsert on an existing project name replaces its fields (e.g. new concurrency_cap) in BOTH the in-memory list and the projects table, and the Oban queue limit reflects the new cap (assert via Oban queue state, not a sleep).
Test: upsert on a brand-new name inserts the row and starts its queue; ProjectRegistry.list/0 then includes it.
Test (NEVER-HIDE-FAILURES): a re-upsert with identical attrs is a clean no-op-equivalent (idempotent), flunking on any unexpected error.
mix precommit.full green.
task.body:
Foundational primitive for the config-surface bundle (blocks 284 + 285). The recurring operator pain: editing config/dev.local.exs to change a project's concurrency_cap / paths does NOTHING because Postgres is the source of truth and config only seeds rows whose name is ABSENT (ProjectRegistry.import_missing_config_projects/2). The fix direction is to make the DB the live edit surface — but register/1 REJECTS an existing name ({:error, {:duplicate, name}}), and only the internal Persistence.upsert/1 (on_conflict: :replace_all) replaces, and it bypasses the GenServer's in-memory map + Oban queue.

Add a public, GenServer-routed upsert/1 that replaces-or-inserts in one shot: in-memory map, Postgres row, Oban queue (started if new, SCALED via Oban.scale_queue if the cap changed). This is the primitive both the dashboard cap-editor/register-form (284) and the reproducible seed script (285) call. The dev.local.exs rationale comments already wished for exactly 'an upsert'.

Mechanics only (mantra-clean): replace a map entry, write a row, scale a queue to a number. No judgment.
