task.title: Dashboard: concurrency_cap editor + project register/edit/unregister form (close the last config-surface holes)
acceptance_criteria: A `set_concurrency` LiveView event on /harness/settings (SettingsLive) sets a registered project's concurrency_cap via Harness.ProjectRegistry.upsert/1 — value persists to Postgres and scales the Oban queue live (no restart). Mirrors the existing `set_landing` handler pattern (settings_live.ex ~line 104) and per-project landing form (components.ex ~lines 730-774).

A project register/edit form on the same page upserts a project via ProjectRegistry.upsert/1 with: name, source local path (rendered/stored as {:local, path}; a github url is acceptable as an optional alternative source), roadmap_path, check_command, target_branch, concurrency_cap. Editing an existing project pre-fills its current values; submitting an existing name UPDATES it (upsert), a new name CREATES it.
An unregister/remove control per project calls ProjectRegistry.unregister/1 and the row disappears from the list.
The config_inspector cap row is no longer the ONLY surface for concurrency_cap (it may remain as a read-only mirror, but the editable control lives in SettingsLive).
UI matches the existing dashboard design system (the tokens/components already used by SettingsLive) — incremental, NOT a redesign.

Tests (LiveViewTest, NEVER-HIDE-FAILURES — flunk on unexpected): page renders the cap editor + register form; set_concurrency on a registered project updates ProjectRegistry.list/0 + the projects table; register a NEW project via the form -> appears in list/0; edit an existing project's path -> reflected; unregister -> removed.
mix precommit.full green.
out_of_scope: Editing settings already covered by SettingsLive today (landing policy/target, cron autonomy + schedule, agent enable, reviewer eligibility/pin, agent/reviewer models, run timeouts, default agent, model catalog) — those handlers exist; do not duplicate them.
Deleting config/dev.local.exs or the config restructure — that is Task 285.
task.body:
After Task 283 lands ProjectRegistry.upsert/1, close the two remaining per-project config holes that keep the operator editing config/dev.local.exs. Verified against SettingsLive: the dashboard ALREADY edits live -> Postgres for landing/cron/agent-models/reviewer/run-timeouts/default-agent/model-catalog. The ONLY gaps are (1) concurrency_cap (currently read-only in config_inspector as `cap=N`) and (2) project registration/editing of source path / roadmap_path / check_command (no form; only config-seed, the dispatch-register_project MCP tool, or IEx).

Add a concurrency_cap editor and a project register/edit/unregister form to /harness/settings, both routed through ProjectRegistry.upsert/1 (283) / unregister/1, so the dashboard becomes the COMPLETE per-project edit surface writing Postgres. This is what makes deleting config/dev.local.exs (285) lossless and the 'edit a file, restart, nothing happens' trap go away — there's a live UI that actually writes the source of truth.

Incremental UI against the existing dashboard design system — match settings_live.ex / components.ex patterns, don't invent a new look.

config/dev.local.exs.example is DELETED and replaced by a tracked priv/repo/seeds.exs.example: an Elixir seed script that upserts the project registrations via Harness.ProjectRegistry.upsert/1, carrying the per-project rationale comments. It opens with a prominent header stating: NOT read at boot; Postgres is the source of truth; edit + run `mix harness.seed` to upsert OR use the dashboard /harness/settings; for a RUNNING node use the dashboard / IEx upsert — this script is the fresh-DB / reset path only.
.gitignore drops `/config/dev.local.exs` and adds `/priv/repo/seeds.exs` (the real host seed stays gitignored; only the .example is tracked).
mix.exs aliases gain: `ecto.setup` (ecto.create + ecto.migrate + run priv/repo/seeds.exs when present), `ecto.reset` (ecto.drop + ecto.setup), and `harness.seed` (run priv/repo/seeds.exs).

Keep the rationale comment.

Boot guard in Harness.ProjectRegistry: when Persistence.enabled?() (repo_enabled) AND `config :harness, :projects` is non-empty, Logger.warning that config projects are seed-only and shadowed by the Postgres projects table, naming the dashboard/seeds edit path. (It will not fire after this change, since dev.exs no longer sets :projects — it is a net for re-introduction.)

Docs updated: skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md (the dev.local.exs registration instructions ~lines 43-70 + 582 -> dashboard /harness/settings or the seed script), priv/playbooks/dispatch-single-task.md (~line 10), CLAUDE.md 'First-time DB' row -> `mix ecto.setup`. Historical references in roadmap/tasks.toml, roadmap/data.json, CHANGELOG.md are left untouched.

Tests (NEVER-HIDE-FAILURES): boot guard emits the warning when repo_enabled and config :projects is non-empty, and is silent when empty; a guard/grep test asserts config/dev.exs sets no :projects key.
mix precommit.full green.
out_of_scope: Physically removing the operator's untracked config/dev.local.exs from their main checkout, exporting HARNESS_RUN_MEM_THRESHOLD_GB, and restarting iex — those are host-local steps the operator does inline; the file is gitignored and not present in a worktree.
Removing the config-seed mechanism (import_missing_config_projects) — library/repo_enabled:false consumers still need it.
Changing the test/harness/worktree/isolation_test.exs fixture that writes a throwaway dev.local.exs (incidental filename in a temp worktree, not the real file).
task.body:
The payoff task: once the dashboard is the complete per-project edit surface (283 + 284), delete the config/dev.local.exs trap for good. Every AI agent (and the operator, repeatedly) edits that gitignored file to change a project's cap/paths, restarts, and nothing happens — Postgres is the source of truth; config only seeds ABSENT names, so an existing row ignores the file forever.

Safety fact: the live Postgres projects table already holds all 9 projects, so removing the file/seed is lossless — on restart load_projects reads them from Postgres. The only non-DB value in dev.local.exs is mem_threshold_kb: 18 GB, which moves to a HARNESS_RUN_MEM_THRESHOLD_GB env var (matching the HARNESS_* pattern).

Replace the read-at-boot-but-silently-shadowed file with a RUN-to-apply priv/repo/seeds.exs (gitignored; .example tracked) that upserts Postgres via ProjectRegistry.upsert/1 — editing it does nothing until you run `mix harness.seed`, and running it actually writes the source of truth. Add a boot guard that warns if anyone re-introduces a config :projects block under repo_enabled. Update the docs that currently send people to dev.local.exs.

task.title: Dispatch in-flight idempotency: a second dispatch of {project, task_id} with a non-terminal run must return the existing run, not spawn a duplicate
acceptance_criteria: Both Oban enqueue sites — Harness.Run.Worker.enqueue/4 (worker.ex ~line 84) and Harness.Batch.enqueue_item/3 (batch.ex ~line 253) — set a `unique:` option on RunWorker.new/1 keyed on the job args identifying the task ({project_name, item_id}) over the NON-TERMINAL job states (:available, :scheduled, :executing, :retryable; period: :infinity). Centralize the unique spec in one helper so the two sites can't drift.

When a dispatch is enqueued while a non-terminal Oban job for the SAME {project_name, item_id} already exists, Oban.insert returns the existing (conflict?: true) job and the dispatch path returns {:ok, <existing_run_id>, job} — NOT a second job and NOT an error. The caller gets the live run's handle (this also closes the 'error with no run_id, so I retried blind' gap).

A terminal prior run (done/failed/cancelled/discarded/completed) does NOT block re-dispatch — the recovery verbs (dispatch-reland / dispatch-rereview / dispatch-resume_failed) and an honest fresh re-dispatch of a settled task still enqueue normally. Uniqueness applies ONLY to the in-flight window.

Test (the repro, NEVER-HIDE-FAILURES): dispatch a task, then dispatch the SAME {project, task_id} again while the first job is still executing -> the second call returns the SAME run_id as the first, exactly ONE Oban job exists for that task, and no second Harness.Run gen_statem is spawned. Flunk on any unexpected error or on a second distinct run_id.
Test: after the first run reaches a terminal state, a fresh dispatch of the same {project, task_id} enqueues a NEW job (uniqueness does not leak past terminal).
mix precommit.full green.
out_of_scope: Any change to the recovery verbs (dispatch-reland / dispatch-rereview / dispatch-resume_failed) — they operate on settled runs, which terminal-state uniqueness already exempts.
Cross-project dedup — task IDs are per-project; the unique key MUST include project_name (tapakly/146 and ccxt_extract/146 are unrelated and must both be dispatchable).

Diagnosing the MCP transport 'Server unavailable' the dispatching client reported — that was a client-side MCP-session fault (the harness MCP HTTP server was verified healthy end-to-end), not a harness dispatch defect, and is not in scope here.
task_fingerprint-based dedup of semantically-identical-but-different-id tasks — the key is the explicit {project, task_id}, not content similarity.
task.body:
VERIFIED REPRO (2026-06-14, against the live node): ccxt_extract task 146 spawned TWO concurrent runs.
- run-1781433844647-abc2f80c — started first, progressed implement -> review, healthy (:reviewing).
- run-1781434039778-d9568c69 — started ~195s LATER for the SAME {ccxt_extract, 146}, ran 115s, then :cancelled.
The second run burned ~115s of cursor/composer tokens before someone caught it and killed it. (A third record, tapakly/146, is a DIFFERENT project — IDs are per-project, not a duplicate.)

Root cause (mechanical, mantra-clean): the dispatch path has no in-flight idempotency guard. Both enqueue sites build the Oban job via RunWorker.new(queue: ...) with NO `unique:` option (worker.ex ~84, batch.ex ~253), so a second dispatch of an already-live task enqueues a second job -> a second gen_statem -> a parallel duplicate run. This is a count/lookup ('does a non-terminal run for this {project, task_id} exist?'), not a judgment, so it belongs in harness code.

Fix direction (Oban-native, idiomatic): add a `unique:` spec on the RunWorker job keyed on the task-identifying args over non-terminal states (:available/:scheduled/:executing/:retryable, period: :infinity), centralized in one helper shared by both enqueue sites. The worker keeps the Oban job `executing` for the whole run lifetime (it spawns the gen_statem and threads its terminal state back), so :executing covers the implement->review window. On conflict, Oban.insert returns the existing job with conflict?: true — surface its run_id back to the caller so a retry gets the LIVE run's handle instead of an error-with-no-handle (this folds in the agent's secondary 'non-atomic dispatch+respond' complaint: there is nothing to make atomic — the retry simply returns the existing run). Terminal jobs don't block, so the recovery verbs and honest re-dispatch of a settled task are unaffected.

NOT a transport bug: the dispatching client also reported MCP 'Server unavailable', but the harness MCP HTTP server was verified healthy end-to-end (initialize -> initialized -> tools/call returning all 14 projects) — that was a client-side stale-session fault, out of scope (see out_of_scope). The only real harness defect is the missing dispatch dedup above.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1781435587994-2492d30b, cdd7fbace888b7cb65f2b1650734a62e2d50ee2c).

task.title: Dispatch idempotency: refuse a fresh run for a task with a settled, unlanded harness/<run-id> branch — return that run, steer to dispatch-reland
acceptance_criteria: Extend the dispatch ingestion guard (Harness.Run.Worker return_existing_run/3 path, around the live_run_id/2 lookup) so that when no live run and no non-terminal Oban job exist, it ALSO queries ResultStore.list_run_records(task_id:) for a SETTLED run with landed_sha == nil whose harness/<run-id> branch still exists (git branch existence check), and returns {:ok, <that_run_id>, <existing>} instead of spawning a duplicate.
The returned shape matches the in-flight guard's contract (caller gets the existing run_id, not a second run and not an error) and the path logs/steers the caller toward dispatch-reland.

A settled run that already LANDED (landed_sha set) or whose harness/<run-id> branch was deleted does NOT block a fresh dispatch — only an unlanded run WITH a retained branch does. This narrows task 286 AC#3 (which freely allowed re-dispatch of any terminal run) to exempt the recoverable-via-reland case.

Test (NEVER-HIDE-FAILURES): settle a run done/approved, leave landed_sha nil + branch present, dispatch the same {project, task_id} -> returns the SAME run_id, exactly zero new Oban jobs/gen_statems; then set landed_sha (or delete the branch) and assert a fresh dispatch DOES enqueue. Flunk on any unexpected error.
mix precommit.full green.
out_of_scope: The lander conflict-retain fix (already shipped separately) — that stops the AUTONOMOUS duplicate; this guard covers a manual/orchestrator dispatch-task of an already-blocked task.
task_fingerprint-based dedup of different-id-but-equivalent tasks — the key stays the explicit {project, task_id}.
Any change to dispatch-reland / dispatch-rereview / dispatch-resume_failed themselves.
task.body:
The in-flight idempotency guard (task 286) only dedups against LIVE runs + non-terminal Oban jobs (Harness.Run.Worker live_run_id/2, return_existing_run/3). A run that settled :done/approved and then had its auto-land BLOCKED on a conflict leaves a settled ResultStore LogRecord with landed_sha == nil and a retained harness/<run-id> branch — invisible to that guard. A subsequent explicit dispatch-task of the same {project, task_id} therefore spawns a DUPLICATE implementer run instead of returning the existing approved-but-unlanded run.

Defense-in-depth follow-up to the lander conflict-retain fix: the lander no longer re-dispatches on conflict (it retains the branch + marks the task blocked), so the autonomous duplicate is already closed. This task closes the remaining vector: a human/orchestrator re-dispatching the blocked task by hand. Extend the guard to detect the settled-unlanded-with-branch case and return the existing run_id, steering the caller to dispatch-reland (zero-token re-land) rather than redoing reviewed work — the "Recover, Don't Redo" contract enforced at the dispatch boundary.

task.title: Enrich the /harness/roadmap page beyond the 4-column rollup
acceptance_criteria: Each project row expands (or links) to show: next pending task (id + title), count of blocked tasks with their blocked_reason text, and the parallel-dispatchable set grouped by dep_layer (waves)
Roadmap data sourced through Harness.Roadmap / RoadmapSummary structured APIs, not new ad-hoc rmap shell-outs on the render path

No judgment computed in the LiveView — only rmap's own facts/fields are displayed (eff is fine to show; a bespoke importance score or routing pick is not)
Phoenix.LiveViewTest coverage: expanded drill-down renders next-task/blocked/wave data for a fixture project; empty + no-projects states explicit

Agent-routing / capability recommendations — those live on KPILive and the scout artifact, not here
The runs dashboard @roadmap assign — it stays as-is; this task only touches the standalone roadmap page
task.body:
Follow-up to the inline 4-column roadmap extraction (RoadmapLive at /harness/roadmap, shipped alongside this task's creation). That move was deliberately minimal: it relocated the per-project open/done/total/landed rollup table to its own navbar page, nothing more. This task makes the page a real planning surface.

Add per-project drill-down so an operator can answer "what's next / what's blocked / what's the parallel wave?" without leaving the dashboard. Source structured roadmap data via Harness.Roadmap (list/2, next_bundle/1) and RoadmapSummary rather than re-shelling rmap ad hoc. Keep the cold-path discipline: a slow tick (already 30s) or an explicit refresh, no PubSub source invented for it.

Mantra check: this page COUNTS and DISPLAYS roadmap facts (open counts, next task id, blocked reason text, dep-layer/wave grouping) — all mechanical reads of rmap's own output. It must NOT compute any judgment (no "which task is most important" scoring beyond rmap's own eff, no agent-routing recommendation rendered here — that's KPILive/scout territory). Display rmap's computed fields; never recompute meaning from them.

task.title: Blocking multi-run await: dispatch-await_runs MCP tool
acceptance_criteria: A new dispatch-await_runs MCP tool accepts a list of run_ids + timeout_ms and blocks until every run settles or the timeout expires
Returns a compact per-run summary list (run_id, state, reason, review_verdict) — the same summary shape dispatch-await returns for one run
On timeout it returns structured per-run summaries distinguishing settled from still-running, and never wedges the tool call (mirrors dispatch-await's :timed_out contract)
Resolves each run across all lifecycle stages (live / queued Oban job / settled record) via the existing dispatch-status resolution path
Tests cover: all-settle-before-timeout, partial-timeout, and an unknown run_id in the list; descripex api()/MCP annotation exposes the tool
out_of_scope: Push/callback delivery to the driver (the push-sink spike) — this is pull-only: the caller holds one blocking connection
New run state or notification sinks
task.body:
The gap the dogfooding orchestrator hits: dispatch-await blocks on exactly ONE task it dispatches itself. An orchestrator that already fired N runs (dispatch-task x N, or dispatch-bundle) has run_ids in hand and must poll each via dispatch-status in a loop — there is no single call that says "block until these all finish."

Add dispatch-await_runs([run_id], timeout_ms): a blocking MCP tool that awaits settlement of an arbitrary set of already-started runs and returns their compact summaries together. Pure mechanics, mantra-clean — it COUNTS lifecycle state (settled? reason? verdict?), it judges nothing. The dispatch-status tool already resolves a run across live / queued / settled stages; this reuses that resolution and just waits on it for a set. On timeout, return what's settled plus a still-running marker for the rest (the runs keep going, observable later) — same non-wedging contract as dispatch-await's :timed_out.

Discovered 2026-06-15 dispatching ccxt-distill tasks 2/3/19: three run_ids, three separate dispatch-status polls per check. One await over the set is the 80/20 fix.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1781490184500-8c5d3b99, 55929c4cdc039f255b7c5868d889893c24035156).

task.title: Spike: out-of-band push sink so a settled run wakes the orchestrator
acceptance_criteria: A decision doc (concept doc or docs/) names the chosen push transport and the rejected alternatives with rationale
The doc decides whether to add a per-run :settled witness event beside the existing :land/:blocked events (the orchestrator-wakeup case needs settle, not just land)
The doc sketches the reference Sink impl (delivery channel, payload shape, failure isolation) so the follow-up build task is mechanical
A follow-up build task is filed (or this task's out-of-scope names it) for the actual sink implementation
out_of_scope: Building the full push sink — this is a decision spike: pick the transport + payload, sketch the impl, file the build task
Shipping a production sink
task.body:
Harness.Notification already fans witness events (land / blocked / red-post-merge) to configured sinks (lib/harness/notification/, read-only by construction). Two gaps for the "harness tells me when my run is done" feature:

1. No sink reaches the DRIVING orchestrator session. A sink writes to a configured channel (CommandSink), but an MCP/chat driver has no inbound channel — it must poll. The transport is undecided: webhook to a local listener the driver tails, an OS notifier (terminal-notifier / notify-send), a file-drop the CLI watches, or extending CommandSink. Each trades immediacy vs. setup vs. survives-driver-restart.
2. Events fire on land/blocked only. The orchestrator-wakeup case wants notification on EVERY run settle (approve, reject, failed, timed_out) — so this may need a new :settled event alongside the existing land/blocked ones.

This is the nicer-but-bigger half of the orchestrator-feedback pair (the pull-only multi-run await is the sibling). Decide the channel + payload + whether to add :settled, sketch the Sink, file the build. Don't ship a production sink in the spike.

task.title: Model catalog card: membership multi-select (probed universe + operator subset) replacing the flat removable list
acceptance_criteria: The Model catalog card renders each agent's models as a TOGGLE/CHECKBOX membership list (built from the existing `.toggle`/`.pill` design-token vocabulary — NOT a native `<select multiple>`), where the CLI-probed catalog is the read-only UNIVERSE and the operator toggles which ids are SELECTED into the dropdown-feeding set. Clicking a model adds/removes membership in one interaction; no per-row Add-form + N Remove-buttons.

A per-agent filter/search input narrows the universe so a large probed list (cursor lists many models) stays usable; filtering is client-or-server but must not lose unselected-but-filtered selections.

ModelAvailability distinguishes the probed universe from the operator-selected subset: `catalog/1` (the source feeding the Agent/Reviewer model dropdowns) returns the SELECTED subset; a new query exposes the full universe (probed ∪ operator-added) for the card to render with selected-state. `refresh_catalog` no longer flattens the probe into one indistinguishable removable static list.
Free-text ADD remains as a fallback for non-probeable agents (no CLI universe) and for ids the probe does not report — a typed id becomes both universe-member and selected.

Tests: ModelAvailability universe-vs-selected round-trip (toggle membership, refresh merges into universe not selection, selected survives a refresh); settings_components render test for the membership list + filter; settings_live event test for toggle-membership and free-text add.
out_of_scope: Removing the catalog management surface entirely (the autocomplete-only 'option C' alternative) — this task keeps an explicit curation surface, just as a membership UI.
Changing the {agent,model} BLOCK semantics (operator/failure blocks) — this is catalog membership, not availability blocking.
Validating model ids against --list-models output (ids are free-text/unvalidated; they churn).
task.body:
The Model catalog card (Harness.Dashboard.SettingsComponents.model_catalog_card)
renders every model id per agent as a `<pill> + Remove` form. Because
ModelAvailability.refresh_catalog MERGES the CLI probe into the operator static
catalog and persists it, a single refresh dumps the entire CLI model list (dozens
of ids for e.g. cursor) into the removable static set — so the card shows a bulk
import with per-item curation UI meant for a handful of hand-picked ids. Visually a
wall of pill+button rows; conceptually it conflates two sources.

DECISION (2026-06-15, with the repo owner): redesign as a MEMBERSHIP MULTI-SELECT.
The probed CLI list is the read-only UNIVERSE (source of truth for what an agent
can run); the operator toggles which ids are SELECTED into the curated subset that
actually feeds the Agent models / Reviewer models dropdowns. Add+remove collapse
into one click; a filter box tames large universes. This is option B
(provenance-aware: universe vs selected) realized as a membership UI rather than two
stacked lists. Build it from the existing `.toggle`/`.pill` tokens — NOT a native
`<select multiple>` (unstyleable, ugly). Keep the free-text ADD as the fallback for
non-probeable agents and ids the probe omits.

Mantra-clean: membership is a COUNTED FACT (id ∈ selected?), not a judgment — no
scoring/weighting of models, just set toggling. The dropdowns read the selected
set; the card reads the universe with selected-state overlaid.

Context: settings page was just refactored into section tabs (Autonomy/Agents/
Models/Projects/Advanced); this card lives under the Models tab. Select/input chrome
was just unified (custom caret, no native dropdown) — match it. No daisyUI/Tailwind
in this repo; styling is selector-explicit in tokens.ex.

task.title: Collision-aware dispatch: serialize ready-set tasks with overlapping write-sets instead of fanning them out
acceptance_criteria: dispatch-bundle / parallel dispatch computes (touches union files_to_modify) per task and refuses-or-serializes any subset whose write-sets intersect — colliding tasks dispatch as a chain (await land, then next), only disjoint write-sets fan out concurrently
The collision check is independent of the depends_on graph: tasks that share a write target but have no dep edge are still detected as colliding
A log/notification line names which tasks were serialized and on which shared files (no silent reordering)
Regression test: a 3-task ready set all listing src/x in their write-set produces a serial dispatch plan, not a parallel wave
Documented in the driver SKILL + harness-workflow: the dispatcher honors write-set collisions, callers no longer hand-dedupe
out_of_scope: Resolving conflicts that still occur (that is the resolver's job — separate task)
Inferring write-sets from task body when touches/files_to_modify are unset — the fields are the contract
task.body:
Root cause of the 2026-06-15 ccxt-distill 2/3/19 land pile-up. Tasks 2, 3, 19 were dispatched in parallel because their depends_on graph said independent (all only depended on task 1) — but all three WROTE THE SAME FILES (src/cli.ts, test/cli.test.ts, CHANGELOG.md), each registering a CLI subcommand in the same function. Task 3 landed clean; 19 and 2 then hit real same-line content conflicts rebasing onto it, the merge-train blocked both, and recovery needed manual three-way merges + full re-verify per branch (runs run-1781478762049 / ...763383).

rmap.md already documents the collision rule — two tasks conflict iff (touches union files_to_modify) intersect — but it's a CONSUMER-side dedupe that nothing enforced at dispatch time. Move it into the dispatcher: before fanning out a ready set / bundle, partition by write-set overlap and serialize the colliding groups (dispatch one, await its land, dispatch the next so it rebases onto landed work — exactly what dodges the conflict). The concurrency-cap bump during the incident made it worse: at cap=1 the three would have landed serially and conflict-free; raising the cap turned a safe serial chain into a collision. Serialization for file-coupled tasks is a feature, not a limit.

Mantra-clean: this is COUNTING file-set intersection (mechanical), not judging conflict content.

task.title: MCP transport 30s GenServer.call ceiling defeats every blocking dispatch tool
acceptance_criteria: A dispatch-await_runs / dispatch-await call that blocks server-side longer than 30s completes and returns its summary instead of failing the MCP request with session_call_failed {:timeout, {GenServer, :call, ..., 30000}}
The fix raises or removes the transport-layer GenServer.call timeout for blocking tool requests so it tracks the tool's own timeout_ms (default 30 min), not a hardcoded 30s
dispatch-await, dispatch-await_runs, and dispatch-compare (all blocking) verified to hold a >30s wait over /harness/mcp without transport timeout
A regression test exercises a blocking tool whose server-side wait exceeds the old 30s ceiling (synthetic slow tool or a real run awaited past 30s)
out_of_scope: Push/callback delivery to the driver (Task 290 push-sink spike) - this is the pull/blocking path only
Changing the blocking tools' own timeout_ms semantics or default values
task.body:
Observed 2026-06-15 calling dispatch-await_runs over MCP to await two in-flight ccxt-distill runs (tasks 4/5). The tool blocked server-side as designed, but the request failed at the transport layer:

  MCP transport event: session_call_failed
  reason: {:timeout, {GenServer, :call, [#PID, {:mcp_request, %{"name" => "dispatch-await_runs", ...}}, 30000]}}

The anubis StreamableHTTP transport handles each tools/call via a GenServer.call with a hardcoded 30_000ms timeout. Any blocking tool that waits longer than 30s exceeds this ceiling and the MCP request dies, even though the tool's own timeout_ms is 30 min and the run keeps going. This silently defeats the entire purpose of the blocking-await design:

  - dispatch-await (Task ~ dispatch__await): blocks on one run
  - dispatch-await_runs (Task 289): blocks on a set of runs
  - dispatch-compare: blocks until all adapters settle

All three are unusable over MCP for any wait > 30s - i.e. essentially always, since implement->review->land cycles take minutes. The orchestrator is forced back to dispatch-status poll loops, which is exactly what 289 was filed to eliminate.

Investigation paths: the GenServer.call timeout lives in anubis_mcp's StreamableHTTP transport request dispatch (deps/anubis_mcp). Options: (a) configure/override the transport's call timeout for the harness MCP child spec; (b) make blocking tools return a progress/streaming response instead of holding one synchronous call; (c) cap harness blocking tools below 30s and document the ceiling (worst option - reintroduces polling). Prefer (a) if anubis exposes the timeout, else upstream it.

Discovered while dogfooding ccxt-distill dispatch; pairs with Task 289 (the tool that exposed the ceiling) and Task 290 (push transport, the async alternative).

task.title: Lander resolver still fails 5/5 trivial additive CHANGELOG keep-both conflicts post-293; eliminate the additive-file conflict class mechanically
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce/confirm: in a parallel wave where N runs each append a CHANGELOG.md `### Added` bullet, the first lands clean and the rest auto-land-block with a CHANGELOG-only conflict the auto-resolver leaves :conflict_retained — despite resolver.ex:154-157 already instructing KEEP-BOTH for additive edits (added by Task 293).

Witness resolver attempts: record (best-effort, mantra-clean — count facts, not verdicts) whether the resolver agent was spawned, whether it left markers, or whether selection/spawn failed, so a :conflict_retained is diagnosable WITHOUT hand-inspecting the retained branch (resolver output is not persisted today — resolver.ex:33).

Eliminate the additive-file conflict class MECHANICALLY rather than via the agent: a union-merge path for provably-append-only files (e.g. a `merge=union` gitattributes driver applied in the landing worktree, or `git merge-file --union`) so CHANGELOG.md (and similar append-only artifacts) never reach the resolver. Union of an append-only changelog is counting/mechanics, not judgment — keep it in code.

The agent resolver stays for GENUINE same-region semantic conflicts (the Task 189/293 same-function/same-list case); the mechanical union path is tried first for the configured additive-file set and short-circuits the resolver on success.

Covered by lander/resilience tests: a wave fixture with N additive CHANGELOG appends lands all N with zero manual salvage; a genuine same-region conflict still routes to the resolver then block-on-failure.
CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased].
task.body:
Dogfooding evidence, 2026-06-15 (ccxt-distill Phase 5 domain wave). Tasks 9-14 dispatched in parallel under concurrency_cap=6 (each task designed disjoint-source-file per its PARALLEL-SAFETY CONTRACT: only its own src/extract/domains/<name>.ts + test, registered via Task 7 auto-discovery, no shared cli.ts/pipeline.ts edit). The disjoint-source design worked — the ONLY shared file was CHANGELOG.md.

Result: task 14 landed clean (first to land); tasks 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 ALL auto-land-blocked with a conflict on CHANGELOG.md ONLY. Every conflict was a trivial diff3 additive append (HEAD = the previously-landed task's `### Added` bullet; incoming = this task's bullet; resolution = keep both). The post-293 resolver — which carries explicit "Default to KEEPING BOTH sides when the changes are additive" guidance (resolver.ex:154-157) plus authoritative conflict excerpts (Task 293's stated fix) — STILL left all 5 :conflict_retained.

Manual salvage (this session): a 5-line keep-both awk on CHANGELOG.md resolved every one; dispatch-reland then ff-pushed clean. Tasks 11/12/13 each had TWO CHANGELOG-touching commits (delivery + reviewer-fixes), so each needed two keep-both steps — still all trivial. 5 manual salvages for one wave.

So the resolver fails on the SIMPLEST possible additive conflict despite being explicitly instructed to keep-both. Two gaps:

1. NOT DIAGNOSABLE: resolver output isn't persisted (resolver.ex:33), so we can't tell from the record whether the resolver agent ran-and-left-markers, declined, or was never spawned (selection/cross-family-availability failure → :conflict_retained without the agent ever running). Add minimal witnessing.

2. WRONG TOOL for additive files: a CHANGELOG append conflict is not a judgment call — `git merge=union` / `git merge-file --union` resolves it deterministically. Per the harness mantra (count facts in code; write meaning with an AI), union-merging an append-only changelog is mechanics, NOT judgment, so it belongs in code, not in an agent prompt. A union-merge driver for a configured additive-file set (CHANGELOG.md by default) applied in the landing worktree would eliminate this entire recurring salvage class with zero agent involvement, leaving the agent resolver for genuine same-region semantic conflicts (the Task 189/293 same-function case).

Follow-up to the now-done Task 293 (which added the keep-both PROMPT guidance but, per this evidence, did not make the additive case reliable). Cross-ref Task 189 (resolver origin), Task 293 (prompt-context fix).

2026-06-15 (why-did-harness-never-hit-this verification): checked harness's own repo — it has NO .gitattributes and `git check-attr merge CHANGELOG.md` = unspecified, i.e. NO `merge=union` anywhere in the portfolio. harness avoided this class for two NON-mechanical reasons, neither of which generalizes: (1) it was never dogfooded as a wide parallel wave (the collision is purely N-branches-off-one-base appending the same region → N-1 guaranteed conflicts in ANY repo; ccxt-distill's cap=6 wave 9-14 was the first such wave in the whole portfolio), and (2) it shifts much CHANGELOG hygiene to the SERIAL post-merge audit stage (audit.ex:429 "CHANGELOG gaps"; ~half of recent CHANGELOG touches are `audit(...)` commits on the already-merged trunk, which can never conflict). But implementers DO also write CHANGELOG (canonical.md:10 "CHANGELOG edits inside the worktree are yours"; ~half of touches are deliveries) — so the serial-audit cushion only softens, it does not prevent: even cap=1, the post-merge audit worker is a SECOND committer that moves origin/<target> while the next run is in flight, which is exactly how ccxt-distill task 8 hit a CHANGELOG/test-file conflict under strict serial cap=1. CONCLUSION: the union-merge driver proposed above is genuinely net-new (no existing harness mechanism does this) and is the only fix that covers BOTH the parallel-wave AND the serial audit-race cases. Recommend also dropping a `CHANGELOG.md merge=union` .gitattributes into target repos (ccxt-distill first) as the cheap immediate mitigation, independent of the in-harness driver work here.

acceptance_criteria: Reproduce FIRST before fixing: determine whether the :undef is a hot-code-reload race (a recompile/restart landed while a run's gen_statem was mid-:reviewing) or a genuine missing/undefined path. All transcript_chunk-path callees (handle_common/4 :info clause, parse_chunk/2, maybe_sample_in_run_discernment/2, rearm_running_idle/3, rearm_reviewing_idle/3) ARE defined and 4 prior runs (17/20/18/21) passed cleanly through :reviewing on the same code — so the reload-race hypothesis is primary.

If reload-race: document it as an operational hazard (don't recompile/restart the node with runs in flight) and, if cheap, make the Run.Worker treat a settled-but-:undef-crashed run as recoverable rather than cancelling the Oban job + resetting the task to pending with no record. If genuine gap: add the missing clause + a regression test that feeds a transcript_chunk into :reviewing and asserts no crash.

Either way: a run that crashes with :run_crashed should persist a minimal ResultStore record (it left NONE here — only the Oban job's errors array held the trace), so the failure is diagnosable without digging into oban_jobs.
task.body:
Observed 2026-06-15 dogfooding ccxt-distill task 23 (grok/grok-build). Run run-1781507309330-a1cdd28e: implementer finished, run entered :reviewing, then crashed:

  {:cancel, {:run_crashed, {:undef, [{Harness.Run, :reviewing, [:info, {:transcript_chunk, "<grok json>"}, <data>]}]}}}

Oban job 1510 (queue project_ccxt-distill) -> state "cancelled" after attempt 1; harness reset task 23 to pending (commit "roadmap: task 23 -> pending", author harness). NO ResultStore record was written (result_store-list_run_records empty for the run_id) — the only trace is oban_jobs.errors. An orphan worktree was left at ~/_DATA/worktrees/.harness/ccxt-distill/run-1781507309330-a1cdd28e (cleaned manually this session).

Context that makes reload-race the leading hypothesis: this happened right after a cluster of restarts/recompiles (tasks 294 witness-event, 297 lander union-merge, 298 KPI page all landing + a /mcp HTTP-500 then reconnect). The transcript_chunk that triggered it carried grok's own failed `npx tsx -e ... runPipeline` command (Top-level await not supported with cjs) — that's transcript noise, not the cause; the cause is the :undef on the state callback.

:undef on a defined gen_statem state function is the classic signature of calling into a module mid-purge/reload, not a function_clause miss. So: reproduce under controlled reload before treating it as a state-machine bug. Cross-ref the agent-gate mantra — a real fix is mechanical substrate hardening (record-on-crash, reload safety), not judgment.

Filed per dogfooding mandate (harness bugs found while dogfooding -> rmap tasks). Re-dispatch of task 23 proceeds separately.

task.title: list_available_models conflates 'no catalog' with 'probed-but-none-selected' — distinguish the two diagnostic states
acceptance_criteria: list_available_models/2 returns THREE distinguishable shapes instead of two: (a) models present -> {:ok, %{catalog_status: "available", models: [...]}}; (b) a probed/declared universe EXISTS but the operator-selected subset is empty -> {:ok, %{catalog_status: "probed_none_selected", models: [], universe_count: N}}; (c) no universe at all (probe failed / nothing declared / no builtin) -> {:ok, %{catalog_status: "unavailable", models: []}}. The (b) vs (c) split is decided by consulting catalog_universe/1: non-empty universe + empty selection = probed_none_selected; empty universe = unavailable.

Backward-compat: the existing catalog_unavailable boolean key stays present and is true for BOTH (b) and (c) so current callers do not break; catalog_status is the new precise field. Update the api() returns description to document all three statuses.

No change to list_available/1 (the dispatch-gate read path), to catalog/1 (Task 291 deliberately returns the SELECTED subset — do NOT revert that), or to the block/availability semantics. This is a DIAGNOSTIC-LABEL fix at the MCP boundary only.

Tests in test/harness/model_availability_test.exs cover all three states: available (a model selected into static), probed_none_selected (a non-empty universe via a seeded probe cache with empty static selection -> universe_count > 0, status probed_none_selected), and unavailable (an agent with no builtin, no static, no probe cache).
mix precommit green on the touched files
out_of_scope: Reverting Task 291's universe-vs-selected split (catalog/1 must keep returning the selected subset)
Auto-selecting / falling back to the probed universe in list_available (that would undo 291 and the operator-curation gate)
Changing the settings Model-catalog UI card (that is Task 291, done)
task.body:
Reported 2026-06-15 via dogfooding: model_availability-list_available_models("cursor") returns {:ok, %{catalog_unavailable: true, models: []}} even though the node holds a FULLY PROBED 150-model cursor catalog (:model_catalogs, fetched_at today). The diagnostic is misleading: "unavailable" reads as "probe failed / CLI absent / no catalog", but the real state is "catalog probed, operator has selected zero models into the static subset".

Verified live: :model_catalog_static = :not_found (no selection persisted for ANY agent), cursor catalog_universe = 150 models all selected?: false, list_available(:cursor) = {:error, :catalog_unavailable}. The probe-cache key (:model_catalogs) and the read key (:model_catalog_static) are correctly disjoint by Task 291's design (catalog/1 returns the operator-SELECTED subset); the operator simply never toggled any cursor model in /harness/settings. That selection gate is intended. What is NOT intended is the response collapsing "no universe" and "universe-but-nothing-selected" into the same catalog_unavailable: true — the caller cannot tell "go select some models" from "the CLI probe is broken / re-probe".

Fix is diagnostic-only at the MCP boundary (list_available_models/2, lib/harness/model_availability.ex ~L212): when list_available returns :catalog_unavailable, consult catalog_universe/1 to emit catalog_status "probed_none_selected" (universe non-empty) vs "unavailable" (universe empty), keeping the legacy catalog_unavailable boolean for back-compat. Do not touch the dispatch gate, catalog/1, or the selection model.

Promoting exograph to a runtime dep for prod-release support -- additive, deferred; the Code.ensure_loaded? guard makes this a later non-breaking change
The dashboard project-structure explorer UI -- Task 303
Any judgment/score/verdict derived from the structural facts -- agents interpret meaning; CodeSearch only retrieves facts (THE MANTRA)
task.body:
Idea origin: this session's exograph investigation (exograph kept as a dev/test structural-search dep, commit f525368). Goal: let harness "see inside" the Elixir projects it federates -- give the reviewer/audit agents (and, via Task 303, the operator) structural queries grep cannot do: cross-module caller blast-radius for a changed signature, callees, definitions-by-name, and ex_dna duplicate detection.

Architecture decided 2026-06-16 (vetoable): in-process, dev/test-gated. runtime:false only skips app-start + release inclusion -- in the dev node (iex -S mix, MIX_ENV=dev) exograph's modules ARE compiled and callable. So CodeSearch calls Exograph.{index,search_callers,search_callees,search_definitions} directly, guarded by Code.ensure_loaded?(Exograph) exactly like Harness.Dashboard.Endpoint guards Bandit. It starts the QuackDB.Server + Exograph.DuckDBRepo itself (the app is not auto-started) and caches a DuckDB file per project under ~/.harness. No runtime-dep promotion needed; prod-release support is a deferred additive change.

Mantra-clean by construction: CodeSearch is pure fact-retrieval (it COUNTS/LOCATES defs, callers, call-edges, duplicates) and never computes meaning -- the reviewer/audit agent reads the facts and writes the judgment. Elixir-only is a hard boundary (exograph indexes Elixir AST via ExAST); other registered project languages are skipped with a visible log, never silently faked.

Future (not in scope, noted for later): cross-project / hex-corpus precedent queries ("is this pattern used elsewhere?") to serve the library-first/precedent rule -- an additive extension once the per-project core lands.

task.title: Cron poller: suppress re-dispatch of a task whose adapter is unavailable (no churn loop)
acceptance_criteria: When a cron-dispatched run for task T fails to START because its resolved adapter/model is unavailable ({:start_run_failed, {:no_available_agent, _}} → mechanical_retry_exhausted → job cancelled), the next poll tick does NOT immediately re-dispatch T against the same unavailable adapter

Suppression keys off the existing ModelAvailability/AgentRegistry availability fact (Task 16) — a mechanical 'is this adapter available right now' check, NOT a new judgment/scoring branch in harness code

A task suppressed only because its adapter is unavailable becomes dispatchable again automatically once the adapter is available (no manual unblock needed); availability is the gate, not a sticky blocklist
The churn is observable-then-gone: a log/witness line names the suppressed (task, adapter, reason) so the operator sees why a ready task isn't dispatching
Tests: a poll tick with an unavailable adapter for a ready task enqueues nothing and logs the suppression; once the adapter is marked available the same task dispatches
out_of_scope: Marking a quota-exhausted/unavailable agent unavailable in the first place — that detection is Task 16; this task only consumes the availability fact at poll time

In-run retry/backoff classification of a run that already STARTED then failed — that is Harness.Run.RetryPolicy (Tasks 10/41); this is the poller declining to (re-)START when the adapter can't run at all
Any change to dispatch-await/dispatch-task interactive paths
task.body:
Observed 2026-06-16: task 130/ccxt_client was re-enqueued by the cron poller every ~3 min (Oban jobs 1597-1600), each run cancelling ~22s later with no_available_agent for Codex. Codex was unavailable so the run never started; mechanical retry (5 attempts) exhausted, the Oban job cancelled, the task reverted to pending, and the next cron tick re-selected it — a tight re-dispatch loop with no agent-unavailable suppression at the poller. The existing run_in_flight? guard does not help: a cancelled job is terminal (not in-flight), so the task is legitimately ready again every tick.

The fix is mechanical, not judgment: before enqueuing a ready task whose resolved adapter/model is currently unavailable (the same availability fact Task 16 computes), the poller declines and logs/witnesses the suppression — and resumes dispatching automatically once the adapter is available. No new scoring or is-this-worth-retrying classifier. Discovered while fixing the orthogonal dispatch-await duplicate-dispatch hole.

task.title: Triage + persist .sobelow-skips for the full outstanding sobelow finding set (incl. 3 high-confidence binary_to_term)
acceptance_criteria: Review every outstanding `mix sobelow` finding (project-wide: 67 low + 3 high as of audit d3d6ac3) and classify each as genuine-fix vs false-positive.

The 3 high-confidence `Misc.BinToTerm` findings (settings_store/postgres.ex:58, result_store/postgres.ex:594, project_registry/persistence.ex:148) are explicitly assessed: confirm the deserialized binary originates only from harness's own Postgres writes (term_to_binary round-trip, trusted) before skipping; if any path can ingest external bytes, fix it.

Extend the committed `.sobelow-skips` (currently only the 3 reviewed-FP files from audit d3d6ac3: code_search.ex, file_sink.ex, lander/resolver.ex) to cover the remaining confirmed false positives, hash-pinned; commit it.
`mix sobelow --skip` is clean (0/0) and the result is durable across sessions (no inline comments, which this host's hook ignores).
out_of_scope: Any functional change to the flagged modules beyond a genuine vuln fix surfaced during triage.
task.body:
Filed by the post-merge audit of the d3d6ac3 range (run run-1781587226238-3042a824).

That audit hit the local precommit sobelow gate (no `.sobelow-skips` was ever tracked in the repo). To land its docs-only commit it added a MINIMAL `.sobelow-skips` covering only the 3 files the hook's blocking run flagged -- code_search.ex (SQL.Query on the local `query/3` helper; Traversal on the fixed ~/.harness index dir; BinToAtom on controlled module names), notification/file_sink.ex (Traversal on operator-configured notification path), and lander/resolver.ex (Traversal on a harness-controlled worktree path) -- all confirmed false positives.

But a project-wide `mix sobelow` reports 67 low + 3 HIGH-confidence findings. The 3 high-confidence ones are `Misc.BinToTerm: Unsafe binary_to_term` in the Postgres-backed stores (settings_store, result_store, project_registry) -- the standard Ecto trusted-DB term serialization pattern, almost certainly FP, but high-confidence binary_to_term deserves an explicit human confirm-the-source pass before suppression rather than a rushed `--mark-skip-all`. The audit deliberately did NOT blanket-skip these (the host CLAUDE.md warns `--mark-skip-all` can bury a real finding). This task does the full triage and persists the complete skip file so the local gate stops blocking unrelated commits.
task.implemented: Triaged the full outstanding set (~170 findings). The 3 high-confidence Misc.BinToTerm sites (settings_store/postgres.ex:58, result_store/postgres.ex:594, project_registry/persistence.ex:148) confirmed FP: each binary_to_term deserializes a harness-owned DB blob written by the same store's term_to_binary, guarded by a rescue. Persisted the complete .sobelow-skips; mix sobelow --skip is clean (0/0).

task.title: Decide whether to track .sobelow-skips (un-gitignore) for a durable suppression record
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded: keep .sobelow-skips gitignored (per-worktree regeneration, status quo) OR un-gitignore it (remove /.sobelow-skips from .gitignore:36) and commit the hash-based suppression record so CI / fresh worktrees / other devs do not re-flag
If tracked: a committed .sobelow-skips that makes `mix sobelow --skip --format compact` report zero findings, regenerated against current HEAD
out_of_scope: Re-triaging the findings themselves -- already done in audit(d3d6ac3): the sole genuine finding (code_search.ex:339 atom leak) was fixed there; every remaining finding is an author-verified false positive (argv-list System.cmd, harness-owned binary_to_term DB blobs, own-INSERT String.to_atom, operator/worktree-controlled File.* paths)
task.body:
Filed by audit(d3d6ac3) 2026-06-16. The host commit hook honors only the hash-based .sobelow-skips file (not the inline `# sobelow_skip` comments the authors wrote), and this repo gitignores /.sobelow-skips (.gitignore:36), so the full-project Sobelow scan (~60 author-verified false positives) trips EVERY commit -- including doc-only ones -- and a freshly-created worktree must regenerate the skip file once before it can commit.

The audit fixed the one genuine finding (code_search.ex:339: dynamic Ecto repo named with a monotonic unique_integer minted a permanently-retained atom per query; changed to name: nil since the repo is pid-referenced) and generated .sobelow-skips locally to unblock its own commit, but did NOT override the deliberate .gitignore decision by force-committing it.

Remaining decision (project policy, hence assignee=human): the host convention says track .sobelow-skips as the shared suppression record; this repo's .gitignore says don't. Pick one. If tracking: drop the .gitignore line and commit a current .sobelow-skips. If keeping it ignored: accept the once-per-worktree regeneration and close.
task.implemented: Decision: track .sobelow-skips. Removed /.sobelow-skips from .gitignore and committed the hash-pinned baseline regenerated against HEAD; mix sobelow --skip reports 0/0.

task.title: CodeSearch: reuse a long-lived DuckDB server + dynamic repo instead of booting/tearing-down per query (project explorer ~800ms -> sub-150ms)
acceptance_criteria: Eliminate the per-query cold start in Harness.CodeSearch.query/3's lifecycle (lib/harness/code_search.ex with_repo/with_index): today every definitions/callers/callees/duplicates call runs start_app(:ecto_sql)+start_app(:quackdb), starts a fresh QuackDB.Server + Exograph.DuckDBRepo dynamic repo, opens the index, then stop_pid tears it all down. Replace with a long-lived, supervised server+repo reused across queries so a warm query pays no process boot/teardown.

Implementation approach is the implementer's call (a supervised Harness.CodeSearch.Server GenServer owning the QuackDB.Server + dynamic repo per index_path is the expected shape), but it MUST: (a) stay dev/test-gated exactly as today behind Code.ensure_loaded?(Exograph)/Code.ensure_loaded?(QuackDB.Server) -- exograph absent (prod release) or non-Elixir project is still a clearly-logged graceful no-op, never a crash, and the supervised child must not crash boot when exograph is unavailable; (b) preserve existing staleness semantics (re-index when source mtime is newer than the index); (c) be safe under concurrent dashboard requests -- a single DuckDB dynamic repo/connection is not concurrently safe, so serialize or pool access (the GenServer mailbox is a natural serialization point).

Measurable latency win: a warm /harness/projects/:name/explore navigation with a fresh index drops from ~800ms server render to well under 150ms; record the before/after numbers in the implemented field. First-ever cold load may still pay the one-time index build -- that is acceptable and out of scope to eliminate.

Mantra-clean and non-breaking: still pure fact-retrieval (no score/verdict/route added); the returned fact map shape (file,line,kind,module,name,arity) is unchanged; Task 302's CodeSearch tests and Task 303's ProjectExplorer LiveView tests stay green with no assertion changes.

Tests: assert the server/repo is reused across successive queries (e.g. the server pid / repo is stable across two back-to-back queries rather than booted twice), that a stale index still triggers re-index, and that the exograph-absent and non-Elixir guard paths still no-op with flunk on any unexpected outcome (never a silent skip). Coverage stays >= 80% on lib/harness/code_search.ex and any new server module.
out_of_scope: Promoting exograph to a runtime/prod-release dep -- still deferred and additive; the Code.ensure_loaded? guard keeps this a later non-breaking change
Any change to the CodeSearch fact API shape or the explorer UI -- Tasks 302/303 own those; this is purely the index/repo lifecycle
The /harness/projects -> /harness/projects/explore index redirect (no index alias for the bare projects segment) -- trivial one-line router convenience, handled inline, not part of this task
task.body:
Discovered 2026-06-16 while timing the project explorer in the browser: a warm /harness/projects/:name/explore navigation takes ~814ms TTFB. Mount itself is cheap (ProjectRegistry.list()); the entire cost is handle_params -> load_elixir_project -> Harness.CodeSearch.definitions/1.

Harness.CodeSearch.query/3 (lib/harness/code_search.ex:175) wraps every query in with_repo/2 (line 273), which on EACH call does: start_app(:ecto_sql), start_app(:quackdb), start_server(index_path) (boots a fresh QuackDB/DuckDB server process), start_repo (starts a dynamic Exograph.DuckDBRepo), runs the query, then tears the whole thing down via stop_pid in the after-block. So every explorer navigation -- and every select_project push_patch -- pays a full cold DuckDB-process boot + dynamic-repo start + teardown. There is no pooling or memoization across requests. If the index is also stale, refresh_index re-parses all source on top.

Fix: hold a long-lived, supervised server+repo and reuse it across queries instead of boot-query-teardown per request. The DuckDB connection isn't concurrently safe, so access must be serialized/pooled (a GenServer is the natural fit). Keep the existing dev/test gating (Code.ensure_loaded?(Exograph), mirroring the Bandit guard) and the source-mtime staleness check intact.

Lineage: Task 302 built Harness.CodeSearch (the index lifecycle + query API), Task 303 the ProjectExplorer LiveView, Task 304 the navbar link. This task makes that surface usable interactively by removing the per-request spin-up tax -- otherwise the whole exograph investment reads as sluggish.

Routing: codex/gpt-5.5 (OTP+Ecto lifecycle work; cursor-Opus is operator-blocked on monthly budget until 2026-07-05).
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1781589690215-f48d97d2, b400c1a9c1bbc07fa0ed8625cbef1b883481845e).

task.body:
GAP (found 2026-06-16): warm_paths shipped on %Harness.Project{} + the projects.warm_paths Postgres column (Task 252), but NEITHER operator-authoring surface can set it:
- MCP dispatch-register_project (Harness.Dispatch.register_project/7, dispatch.ex:855) has no warm_paths param.
- Dashboard register/edit form (settings_live.ex project_attrs/1) only PRESERVES existing warm_paths via preserved_project_attrs/1 (line ~628) — no input field, no parse.

So the only way to author warm_paths is Harness.ProjectRegistry.upsert/1 from IEx/tidewave or priv/repo/seeds.exs. Task 284 explicitly closed "the last per-project config surface holes" but left this one. Close it: add the param to the MCP tool and a field to the dashboard form, both routing through the existing ProjectRegistry.upsert path (Postgres-is-truth already works — only the authoring entry points are missing).

Reviewer approved, no fixes.

task.title: dispatch-await attach-to-in-flight-run wedges the MCP transport instead of returning the structured :timed_out summary (and poisons subsequent dispatch-status/list_runs calls)
acceptance_criteria: REPRO (observed 2026-06-16, ccxt-distill task 47, run-1781604067447-043d5fac dispatched on codex/gpt-5.5): with a run already in flight, calling mcp__harness__dispatch-await {task: '47', project_name: 'ccxt-distill', timeout_ms: 1_800_000} returns a transport-level 'The operation timed out.' error after the MCP client's own (~60s) deadline — NOT the documented structured :timed_out summary. The tool doc promises 'on timeout it returns a structured :timed_out summary ... never a wedged tool call'; the attach path violates that promise.

SECONDARY SYMPTOM: after that await call, the immediately-following mcp__harness__dispatch-status {run_id} and mcp__harness__supervisor-list_runs calls ALSO timed out (3x), while the BEAM (phx.server pid alive) and the dispatched codex exec process were both healthy and the run was genuinely still running. So the wedged await appears to block/serialize the MCP request handler (or hold a GenServer call) such that subsequent read-only dispatch tools hang too — not just the await itself.

ROOT CAUSE to confirm: the attach-to-existing-run path (dispatch-await for a task already in flight ATTACHES rather than re-dispatching) does a blocking GenServer.call / receive whose own timeout is unbounded or >> the MCP transport deadline, so the MCP framing layer times out first and the call never honors timeout_ms. Whether the handler also holds a lock that starves status/list_runs must be verified.

FIX: the await wait must be bounded by timeout_ms at a layer BELOW the MCP transport deadline semantics — i.e. honor timeout_ms (default 30min) by returning the structured :timed_out summary map {state: :timed_out, run_id, ...} as a normal tool result, and ensure attach uses a non-blocking/monitored wait that never holds a shared lock. Read-only tools (dispatch-status, supervisor-list_runs) must stay responsive while an await is in flight.

TEST: a test that dispatches (or fakes) an in-flight run, then awaits with a short timeout_ms, asserts the structured :timed_out summary is returned (not an exception/transport error) and that a concurrent dispatch-status/list_runs returns promptly while the await is pending. flunk on a hang/raise.
mix precommit.full green.
out_of_scope: The happy-path await (run settles before timeout) — that works; this is the attach + timeout + concurrency-starvation path.
Changing the default timeout_ms value.
The MCP client's own transport deadline (client-side, not harness) — the fix is harness honoring timeout_ms server-side so the transport deadline is never the thing that fires first.
task.body:
Found 2026-06-16 from a ccxt-distill orchestration session (driving harness via the MCP dispatch tools to chain rmap tasks). Run-1781604067447-043d5fac (ccxt-distill task 47, codex/gpt-5.5) was in flight. To block until it settled I called dispatch-await {task: '47', project_name: 'ccxt-distill', timeout_ms: 1_800_000}. It returned a bare 'The operation timed out.' transport error after ~60s — not the structured :timed_out summary the tool doc guarantees ('never a wedged tool call'). Worse, the next three calls (dispatch-status on the run_id, then supervisor-list_runs twice) ALSO timed out, even though `ps` confirmed the BEAM phx.server, the postgres pool, and the codex exec child (pid 66034) were all alive and the run was still progressing (a watcher shell was counting toward its 40-min cap). So the attach path doesn't just fail to honor timeout_ms — it appears to wedge the MCP request handler so read-only status calls starve behind it.

Operator workaround used: abandon the MCP await, poll run state out-of-band (ps / watch the worktree's .harness/review.json) instead. That defeats the point of dispatch-await as the 'one call gets the answer' bounded-blocking variant.

This blocks programmatic 'await this run, then dispatch the next ready task' orchestration loops — exactly the goal-driven chaining the dispatch MCP surface exists to support.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1781607673833-50f47009, d1596df90cd280cff095ba30fb7907598a2cd019).

task.title: Transcript legibility — kill the content-less 'OTHER' wall (the flying-blind core)
acceptance_criteria: Viewing a live `reviewing` run at /harness/runs/<id> no longer renders a wall of identical content-less rows: consecutive `{:system, %{kind: :other}}` / `:unknown` events collapse into ONE block (reuse the existing consecutive-:thought collapse path in group_events/2) that shows a count AND the distinct underlying `_type` value(s) seen — never N blank 'OTHER' lines.

cursor.ex maps the event `type`s its current stream-json actually emits but the parser drops to `:other` (enumerate them from a real cursor reviewer transcript — read Harness.Run.LogRecord.agent_output for a cursor-reviewed run via mcp__tidewave__execute_sql_query, or the raw stream): assistant text -> :assistant_text, tool calls -> :assistant_tool_use/:tool_result, reasoning -> :thought — so the reviewer's real work renders as chat turns, not eyebrows.

The `:other`/`:unknown` fallthrough is RETAINED as a never-crash/never-drop safety net (the `when is_binary(other)` and final clauses stay), but its rendering surfaces the payload's `_type` + a short snippet, not a bare kind label.
eyebrow/1 (or the block built for `:other` in group_events/2) carries enough of `data` to be legible — at minimum the `_type` — instead of dropping the payload.

Tests: a fixture of N consecutive cursor `:other` events renders as one collapsed block carrying the count; each newly-recognized cursor type renders as the correct block kind; round-trip through transcript_view/1; the unknown-safety fixture still renders (nothing lost).
Mantra-clean: pure parse + verbatim relay of raw agent output; no event is judged for importance, nothing classified by meaning.
out_of_scope: The run-header stage stepper / token / verdict surfacing (Task 312)
Run timing / elapsed (Task 313)
File-chip counters and activity heartbeat (Task 314)
Rewriting the claude/codex/grok/pi/antigravity parsers beyond the shared eyebrow + :other-collapse fix that benefits all of them
task.body:
Observed live 2026-06-16 on run-1781649574472-0b0e5a80 (state `reviewing`, implementer codex, reviewer cursor). The run-detail page showed Tokens —, Verdict —, 'Files being edited: No file edits observed yet', and a transcript of 500 blocks that every one rendered the literal word 'OTHER'. The operator's words: 'we are flying blind.'

Root cause is mechanical and two-part:
1. lib/harness/dashboard/transcript/parser/cursor.ex:83 — `translate(%{"type" => other} = event) when is_binary(other)` routes EVERY unrecognized cursor event type to `{:system, %{kind: :other, data: ...}}`. Cursor's newer stream-json emits message/delta types the parser never learned, so the reviewer's entire output falls through here.
2. lib/harness/dashboard/components.ex:608 eyebrow/1 renders a `:system` event as JUST `to_string(@kind)` — the `data` payload is deliberately dropped. So 500 `:other` events become 500 content-free 'other' lines (uppercased in display).

Net: during the reviewing stage — exactly when the operator most needs to see what the cross-family reviewer is doing — the transcript is unreadable noise. This is task #1 of the live-run-legibility bundle because the richer header telemetry (312-314) is worthless if the transcript itself is illegible.

Fix is pure mechanics: teach cursor.ex the real event types (read a live cursor transcript to enumerate them — do NOT guess the wire format), keep the `:other`/`:unknown` clauses as a safety net but make them carry their `_type`, and collapse consecutive unknown/other events into one counted block the way consecutive `:thought` events already collapse. Count and relay facts; never judge them.
task.implemented: Killed the content-less 'OTHER' wall: cursor.ex no longer routes unrecognized stream-json types to data-less :other; eyebrow/1 renders the :system data payload. Reviewer approved + landed.

task.title: Live run header — stage stepper + active-agent indicator + live token counter
acceptance_criteria: The run-info region (live.ex render_show, the State row) renders a horizontal STAGE STEPPER mapping Harness.Run.Status.state — dispatched -> running -> committing -> reviewing -> done/failed, with recovering/held shown only when the run is in them — current stage emphasized, prior stages marked complete. It replaces the bare `<dd>{@run_status.state}</dd>` text. Pure render of the state fact; landing/audit (post-settle, separate workers) are explicitly NOT stages here.

The agent active in the CURRENT stage is visually distinguished using the existing stage_agent_label/1 (reviewer while :reviewing, recovery while :recovering, else implementer) — the operator sees WHO is working now, not just Agent + Reviewer listed flat. Use the same pulsing-dot affordance the changed-files-live panel already uses (cf-live-dot).

The Tokens field shows a LIVE running total parsed from the in-flight transcript (token_label/2 already extracts usage from the transcript string) instead of '—' while the run is in flight; '—' remains only when usage is genuinely unavailable for the agent/format.
Smoke-tested via Phoenix.LiveViewTest: each state renders the right stepper position; the active-agent marker tracks state; a transcript carrying usage renders a non-'—' token total.
Mantra-clean: stepper = the state fact rendered; token total = a counted fact; nothing judged.

Per-stage durations (e.g. implement vs review split) render from the entered-at map where present.

task.body:
Observability follow-up to phase-22 live-run-legibility (tasks 311-314, all landed) and Task 204 (the verdict-recovery reviewer feature). Surfaced 2026-06-17 watching ccxt-distill run-1781660224215-a0c2cde3: the first reviewer pass made fix commits but TIMED OUT before writing a valid .harness/review.json, so harness (Task 204) spawned a recovery reviewer (a live `claude -p`, real OS pid, actively editing the worktree to fix a failing `npm run check`). The run was genuinely progressing.

But dispatch-status and the run-detail page reported agent_os_pid=nil and agent_kind=[:timed_out,:total] — the PRIOR, timed-out pass's terminal fields. The live recovery-reviewer process is tracked NOWHERE in the status surface, so the page looks frozen ('output a few seconds ago') while a real process churns underneath. Operators misread this as a hang and may kill a live run. This is the exact 'flying blind' failure mode the 311-314 bundle fixed, one code path over — the recovery-reviewer pass.

Fix: thread the recovery-reviewer invocation's pid + a distinct kind through Harness.Run.Status (same way the normal reviewer is tracked) so dispatch-status and the run-detail page show the LIVE recovery pass — its pid, its elapsed-since-recovery-start, its streaming transcript — instead of the dead prior pass's fields.

Mantra: pure mechanical fact-surfacing. The page counts and relays (pid, kind, elapsed, transcript); 'stuck vs working' stays with the human/AI, never a formula. Cross-ref: Task 204 (recovery feature), bundle live-run-legibility.
