task.title: dispatch-bundle ignores per-task assignee — routes whole wave to one global adapter, and doesn't gate depends_on
acceptance_criteria: dispatch-bundle resolves the adapter for each task from that task's own assignee (reusing recommended_adapter_for_item/3 or equivalent), not a single wave-wide render_agent
Each task's model is resolved via effective_model/2 semantics: the rmap pin when it matches the resolved agent, else Config.agent_model(agent) — never a foreign pin handed to a mismatched adapter
The `adapter` param is the fallback for tasks with no assignee, not an override of assigned tasks
A mixed-roster bundle (tasks assigned codex/cursor/grok) enqueues three jobs with the matching Codex/Cursor/Grok adapters — regression test

dispatch-bundle excludes or defers any task whose depends_on includes a non-done task in the dispatch set, matching roadmap-ready semantics; a dependent task is never placed in the same wave as a pending/in-flight dependency — regression test
Existing single-family bundle dispatch behaviour is unchanged (no regression for the homogeneous-adapter calls that work today)
out_of_scope: Changing WriteSetPlan's write-set collision semantics (Task 292 design — collision detection stays independent of the dep graph; this adds a separate dep gate, it does not alter collision behaviour)
The cron RoadmapPoller routing (already on assignee via Task 130)
New AgentAdapters or new rmap delegate --to targets
task.body:
The dispatch-bundle MCP tool (Harness.Dispatch.bundle/3) ignores each task's per-task assignee/model and routes the ENTIRE wave to a single global adapter (the `adapter` param, defaulting to "claude"). bundle/3 resolves one {module, render_agent} and ingest_bundle/3 ingests every task with that same render_agent; the per-task Item.assignee is carried structurally but never consulted, and Batch.enqueue_item routes off Item.agent (the global render agent), not Item.assignee. Each task keeps its rmap-pinned `model`, so a task pinned to a non-claude model (e.g. gpt-5.5, composer-2.5, grok-composer-2.5-fast) gets the claude adapter + its foreign model and fails spawn with {:invalid_model_for_adapter, Claude, <model>} at AgentAdapter.validate_model/2.

Confirmed in production 2026-06-17: a no-adapter-arg dispatch-bundle on delta_calc (tasks 27-34) + ccxt-distill (53) produced 9 failed runs, every one adapter=Claude paired with a foreign model. The reason it normally "works" is survivorship: callers dispatch one family at a time with a matching explicit `adapter`, so the single global adapter happens to match the tasks' pins. A genuinely mixed-roster bundle dispatched with any single adapter fails every off-family task.

dispatch-task already does this correctly: its recommend path calls recommended_adapter_for_item/3 (reads Item.assignee) and effective_model/2 (falls back to Config.agent_model/1 when the pin doesn't match the agent). The bundle path calls neither. The fix is to make the bundle path resolve adapter+model PER TASK from each task's own assignee (reusing recommended_adapter_for_item/3 + effective_model/2), with the `adapter` param as the fallback for unassigned tasks rather than a wave-wide override.

Secondary defect in the same path: WriteSetPlan (the only wave serializer) groups tasks purely by write-set collision (touches union files_to_modify) and never reads depends_on. So a dependent task can land in the SAME wave as its dependency (observed: task 33 depends_on [28-32], task 34 depends_on [26,28,30], all enqueued in wave 1), forking off pre-dep HEAD. roadmap-ready already excludes dep-unsatisfied tasks; the bundle path must match those semantics — exclude (or defer to a later wave) any task whose depends_on includes a non-done task in the dispatch set.
task.implemented: Codex/gpt-5.5 delivery (run-1781707166155-8772138d), cross-family reviewer Cursor approved. dispatch-bundle now resolves adapter+model per task from each task's assignee (falls back to the adapter param for unassigned tasks) instead of one wave-wide render_agent, and gates depends_on so dependent tasks aren't placed in a wave with non-done deps. Regression tests for mixed codex/cursor/grok roster + dep-gating. diff 326 LOC.

task.title: Harden the reviewer verdict contract — reject-red-tree rule + structured `checks` claim + `concerns` field in review.json
acceptance_criteria: reviewer_prompt/1 AND reviewer_reprompt/1 both instruct: you MUST run the project's checks; a red you cannot make green and choose to DISMISS as environmental/out-of-scope MUST be recorded as a reproduced root cause in the structured `checks`/`concerns` claim — never waved through on an unsupported 'environmental' aside. This REPLACES the earlier absolute 'a red suite is never environmental => MUST reject' (keep reviewer judgment; make a dismissed red un-buryable; do not substitute prompt dogma for judgment).

review.json contract extended with a `checks` field (commands run + the reviewer's own per-check pass/fail) and a `concerns` list (self-flagged caveats); reviewer prompt instructs the reviewer to emit both.
Harness.Run.Review parses `checks` + `concerns` verbatim; missing blocks => %{}/[] with no crash and no closed enum (same tolerance as facets/skills).
Both persist onto LogRecord + the Postgres run_record schema via one additive migration; a record carrying both reads back from ResultStore.

A non-empty `concerns` OR a reviewer-self-marked-failing `checks` claim on an `approve` verdict is surfaced loudly (run record flag + notification + dashboard) — harness only counts presence/fail-flag, never classifies prose; no regex/keyword classifier is added.

Tests cover: prompt asserts the dismissed-red-must-be-a-recorded-concern/check + emit-checks/concerns language; checks/concerns parse+persist round-trip; missing-block tolerance; loud-surface on approve+non-empty-concerns. NEVER-HIDE-FAILURES assertions (flunk on unexpected), not assert-true-on-any-outcome.
Offline suite green; mix precommit green; CLAUDE.md + docs/agent-gate-workflow.md + skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md re-keyed to the extended contract; CHANGELOG entry.
out_of_scope: Reintroducing Harness.Verification / CheckStack / presets / a mechanical check gate / lander re-verification.
Any prose classifier, keyword match, or harness-derived verdict from the report/checks text.
The post-merge cold-build witness (separate task) and the dispatch-reland guard (separate task).
Auto-blocking an approve on non-empty concerns — flag-loudly is the chosen default; blocking is explicitly deferred unless the design call above flips it.
task.body:
Origin: 2026-06-20 post-mortem of two post-rebuild false-green landings — task 241 (reviewer approved a roadmap-load optimization that hung every render) and the tapakly gettext incident (reviewer SAW the full suite red, judged it a warm-cache/environmental artifact, named the exact mechanism, and approved it "out of scope"). Both passed THE gate. The reviewer is told to run the project's checks (step 2 of reviewer_prompt/1) but is never forced to, never has to prove it, and the prompt's reject condition is so narrow ("nothing to salvage") plus its "fixing is always cheaper than rejecting" pressure that a red-but-rationalizable tree biases toward approve. Harness reads only the `verdict` word; whether checks ran / what they returned is invisible.

VERIFIED EVIDENCE CASE (the canonical one — git-blame proven, 2026-06-20): tapakly task 225 was delivered by a dispatched agent in commit f7e6549 ("Make precommit.full test failures diagnosable and stable", 2026-06-19 06:12 UTC). The agent added a `preferred_envs` line to tapakly mix.exs for the fancy aliases (test.json / dialyzer.json / precommit.test) but FORGOT the boring path — classic "fixed the fancy path, broke the boring path." The broken build-config produced a non-deterministic doctest doc-chunk failure (`could not retrieve the documentation for module … not compiled with documentation`, a different module each run). The reviewer of task 225 SAW the resulting red suite and mislabeled it "protocol-consolidation / environmental instability," approved, and it landed. Then FOUR more reviewers (tapakly runs 227, 231, 232, 233, 2026-06-19→20) each hit the downstream doc-chunk red and ALSO waved it through as "environmental" — five consecutive false-greens on one real, boring config bug. This is exactly the rationalization this task removes: a hard reject-red rule stops run 225 from landing, and a mandatory `checks`/`concerns` claim turns "I think this red is environmental" from a buried prose excuse into a self-marked-failing fact harness surfaces loudly. (Note: the earlier gettext / warm-cache / shared-DB theories were separate or wrong-cause; the doc-chunk failure traces specifically to f7e6549.)

This is the agent-gate-compatible fix: harden what the reviewer must COMMIT TO as data, and make a self-flagged caveat un-buryable — no new mechanical gate, no harness judgment of meaning.

Three coupled changes, all on the reviewer verdict contract (reviewer_prompt/1 AND reviewer_reprompt/1 are the same embedded prompt twice — change both in sync, per Task 224 note):

1. Prompt rule (SOFTENED 2026-06-20 — see SETTLED note below; do NOT ship the old absolute): "You MUST run the project's checks. If they are still red after your fixes and you DISMISS that red as environmental / out-of-scope, you must FIRST reproduce the cause and record it as a `checks`/`concerns` fact (the command, its failing output, the mechanism) — a dismissed red is never a bare prose aside. If you cannot reproduce a benign cause, treat the red as a real defect." This kills the rationalization both incidents used (an unsupported 'environmental' wave-through) WITHOUT replacing reviewer judgment with a blanket 'red => reject' dogma that would mislabel genuine environmental noise as a defect.

2. Extend the review.json contract (currently {verdict, report, facets, skills} after Task 224/225) with a structured `checks` claim the reviewer must emit: the command(s) it actually ran, and the reviewer's own pass/fail call on each. The reviewer commits to a claim-as-data separable from prose — "I ran X, it was green" becomes a field, not a sentence buried in `report`.

3. Add an optional `concerns: []` list to review.json for the reviewer's self-flagged caveats (the 233 reviewer's "this is the root cause, filing out of scope" would have landed HERE as data). Harness surfaces a non-empty `concerns` — or a `checks` claim the reviewer itself marked failing — LOUDLY on an `approve` (run record + notification + dashboard), WITHOUT classifying the prose. No regex, no keyword match: harness only counts "is `concerns` non-empty" / "did the reviewer's own checks-claim say fail" — facts the reviewer wrote, not meaning harness derived.

Harness.Run.Review must parse `checks`/`concerns` verbatim (free-form, missing → %{}/[], never a crash, never a closed enum — same tolerance as facets/skills). Persist onto LogRecord + the Postgres run_record schema (open :map columns + one additive migration); coordinate migration ordering with any pending run_record migration.

WHY THIS STAYS MANTRA-CLEAN (the agent-gate boundary, confirmed — no longer an open tension): (a) the dismiss-must-be-reproduced rule is reviewer JUDGMENT moved into the prompt, not a harness branch; (b) `checks`/`concerns` are facts the reviewer WRITES, and harness only counts presence/non-emptiness — it never interprets the prose or re-derives a verdict. It does NOT reintroduce Harness.Verification, a mechanical check gate, or harness judging pass/fail. The one judgment call (block vs flag a non-empty `concerns` on approve) is SETTLED: flag loudly + let the orchestrator/audit act, never auto-block (see SETTLED point 3 + out_of_scope).

SETTLED 2026-06-20 (overfit analysis + codex cross-review converged — build to these):
1. SEQUENCING — `depends_on 320` is now DONE (shipped 824466c). The shared-DB contamination that made reds genuinely-often-environmental is closed, so a red is now a real signal and the dismiss-must-be-reproduced rule is safe to ship. (Had this landed before 320 it would have forced rejection of real environmental reds → a re-dispatch storm of false-reds.)
2. SOFTENED THE ABSOLUTE (AC[0] + body change #1 now reflect this) — the blanket "a red suite is NEVER environmental → MUST reject" is REPLACED by "a DISMISSED red must be recorded as a reproduced `checks`/`concerns` fact." The loud-surface mechanism (parts 2+3 — the structured claim + un-buryable caveat) does the real work; keep reviewer judgment, do not substitute prompt dogma. The `checks`/`concerns` structured-claim half is unchanged — it is the durable win.
3. flag-loudly, NOT auto-block (out_of_scope already states this): a non-empty `concerns` / self-failing `checks` on an approve is surfaced loudly; the orchestrator/audit acts on it. Harness never auto-blocks an approve from the prose.

task.title: Post-merge cold-build witness — un-warmed audit pass; the audit AI runs the clean build and reports red as an agent-written FACT, red => blocked task + loud notify (never revert)
acceptance_criteria: The post-merge audit runs ONE pass on an UN-warmed worktree of the landed SHA — `Worktree.warm/2` is simply NOT called for this pass (cold deps/_build/plts); the implementer/reviewer warm paths are untouched. (The lander's existing checkout is already un-warmed — same pattern.)

The audit AI is prompted to run the project's clean-build/check on that cold tree and REPORT the result (pass/fail + the failing output tail) in its audit artifact; harness does NOT shell out the build itself and does NOT read an exit code — the agent runs it, the agent reports it.
The audit AI's reported cold-check result is persisted as a counted FACT on the audit/run record (a field the agent wrote, never a harness-derived verdict).
A reported-red cold check files a `blocked` rmap task (naming landed SHA + failure tail) and fires a loud Harness.Notification; a reported-green cold check is a silent recorded fact.
The audit NEVER reverts, unmerges, blocks the merge, or feeds the cold-check result back into any approve/reject decision — assert the no-gate/no-revert contract holds.

A regression test simulates a cold-only failure (a fixture that the audit AI double reports green warm / red cold, via the existing FakeAdapter audit seam) and asserts: blocked task filed + notification fired + NO revert + merge untouched.

Offline suite green; mix precommit green; docs (agent-gate-workflow.md, audit doc, CLAUDE.md) note the cold-build witness is a post-merge agent-reported FACT, not a gate, and that harness never runs the build itself; CHANGELOG entry.
out_of_scope: Any PRE-merge cold-build gate, lander re-verification, or blocking a land on cold-check red (explicitly the line we do not cross here).

Harness shelling out the cold build / reading an exit code itself, OR a `clean_check_command` project-field subsystem — REJECTED as mechanical-verification creep; the audit AI runs and reports it (the warm `check_command` hint is the only command source).
Reverting / unmerging / auto-fixing the cold-broken base — the audit only files a task + notifies.
Catching runtime-side-effect regressions (task 241 class) — a cold build won't catch a hang-under-render; that's reviewer-exercise-runtime + test coverage, out of scope here.
Changing Worktree.warm/2 for the implementer/reviewer paths — they stay warm; only this audit pass is un-warmed.
task.body:
Origin: 2026-06-20 post-mortem. The deepest structural finding: NO agent in the loop ever does a cold build. Worktree.warm/2 (Task ~219) deliberately CoW-copies the parent checkout's built deps/_build/plts into every implementer, reviewer, AND auditor worktree, so a dep-compile-time / cold-only regression is invisible to every judge in the chain. The tapakly gettext incident proves the class: task 224 put `config :gettext, :plural_forms` in config/config.exs, read at DEP-compile time before the app module exists => `:nofile` on a cold `mix compile`. The reviewer (warm _build) saw it as environmental and approved; the lander builds warm too; the breakage only appears on a fresh checkout / a contributor's machine. Witnessing the reviewer's output better would NOT have caught it — only a clean checkout reproduces it.

FIX DIRECTION — SETTLED 2026-06-20 (overfit analysis + codex cross-review converged on the LEAN form; build THIS, not the original heavy version):

The audit already creates a worktree (audit.ex:593), warms it (audit.ex:138 — the only `warm/2` calls are run.ex:670 implementer + audit.ex:138), and already prompts the audit AI to run the project's checks (prompt ~line 432). The lander's checkout is ALREADY un-warmed — a cold-worktree pattern exists. So the cold-build witness is near-free and stays mantra-clean:

1. Do NOT warm the audit worktree for this witness pass — simply skip the `Worktree.warm/2` call so the audit AI faces a cold tree (cold deps/_build/plts). A dep-compile-time / cold-only regression (the tapakly gettext class: `config :gettext` read at DEP-compile before the app module exists => `:nofile` on a cold `mix compile`) only reproduces on a clean checkout — warming is exactly what hid it from every judge in the chain.

2. Prompt the audit AI (one added instruction) to run the project's clean-build/check on that cold tree and REPORT the result in its audit artifact. Harness does NOT shell out the build and does NOT read an exit code — "harness runs the check + records pass/fail" is the camel's nose straight back to the mechanical Harness.Verification the 2026-06-03 rebuild deleted. The agent runs it; the agent reports it; harness only COUNTS the fact the agent wrote (mantra-clean: count facts, judge with an AI).

3. Persist the audit AI's reported cold-check result as a fact on the audit/run record. A reported-red files a `blocked` rmap task (landed SHA + failure tail) + fires a loud Harness.Notification; a reported-green is a silent fact. NEVER revert / unmerge / block — the merge already happened; this is a best-effort post-merge witness consistent with the audit's existing no-gate contract. It catches the cold-only class one merge late, but LOUDLY, so later work doesn't keep building on a cold-broken base.

REJECTED from the original draft: the separate clean-clone machinery, harness shelling out the build + reading exit codes, and the `clean_check_command` per-project field. All are mechanical-verification creep; the un-warmed audit pass + the agent's own report replace them.

SEQUENCING: `depends_on 317` — NOT a logical dependency but a write-set serialization. Both 317 and this add a field to LogRecord/run_record + a migration; dispatched in parallel they collide on log_record.ex + the migrations dir. 317 lands first, this rebases onto its migration. (320, the shared-DB root cause, is already DONE — a cold red is now a real signal.)

PAIRS WITH task 321 (the consumer): this is the WRITE side — the audit witnesses a cold red as a fact. 321 is the READ side — it keys an approved-then-found-red fact to the reviewer and surfaces it in routing. Same audit surface, producer/consumer split, two dispatches, one design.

task.title: Close two reviewer-gate trust holes from the 2026-06-20 audit: dispatch-reland verdict guard + fake-reviewer artifact can't leak into a real checkout
acceptance_criteria: dispatch-reland / Lander.enqueue asserts the loaded run record reached an approved (done) outcome before enqueuing the land; a reland of a rejected/failed/non-approved run is refused with a clear error and pushes nothing.
A test proves reland of a non-approved run_id is rejected (no push), and reland of an approved run still works.

The fake reviewer adapter + fake codex binary write `.harness/review.json` only inside the test's temp worktree, never the repository root; a guard/test asserts no stray verdict file lands in the repo root after the suite runs.
Offline suite green; mix precommit green; CHANGELOG note for both fixes.
out_of_scope: The reviewer prompt / review.json contract changes (separate task).
The post-merge cold-build witness (separate task).
Any change to the auto-land path (already correctly gated on reason: :approved).
task.body:
Two small, independent safety holes surfaced by the 2026-06-20 trust-chain audit. Both are inline-sized (≤30 LOC each, no public-surface redesign) and land together in one session; neither warrants its own dispatch cycle.

1. dispatch-reland has no verdict guard. Lander.enqueue/1 -> load_record/1 (lib/harness/lander.ex ~141) loads the run record via ResultStore.list_run_records(run_id:) with NO filter on run state or verdict, then ff-pushes whatever is on harness/<run-id> to origin/<target>. The moduledoc says "reviewer-approved," but the code never asserts it — an operator/orchestrator can reland a run whose verdict was `reject` or whose state is `:failed`, pushing un-approved work with zero checks. Fix: assert the loaded record reached an approved/done outcome before relanding; reject a reland of a non-approved run with a clear error. (The auto-land path in maybe_enqueue_landing/2 is already gated on reason: :approved — only this manual re-land path is missing the guard.)

2. The fake reviewer artifact can leak a real auto-approve file. FakeAdapter.review_report/1 (test/support/fake_adapter.ex ~437) and the fake codex binary (test/support/run_case.ex ~388) do `mkdir -p .harness && printf ... > .harness/review.json` relative to CWD. On 2026-06-20 a `{"verdict":"approve","report":"fake review: approve"}` file was found sitting in the MAIN checkout root (deleted by hand this session). Harmless in production (real runs read isolated worktrees), but a stray auto-approve file in a repo root is a loaded gun. Fix: make the fake adapter/codex write its verdict only inside the test's own temp worktree CWD (never the project root), and/or have the test harness assert no .harness/review.json escaped to the repo root after the suite.

These are unrelated files (lander.ex vs test/support) but share one motivating audit and one short session — bundled to avoid two manufactured dispatch cycles, not as a grab-bag.
task.implemented: Hand-built. (1) Lander.enqueue/1 now asserts the loaded record settled :done with verdict :approve before relanding (ensure_approved/1); non-approved reland refused {:not_approved,_}, pushes nothing. (2) RunCase setup on_exit guard removes+flunks on any repo-root .harness/review.json leak. Tests: reland guard (reject/failed refused, approved re-lands) + 215 RunCase tests green. Lander 85.8% cov.

task.title: Per-run test-DB isolation — concurrent worktree runs share one test DB and cross-contaminate (the verified root cause of tapakly's recurring 'environmental' red suites)
acceptance_criteria: Every dispatched run injects a per-run-unique, DB-name-safe env var (default MIX_TEST_PARTITION, derived from the run id) into the implementer AND reviewer Port environment via the existing :env threading — no two concurrent runs of the same project resolve the same test DB.
A per-project override selects the env-var name (and an explicit opt-out) on %Harness.Project{}; an opted-out or non-DB project sees ZERO behavior change.

Teardown of the per-run test DB is best-effort and never a gate (logged on failure, never blocks settle/land) — or, if deferred to the project, that decision is documented in the PR with the accumulation tradeoff named.
A regression test proves two concurrent runs of the same project with divergent migrations do NOT contaminate each other's test DB (each resolves a distinct database name from its injected env).

Documented in CLAUDE.md + docs/agent-gate-workflow.md: the reviewer runs checks in a per-run-isolated test DB; projects must honor the isolation env var (Phoenix default already does); the agent-gate rebuild's deletion of per-worktree DB provisioning is recorded as the regression this restores.
Offline suite green; mix precommit green; CHANGELOG entry referencing the tapakly contamination (first observed run task 85, 2026-06-10).
out_of_scope: Reintroducing Harness.Verification / CheckStack / a mechanical check gate — this only SETS an env var; the reviewer still runs the checks and remains the gate.
The reviewer prompt / verdict contract changes (task 317) and the post-merge cold-build witness (task 318) — separate.
Fixing any genuine (non-environmental) tapakly test failure that survives DB isolation — that is tapakly's own defect, verified separately.
Harness's OWN test-suite async/sandbox isolation (separate roadmap thread).
task.body:
VERIFIED ROOT CAUSE (run_records evidence, 2026-06-20 investigation): every dispatched run for a project shares ONE test database (e.g. `tapakly_test`). The reviewer (and implementer) run `mix test` themselves inside the worktree, and the project's test config resolves the SAME DB name for every concurrent run. Parallel runs on different `harness/<run-id>` branches carry DIVERGENT migrations/schemas, so they stomp each other's DB → red suites that "pass in isolation / on a clean DB." First observed tapakly run: task 85, 2026-06-10 13:25:42 — 3 SavedSearch tests failing `null value in column "user_id" of relation "saved_searches"`, the reviewer naming it "contamination in the SHARED tapakly_test DB from a concurrent harness run on another branch" with "29 other sessions hold the DB." The same family of symptom ("module not available," "Postgrex connection-pool cascade," failure count scaling with --max-cases) recurred and was waved past as "environmental" ~16 times (tasks 85,87,143,169,192,194,195,197,205,221,227,231,232,233) through 2026-06-20. This is the ORIGINAL recurring failure — distinct from and older than the gettext cold-build (task 224, 19 Jun) and unrelated to the (falsified) warm/2 abs-path theory.

REGRESSION CONTEXT: harness USED to provision a per-worktree DB — Task 145 ("Check.env with {:harness, :test_database}, per-worktree HARNESS_DB_NAME, test-db-create/migrate setup"). The agent-gate rebuild (2026-06-03) deleted Harness.Verification/CheckStack wholesale and took that per-worktree DB provisioning with it as collateral (same pattern as Worktree.warm). With the reviewer now running checks itself and no per-run DB isolation, the shared-DB contamination resurfaced one week later (10 Jun).

FIX DIRECTION (mantra-clean — this is mechanical SUBSTRATE, env-setting, not judgment): give each run's worktree its OWN test database by threading a per-run-unique env var into the run's Port environment via the EXISTING `:env` plumbing (Run.start_run :env -> Oban args -> worker -> AgentAdapter port_env). The Ecto/Phoenix convention is `MIX_TEST_PARTITION` — generated `config/test.exs` reads `database: "<app>_test#{System.get_env("MIX_TEST_PARTITION")}"`, and the default `test` alias (`ecto.create --quiet`, `ecto.migrate`) then creates the partitioned DB on demand, so simply setting a unique `MIX_TEST_PARTITION` per run is enough for any project that follows the Phoenix default. Set it by default for every run, derived from the run id (a short, DB-name-safe suffix).

DESIGN CALLS — SETTLED 2026-06-20 (build to these; they were the assignee=human gate, now decided):
1. Env-var name: DEFAULT `MIX_TEST_PARTITION` (Phoenix/Ecto idiom). Add an OPTIONAL per-project override on %Harness.Project{} (`test_db_isolation_env`, free-text) for projects that name their isolation var differently; unset => MIX_TEST_PARTITION. The value injected is a short, DB-name-safe suffix derived from the run id.
2. Teardown: best-effort post-run drop of the run's partition DB — mechanical, logged on failure, NEVER a gate (never blocks settle/land). A failed drop is a logged fact, not an error.
3. Opt-out: a per-project explicit opt-out (e.g. `test_db_isolation_env` set to a sentinel like "none"/false) disables injection entirely with ZERO behavior change — for projects managing their own isolation or with no DB (a Rust sqlx project doing ephemeral per-test DBs opts out). Default-on for every other run.

This is the highest-value of the gate-hardening batch: it removes the very "red suite that's actually environmental" signal that trained reviewers to rubber-stamp red — pairs with task 317 (reject-red rule) so that, once the DB noise is gone, a red suite is genuinely a defect.

task.title: Close the false-green loop: audit records approved-then-found-red as a structured reviewer FACT; surface it for AI-judged reviewer routing (no score formula)
acceptance_criteria: The post-merge audit, when its cold check of the landed SHA is reported red (the task-318 witness), persists a STRUCTURED approved-then-found-red fact on the run/audit record keyed to the reviewer adapter + model + the run's facets/domains — never prose, never a closed enum, missing => empty with no crash.

AgentKPI exposes a reviewer false-approval rollup (a counted rate per {reviewer-agent, model}) alongside the existing aggregate_reviewer_rejections rejection/no-verdict signals; pure read-only rollup over run records.

The false-approval rate is SURFACED to the routing surfaces (routing-brief KPI cells / the scout's raw inputs) as a counted fact, for the orchestrating/scout AI to judge when selecting a reviewer adapter. Harness persists and surfaces the fact and computes NO down-weight, penalty, percentile gate, score adjustment, or auto-exclusion over it — the routing decision stays with the AI, never with arithmetic over this number (codex 2026-06-20: an auto-down-weight is the old judgment-as-formula error in new clothes).
No harness branch classifies the audit report prose or re-derives 'good/bad reviewer' — harness only counts the structured red-fact the audit AI wrote (assert: no regex/keyword over report text).

Tests: approved-then-red fact parse+persist round-trip; rollup computes the false-approval rate (a count) from seeded records; the routing surface EXPOSES the rate as a fact (assert NO formula/weight is applied to it); NEVER-HIDE-FAILURES assertions (flunk on unexpected).
Offline suite green; mix precommit green; CLAUDE.md + docs/agent-gate-workflow.md + skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md document the false-green feedback loop; CHANGELOG entry.
out_of_scope: Reintroducing Harness.Verification / a mechanical check gate / lander re-verification / any auto-revert.
The cold-build witness itself (task 318 — this consumes its structured red-fact).
The reviewer prompt / checks/concerns contract (task 317) and test-DB isolation (task 320).
Any prose classifier or harness-derived verdict from the audit report text.
task.body:
Origin: 2026-06-20 overfit analysis of the false-green batch (317/318/319/320). Every fix in that batch is PRE-LAND prevention; none makes the system LEARN when a reviewer was wrong. Today the only thing that catches a false-green is a human post-mortem ~2.5 weeks late. This task adds the missing feedback loop, using surfaces that already almost exist — the durable, in-architecture move the batch circles without naming.

VERIFIED CONTEXT (source, 2026-06-20): AgentKPI/CapabilityScore key on IMPLEMENTER outcomes. aggregate_reviewer_rejections/1 tracks a reviewer's rejection-rate + no_verdict_rate, but there is NO false-APPROVAL signal. The audit prompt already instructs the audit AI to flag false REJECTIONS in its .audit/<sha>.md markdown (audit.ex ~449) — prose, never a structured field, never fed back into scoring. dispatch-recommend already reads CapabilityScore.recommend/2 for routing (dispatch.ex ~1189).

The loop (mantra-clean — harness COUNTS facts the agents WRITE, never judges): the post-merge audit (made a cold second judge by task 318) observes "the reviewer of run X approved; the audit AI reports the landed SHA red on a cold tree." Persist that as a STRUCTURED fact on the run/audit record — an approved-then-found-red flag keyed to {reviewer-agent, model, the run's facets/domains} — NOT prose. AgentKPI rolls it into a counted reviewer false-approval rate (alongside the existing rejection/no-verdict rates), and that rate is SURFACED in routing so the orchestrating/scout AI can route a reviewer that repeatedly approves work the audit later breaks away from the review seat. An AI judging an AI's judgment, on counted facts — exactly the architecture; the AI decides "good reviewer," never a harness formula.

Producer/consumer split from task 318: 318 makes the audit a cold judge and witnesses the red as a fact (write side); THIS task adds the reviewer-keyed false-approval field, the AgentKPI rollup, and the routing SURFACING (read side). Two dispatches, one design.

DESIGN CALLS — SETTLED 2026-06-20 (overfit analysis + codex cross-review; build to these):
1. Field shape: the approved-then-red fact is an open `:map` on LogRecord/run_record (additive migration, same tolerance as facets/skills — missing => empty, no crash, no closed enum), keyed to the reviewer adapter + model + the run's facets/domains.
2. SURFACE ONLY — no auto-down-weight. The false-approval rate is exposed as a counted fact in routing-brief / the scout's inputs; the orchestrating AI decides. Any arithmetic down-weight, penalty, percentile gate, or auto-exclude over this number is FORBIDDEN — that is exactly the judgment-as-formula error the mantra deletes, "in new clothes" (codex 2026-06-20). This is the single most dangerous spot in the batch for formula-creep; the AC asserts no weight is applied.
3. No prose classifier: harness counts the presence of the audit AI's structured red-fact, never parses the audit report text (no regex/keyword over `report`).

task.title: Antigravity is no longer model-incapable — agy 1.0.10 gained --model + a multi-model catalog; make the adapter model-capable
acceptance_criteria: The exact accepted `agy --model` id strings are confirmed against the live CLI (positively — not by absence of error, since unknown ids are silently accepted) and recorded in the adapter (moduledoc or a catalog mapping)
Antigravity capabilities/0 declares a non-empty model_families covering the families agy fronts (gemini/claude/gpt-oss); it is no longer the model_families: [] exemption

build_command/1 threads Invocation.model to `agy --model <id>` and no longer returns {:error, {:unsupported_model, _}}; a model-less dispatch on antigravity is rejected as model_required like every other model-capable adapter (implementer and reviewer paths)
An unknown/unresolved model pin fails fast (validated against the known agy catalog) BEFORE the agy port spawns, never silently running agy's default model
Harness.ModelAvailability probes `agy models` and returns catalog entries for antigravity (no longer :catalog_unavailable), mapping display labels to dash-form ids
Antigravity passes Harness.AgentAdapter.ConformanceCase unchanged, plus unit tests for model threading, the model-required reject, and the unknown-model fast-fail
Stale 'antigravity is model-incapable / the lone exemption' copy is corrected in the adapter moduledoc, CLAUDE.md, and the dashboard settings copy
mix precommit.full passes
out_of_scope: Changing other adapters (claude/codex/cursor/grok/pi) — they already handle --model
Routing policy / KPI changes for which antigravity model to prefer — this only makes the model axis work; routing is downstream
Fixing agy's non-validating --model upstream — harness works with the CLI as shipped and guards around it
Worktree isolation — already resolved (Task 32/198); antigravity stays worktree_isolation: true via --add-dir
task.body:
The `agy` CLI (Antigravity) has evolved past the "lone model-incapable adapter" premise baked into harness. As of `agy` 1.0.10 it is a multi-model front-end like Cursor: it now exposes a `--model` flag and an `agy models` subcommand listing 8 models — Gemini 3.5 Flash (Low/Med/High), Gemini 3.1 Pro (Low/High), Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Thinking), Claude Opus 4.6 (Thinking), GPT-OSS 120B. The settings.json `model` key (default `gemini-3.5-flash`) confirms the accepted id format is the dash-form slug (e.g. `gemini-3.5-flash`, `gemini-3.1-pro`, `claude-opus-4-5`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `gpt-oss-120b` per the shipped binary), NOT the display names `agy models` prints.

Make `Harness.AgentAdapter.Antigravity` model-capable: stop declaring `model_families: []`, stop hard-rejecting a model with `{:error, {:unsupported_model, model}}`, and thread `Invocation.model` through to `agy --model <id>` (use the shared `AgentAdapter.model_args/1` helper the other adapters use). Update `capabilities/0`'s `model_families` to the families agy actually fronts (gemini / claude / gpt-oss), matching the `Capabilities` family-prefix map convention. With this, antigravity stops being the model-incapable exemption and becomes a normal model-required adapter — including the reviewer path (`Run.reviewer_model/1`) and the `{:model_required, agent}` reject when no model resolves.

Also wire antigravity into the model catalog: `Harness.ModelAvailability` currently routes antigravity into the `default_probe(_agent, _) -> {:error, :catalog_unavailable}` fallback. Add an `agy models` probe and parse its output into catalog entries, mapping each display label to its dash-form id (the display names carry reasoning-level suffixes like "(Thinking)"/"(High)" that are NOT part of the id — establish the label→id mapping).

CRITICAL sharp edge — agy's `--model` is non-validating. Verified: `agy --model "__nope__" -p "hi"` returns exit 0 and silently runs the default model with no error. This directly contradicts harness's "reject an unknown/unresolved model, never silently run a CLI default" contract that exists to stop a sticky premium default burning budget while claiming a model it didn't run. Decide and implement the guard: the adapter (or the dispatch/catalog path) must validate the pinned model against the known agy catalog before spawning, failing fast on an unknown id rather than letting agy silently fall back. Document this CLI behavior in the adapter moduledoc as a sharp edge.

Update the now-stale "antigravity is the model-incapable exemption" copy everywhere it asserts that: the adapter moduledoc's "Model Override" section, CLAUDE.md (the three-axis adapter-contract section + the harness-workflow notes that call antigravity the lone `model_families: []` exemption), and the dashboard settings copy in `settings_components.ex` / the `settings_live.ex` model_required logic that special-cases antigravity as exempt.

Because the silent-fallback means a wrong id produces no error, positively confirm the accepted id strings against the live CLI before trusting them (e.g. set the model and verify via the statusline / a "which model are you" probe), since `agy --model <bogus>` will NOT tell you it was rejected.

task.title: Add an integration tripwire: each worktree_isolation:true adapter actually isolates to its run worktree (harness skips the pollution snapshot on trust)
acceptance_criteria: An :integration-tagged test drives each worktree_isolation:true adapter (whose CLI is on PATH) through its real build_command/1 flags in a throwaway linked worktree and asserts the agent's write landed in the worktree, not the main checkout
The main checkout's porcelain status is asserted unchanged across the run (the exact invariant the skipped snapshot would have enforced)
Adapters whose CLI is absent are skipped with an explicit message naming them; a run that exercised zero adapters fails/flunks loudly rather than reporting a green no-op
Test is excluded from the default `mix test.json` run (integration tag) and documented as such
mix precommit.full passes (the new test does not run in the default suite)
out_of_scope: Changing the skip-on-trust design itself — keeping worktree_isolation:true adapters snapshot-free is intentional; this only adds an out-of-band tripwire
Fixing any adapter CLI upstream
Re-enabling the per-run pollution snapshot for isolating adapters
task.body:
For any adapter declaring `worktree_isolation: true`, `Harness.Run.checkout_snapshot_for_run/1` returns nil, so `Harness.Worktree.Isolation.check_pollution/3` short-circuits to `:ok` and harness takes NO pollution snapshot. The entire main-checkout-safety net is therefore trust-only for all six shipped adapters — Task 32's regression guard only protects `worktree_isolation: false` adapters (which still get a snapshot). If a future CLI release (agy historically — Task 32/198 — but equally codex/cursor/grok/pi) regresses its workspace resolution and starts writing to the main checkout, harness will not catch it: the run settles normally and the pollution lands ungraded in the canonical checkout. There is currently no empirical test that any isolating adapter actually isolates.

Add an `:integration`-tagged regression test (excluded from the default suite, run on demand / CI with live CLIs) that, for each registered `worktree_isolation: true` adapter whose CLI is present on PATH, exercises the REAL isolation path: create a throwaway linked git worktree off HEAD, invoke the adapter via its actual `build_command/1` flags (the same Port + cwd + isolation flags a real run uses) with a minimal "create one marker file" prompt, then assert the marker landed inside the worktree AND the main checkout's `git status --porcelain` is byte-identical before/after (no pollution). Skip-with-a-clear-message (never silently) any adapter whose CLI is not installed, listing what was skipped — a suite that ran zero adapters must say so, not report green. Manually verified 2026-06-21 that agy 1.0.10 isolates correctly with `--add-dir <worktree>`; this test makes that a standing tripwire rather than a one-off check.

task.title: Stabilize residual erl_child_setup spawn flake in worktree-heavy suite (Harness.AuditTest noop)
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce the historical erl_child_setup EPIPE on the current pinned Elixir/OTP toolchain with a bounded repeated-run probe, or record durable non-reproduction evidence before changing production code

If reproduced, identify the actual spawn-pressure/interleaving path and eliminate or bound it so `MIX_ENV=test mix test.json --quiet --cover --cover-threshold 80 --summary-only --exclude integration` is green across repeated runs
No sleeps, no @tag :skip, no retry/gate weakening, and no contract changes to the cold-check witness path
out_of_scope: Re-litigating task 324's AgentAdapter fix (already landed and correct)
Disabling ex_unit_json retry or weakening the precommit gate to hide the flake
task.body:
Follow-up to task 324. During that review, `mix precommit.full` went red intermittently (2 of 4 full `--summary-only` runs). The failing test was `Harness.AuditTest` "run/1 — unaudited-range computation the noop path removes its audit worktree" (`test/harness/audit_test.exs`), with `erl_child_setup: failed with error 32 (EPIPE) on line 284`. That is historical evidence, not a current root-cause proof: re-run a bounded probe on the current pinned toolchain before selecting a fix.

This is a DIFFERENT spawn path than 324 fixed: 324 hardened `Harness.AgentAdapter.invoke` (the agent CLI Port), but this flake is in the System.cmd/git-fixture/worktree path. Normal `mix test.json` HEALS it via ex_unit_json auto-retry (reports `flaky: N`, exit 0); precommit's `--summary-only` disables retry, so it surfaces as a hard `failed: 1`, exit 2.

If the failure still reproduces, trace the concrete spawn/interleaving path before changing it; bounding concurrent external-process spawns is one possible outcome, not a preselected solution. Confirm any fix with the project's precommit test command (`--summary-only`, retry disabled) across repeated runs.

task.title: Invert the rule-content seam + make Invocation agent-agnostic (AgentAdapter no longer names Harness.AgentRules)
acceptance_criteria: lib/harness/agent_adapter/ has zero references to Harness.AgentRules (subsystem compiles with AgentRules absent from its alias graph)

Rule content reaches the adapter via caller-supplied input (string on Invocation or behaviour callback); the four rule_channel/0 delivery paths (system-prompt file, codex ephemeral AGENTS.md, cursor ephemeral .cursor/rules, prompt preamble) + cleanup_injected_rules still work unchanged

Invocation no longer carries `languages` (the actual field: nonempty_list(atom()), default [:elixir] — invocation.ex:43/57); `task_id` is an opaque tag with no rmap coupling; Harness.Run's implementer/reviewer/recovery builders supply rendered rules + section/language filtering caller-side
ConformanceCase passes for all 6 adapters asserting against injected fixture content, not AgentRules.render()

RulesInjection.prepend_prompt/1 (arity-1) — public API with zero production callers (only tests use it as an expected-value baseline for the arity-2 variant) — is removed or folded into the reshaped caller-supplied-content API; tests construct expectations via the surviving surface
Full gate green: mix precommit.full (credo --strict, dialyzer 0, doctor 100%, sobelow, tests incl. conformance)
out_of_scope: Moving the subsystem to a separate repo/hex package (the decision-spike task)
Changing AgentRules content or its priv/agent_rules/canonical.md source
The Driver/Reflex watchdog cycle (the sibling task)
task.body:
Cut the only content-coupling in the adapter subsystem so Harness.AgentAdapter.* no longer names Harness.AgentRules. Today Harness.AgentAdapter.RulesInjection calls AgentRules.write_system_prompt_file!/2, install_codex_rules!/2, install_cursor_rules!/2, and prompt_preamble/0,1 directly (rules_injection.ex:18/29/40/51/59) — binding the generic delivery mechanism to harness-specific rule prose (reviewer-gate, rmap, roadmap/tasks.toml, post-merge audit). Invert it: the delivery mechanism (which file path / argv flag / preamble each rule_channel/0 uses, plus the ephemeral-file write+cleanup lifecycle) stays in the subsystem; the rule content (rendered markdown + the :elixir/section filtering in render_opts/1) is supplied by the caller. Pass rule content into the subsystem (pre-rendered string(s) on Invocation, or a render/install callback on the behaviour) so harness injects its AgentRules output without the subsystem importing it. In the same change, make the Invocation struct agent-agnostic: relocate `language` (its sole consumer is the rule filtering in RulesInjection.render_opts/1, which moves caller-side) and generalize `task_id` to an opaque log tag with no rmap semantics. Update Harness.Run's three Invocation builders — implementer (invocation/3 ~run.ex:1979), reviewer (reviewer_invocation/1 ~run.ex:2428), recovery (recovery_invocation/1 ~run.ex:2331) — to supply the rendered content + section/language filtering caller-side, and update ConformanceCase (test/support/agent_adapter/conformance_case.ex, which currently asserts delivered rules equal AgentRules.render()) to assert against injected fixture content instead. acceptance_criteria: lib/harness/agent_adapter/ (incl. driver.ex) has zero references to Harness.Run.*

Full gate green: mix precommit.full

The rule-content seam (the sibling task)

task.body: The Port driver (Harness.AgentAdapter.Driver) reaches UP into the run-lifecycle layer: it aliases Harness.Run.Reflex (driver.ex:57) and calls new/3, expired/1, wait/1, on_output/2 for its idle/total/progress watchdog (driver.ex:134,154,159,173,190). Reflex (lib/harness/run/reflex.ex) is not a leaf: it pulls Harness.Worktree.Isolation -> Harness.Git, and Isolation.validate/1 calls BACK into Harness.AgentAdapter.supports?/2 — a dependency cycle and a layering violation (a low-level Port driver depending on a higher-level run module). Break it so the adapter subsystem depends on nothing above itself: abstract the watchdog behind a behaviour/callback the Driver invokes without naming Reflex (harness injects the Reflex-backed implementation), OR relocate the lifetime/idle/progress-timer machinery the Driver actually uses down into the subsystem and keep only checkout-pollution detection (snapshot/check_pollution, which the Driver does NOT use) up in Run. Either way: `grep -rE "Harness\.Run" lib/harness/agent_adapter` returns nothing, and Isolation no longer calls back into AgentAdapter from a module the Driver transitively depends on. This is genuine architectural hygiene (a real module cycle) regardless of extraction; it is the second of two decoupling cuts that make the subsystem extraction-ready.

task.title: Widen over-tight mix.exs dep constraints + guard against regression
acceptance_criteria: Every three-part `~> x.y.z` dep constraint in mix.exs without a justifying inline comment is widened to two-part `~> x.y`
mix deps.get and mix compile succeed after widening; mix.lock remains the source of exact resolved versions
A guard (credo check or mix ci assertion) fails when a new over-tight three-part `~>` constraint is added without a justifying inline comment, and passes on the widened mix.exs
A test covers the guard flagging an over-tight pin and accepting a justified one
out_of_scope: Actually upgrading deps to newer versions (the dep-bump dispatch task owns that)
Widening constraints in registered target projects — this is harness's own mix.exs only
task.body:
Harness's own mix.exs carries some three-part `~> x.y.z` dependency constraints (e.g. `{:plug, "~> 1.19.2"}`), which resolve to `>= x.y.z and < x.(y+1).0` and therefore exclude already-released compatible minors (1.20.1). This is a self-inflicted "can't update" block: the constraint, not hex, is what stops the bump, and a lazy agent reports the package as blocked instead of widening the pin.

Sweep every over-tight three-part `~>` constraint in mix.exs to the idiomatic two-part `~> x.y` (resolving to `< (x+1).0.0`), letting mix.lock remain the real pin and `mix deps.update` + the reviewer suite control the exact resolved version. Then add a guard so over-tight pins cannot regress silently — a credo check or a `mix ci` assertion that flags any new three-part `~>` constraint UNLESS it carries an inline comment justifying the tight pin (the one narrow legitimate case: a dep with a real minor-bump breakage history). Do not widen a constraint that already carries such a justification comment.

Add an operator-triggered "update deps" action that dispatches a dependency-bump task through the normal agent-gate (implementer -> reviewer -> land), rather than mechanically running `mix deps.update` in harness (which would reintroduce the deleted mechanical verification path). Surface it as a dashboard button (per project) and an MCP tool.

The dispatch plumbing is language-agnostic; the bump prompt is built from `project.languages` (a prompt provider per supported ecosystem, not a new dispatch path) — the Elixir prompt covers mix.exs / `mix deps.update` / `mix test.json --include integration`, and later providers can cover Cargo.toml / npm/pnpm/yarn / go.mod. task.title: Project languages invariant + multi-language provider substrate
acceptance_criteria: `%Harness.Project{}` uses explicit `languages` as a non-empty list of atoms; the old singular `language` field is removed from the runtime struct

Existing persisted project payloads with old singular `language` are backfilled to explicit `languages` (`nil` -> `[:elixir]`, atom -> `[atom]`) and re-persisted so runtime callers do not keep seeing legacy nil

Freshness and tooling-baseline provider resolution iterates `project.languages`, runs every available provider, and records unsupported languages as visible skipped facts rather than treating them as errors or Elixir
Mixed projects such as `[:elixir, :rust]` run Elixir facts today and are structurally ready for Rust/JS/Go providers without another project-model migration
Dashboard, MCP/dispatch registration, rule injection, CodeSearch, ProjectExplorer, and tests are updated to the explicit multi-language contract
Existing Elixir-only behavior is preserved for `languages: [:elixir]`; non-Elixir-only projects do not receive Elixir conformance or Elixir-only code search
Tests cover required-language rejection, single-language projects, mixed-language projects, legacy persistence backfill, provider skip facts, and dashboard language rendering
out_of_scope: Implementing Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript, or Go dependency-freshness providers
Defining Rust/JS/Go tooling-baseline manifests
Changing dependency-bump or tooling-baseline dispatch actions beyond making them consume `project.languages`
task.body:
Make the project language model explicit and future-proof before adding more ecosystem providers. The current singular `project.language` shape cannot model mixed repositories such as rexex, and treating `nil` as Elixir creates a hidden compatibility path that will keep biting later. Replace it with `project.languages`, a required non-empty list of atoms.

New registration must be strict: attrs or JSON/MCP calls without `languages` fail; `:mixed` is not allowed because it erases the actual provider set. Existing persisted rows are data debt, not a runtime fallback: decode old payloads, convert `language: nil` to `languages: [:elixir]`, convert old singular atoms to one-element lists, and write the normalized payload back so runtime consumers only see explicit languages.

Then update the existing provider substrate to iterate languages. Today only Elixir freshness/conformance providers exist, so mixed projects should produce Elixir facts plus visible skipped facts for unsupported languages. Future Rust/JavaScript/Go providers must be additive tasks plugged into this seam, not another project-model refactor.

task.title: Run gen_statem crashes with case_clause when cancel reason is {:redispatched, run_id}
acceptance_criteria: Cancelling a run with a structured reason such as {:redispatched, run_id} settles the run without a gen_statem crash
The settled record preserves the structured reason for verdict/status readers (naming the successor run_id)
The original run's run_record no longer reads :run_crashed when its task was successfully redispatched (ledger hygiene)
A regression test covers cancel-with-structured-reason during an in-flight run

Reworking progress_stalled detection
task.body:
Observed 2026-07-04 dispatching tapakly task 330 (run-1783129787191-c1482f84): the run settled failed with reason {:run_crashed, {:case_clause, {:cancel, {:redispatched, "run-1783130107972-4f577d15"}}}}. Something (the reflex redispatch path) cancelled the superseded run with a structured reason {:redispatched, new_run_id}, and a case/cond in the Run gen_statem's cancel handling only matches the plain :cancelled shape, so the process crashed instead of settling cleanly. The redispatched replacement run itself then halted with {:reflex_halted, :progress_stalled}, so the crash also cost the retry context. Find the cancel-reason case, accept structured cancel reasons (or normalize them before the match), and settle the superseded run as failed/cancelled without a crash.

2026-07-06 content-review note — crash site located: Harness.Run.route_reflex_halt/2 (lib/harness/run.ex ~1631) case-matches only :ok | {:cancel, {:blocked, _}} | {:error, _} from Resilience.route/2, but the reflex-halt redispatch path (Harness.Lander.Resilience.redispatch/3, lib/harness/lander/resilience.ex:178) returns {:cancel, {:redispatched, run_id}} — the unmatched shape IS the case_clause. Fix belongs there (accept {:cancel, reason} generally and settle/witness the structured reason), not in the handle_common :cancel call handler, which already normalizes caller cancels to :cancelled.

2026-07-07 dedupe note — recurred on tapakly task 359 (run-1783371223893-b56b7a77): same {:run_crashed, {:case_clause, {:cancel, {:redispatched, ...}}}} settle while the successor run completed and was approved, so the ledger records :run_crashed for a task that actually shipped. task.title: Land-conflict resolver AI cannot spawn: claude adapter has no configured agent_model
acceptance_criteria: Resolver spawn resolves the agent's configured model via the same lookup the reviewer spawn uses; a configured agent never yields {:model_required, _} from the resolver path

A selected candidate without a configured model rotates to the next eligible cross-family candidate; only when no candidate has a model does the resolve fall back to the existing blocked/retained-branch path
Resolver witness records which agent+model ran (or why none could)
Regression test: conflict + configured reviewer models -> resolver actually spawns (no model_required); conflict + all candidates model-less -> clean fallback to blocked
out_of_scope: Changing when the lander invokes the resolver or the keep-both resolution default
Reviewer model-resolution semantics (Run.reviewer_model) beyond reusing its lookup
Re-running checks in the resolver seat
task.body:
Observed 2026-07-04 on tapakly run run-1783130780286-70e6a32b: the lander hit a rebase conflict (T329 vs T332 gettext catalogs) and the land-conflict resolver AI failed to spawn with {:model_required, Harness.AgentAdapter.Claude} — the claude adapter has no {:agent_model, agent} pin configured, and the resolver path (like the reviewer) resolves its model solely from agent_model config. The land stayed blocked and required manual worktree repair.

Decide + fix: either (a) operator config — pin a standing model for the claude adapter (Config.agent_model) so recovery/resolver/reviewer seats can always spawn on it, and document that model-capable recovery seats require a pin at project-registration/onboarding time; or (b) code — have the resolver seat rotate to the next cross-family candidate with a configured model instead of failing the land when the first candidate is model-less (mirroring the reviewer-rotation behavior). Either way, a rebase-conflict land should degrade to another resolver candidate, not to a blocked task needing hand repair. Human decision spike on (a) vs (b); (b) becomes dispatchable once chosen.

2026-07-05 update — decision resolved to (b) by new evidence: the failure recurred twice on tapakly auto-lands (task 348: {:model_required, Harness.AgentAdapter.Codex}; task 344 / run-1783226904876-5c5b2e99: {:model_required, Harness.AgentAdapter.Claude}) while agents-reviewers showed BOTH adapters with configured models (claude-opus-4-8 / gpt-5.5). Config pins exist, so this is not the (a) config gap — the resolver spawn path does not resolve {:agent_model, agent} (or the Run.reviewer_model equivalent) before spawning. Fix per (b): resolve the model the same way the reviewer spawn does; rotate to the next eligible cross-family candidate when the selected one is model-less; blocked + retained branch stays the terminal sink. Witness which agent+model ran (or why none could).

2026-07-07 dedupe note — fourth recurrence: tapakly task 362 (run-1783371226312-2655d89b), gettext-catalog rebase conflict, resolver witness "selection/spawn failed: {:model_required, Harness.AgentAdapter.Claude}"; operator repaired manually (union-merge .po catalogs + gettext.refresh + dispatch-reland). Live config re-check this date confirms agent_model.claude = "claude-opus-4-8" IS set, re-confirming decision (b): the resolver spawn path simply never resolves {:agent_model, agent}. Candidate selection must additionally skip genuinely model-less candidates (mirror reviewer-slate eligibility), per the folded-in duplicate task 355 (superseded into this one).

task.body: Observed twice on tapakly auto-lands (2026-07-05, task 348 and task 344 / run-1783226904876-5c5b2e99): on a rebase conflict the lander's cross-family resolver selection/spawn fails with {:model_required, Harness.AgentAdapter.Codex} resp. {:model_required, Harness.AgentAdapter.Claude}, so the resolve attempt never runs and the task goes straight to blocked for manual repair — even though both agents HAVE configured models (agents-reviewers shows claude-opus-4-8 / gpt-5.5). task.title: Worktree sweeper is depth-blind: */* glob never finds leaked landing/audit worktrees after a crash mid-land

Changing the landing/audit worktree path layout
task.body: Sweeper.candidates/1 (sweeper.ex:69-71) discovers orphans with a fixed-depth Path.join(base_dir, "*/*") glob, but Worktree.checkout_existing/3 — used by the lander AND the post-merge audit for their detached worktrees — creates paths three levels deep: <base_dir>/<repo_slug>/landing/<id> (worktree.ex:352/368). If the BEAM crashes between checkout_existing and Worktree.remove/1 (the crash-mid-land class the Oban Lifeline work documented — Task 209, job 294), the leaked worktree is never found on any later boot: the glob matches .../landing itself, which has no .git marker, so parent_repo/1 returns nil and it is left in place; the actual <id> worktree one level deeper is never a candidate. Reaper only tracks Run-created worktrees (Reaper.track/4); Lifeline only rescues the Oban job row — nothing else covers this. Make discovery depth-agnostic (e.g. recursively find .git regular FILES under base_dir and reap their dirnames) rather than assuming the two-level shape. task.body: Three coupled fixes in the chat session surface, found by codebase review 2026-07-06 (sites verified against HEAD). task.body: block_with_id/1 (task_id_rewriter.ex:58-64) matches only the quoted form id = "N" (regex ^\s*id\s*=\s*"(\d+)"\s*$), so rewrite_collisions/2 finds zero blocks — and reassigns nothing — for a project whose tasks.toml uses unquoted integer ids. task.body: run_records accretes full agent_output/reviewer_output transcript blobs per run (the backend parity test exercises 50KB blobs) and nothing anywhere prunes, archives, or TTLs rows — no delete_all/prune/retention path exists outside unrelated worktree cleanup. task.body: Observed 2026-07-07, tapakly task 362, run run-1783371226312-2655d89b: the lander hit a rebase conflict (gettext catalogs), and the conflict-resolver attempt failed before spawning with 'resolver witness: selection/spawn failed: {:model_required, Harness.AgentAdapter.Claude}' — the resolver selected the claude adapter, which had no configured {:agent_model, agent}, so the whole resolver attempt died and the task went to blocked for manual repair. task.title: Chat turn-worker crash must fail fast to the caller — monitor instead of bare receive; map ensure_session already_started
acceptance_criteria: A turn-worker crash surfaces to a blocked user_message/3 caller immediately (test: crashing backend -> caller returns/exits well before its timeout, never the full-timeout hang)

task.body: Follow-on to task 348 (landed run run-1783390322257-fd5d8940). The turn now runs in a spawn_link'ed worker; an abnormal worker crash still kills the non-trapping session GenServer (same failure surface as before), but user_message/3 callers now park in a bare receive waiting for {:harness_chat_turn, ...} and only leave via their own after-timeout — previously GenServer.call exited immediately when the server died. ChatLive's fire-and-forget 600s Task therefore hangs 10 minutes on a crashed turn, and no :terminal reaches the stream, so the composer sticks. Flagged independently by the run's cross-family reviewer (review_warning concern) and the orchestrator architecture review 2026-07-07. Fix: have the caller monitor the session (receive {:DOWN, ...} -> immediate exit/return), or trap the worker exit in the session and emit_terminal a :crashed terminal + reply before stopping. Fold-in (same files, same seam): ChatSupervisor.ensure_session/1 currently returns the raw {:error, {:already_started, pid}} when two callers race the cold start — map it to {:ok, session_id, pid}.

task.body:
Surfaced by the 2026-07-12 project health audit (arch-review.md #1). `mix xref graph --format
cycles` reports ONE strongly-connected cycle of 71 modules (~30% of the codebase) spanning
run-lifecycle internals, the lander, the entire dashboard/* tree, chat/*, cron/*, MCP
surface, roadmap, manifest, result_store, and more. The codebase has no enforced layering:
you cannot compile or reason about any one of these modules independently of the rest.

A chunk of the cycle traces to `Harness.Manifest`'s @driver_surface list (curated module
atoms consumed by descripex to build the MCP/chat tool manifest) creating export/compile
edges back into Dispatch/Run/Roadmap, while dashboard LiveViews and Describe/Chat.Tools read
Manifest in the reverse direction — folding the whole app into one component instead of
`core → manifest → {chat, mcp, dashboard}` one-way layering.

Do the work in two moves:
1. AUDIT which edges in the 71-cycle are genuine bidirectional business logic vs accidental
   doc/alias/`@driver_surface` references pulling a cold-path module into the warm-path
   compile graph. The driver-surface core (Run, Roadmap, Dispatch, ResultStore, Lander, …)
   must never depend on Manifest, Chat.*, or Dashboard.* — only the reverse.
2. Break the reverse edges and ENCODE the layering as a boundary policy in `.reach.exs`
   (`boundaries[:public]` facade + forbidden cross-boundary calls) so `mix reach.check --arch`
   gates it going forward — a re-introduced reverse edge becomes a CI failure, not a
   whole-surface discovery.

This is the highest-blast-radius task in the audit set; keep behaviour identical and lean on
the full suite. Ignore the four idiomatic behaviour↔impl store cycles and the parser
dispatch-table cycle (arch-review #5/#6) — those are the standard behaviour+default-impl
pattern, not the target here.

task.title: Decision: resolve the anubis_mcp LGPL-3.0 runtime-dependency licensing exposure on the public repo
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision (accept-with-rationale / upstream-ask / replace) on the anubis_mcp LGPL-3.0 runtime exposure, documented in the repo (NOTICE / THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES preferred over SECURITY.md — it is a licensing record, not a security posture)
The write-up frames the BEAM-release/LGPL relink question as a compliance question that was answered (with the reasoning), not as pre-established legal fact
If accept: the rationale is written down so future audits do not re-flag it as open
out_of_scope: Any dependency/code change until the licensing decision is made — this task is the decision itself
task.body:
Surfaced by the 2026-07-12 project health audit (deps-audit.md #1). `{:anubis_mcp, "~> 1.6"}`
(locked 1.6.2) is a HARD RUNTIME dependency — it backs Harness.Dashboard.MCPServer, not an
optional/dev tool — and its license is GNU LGPL-3.0 (confirmed from upstream LICENSE at
github.com/zoedsoupe/anubis-mcp). Every other runtime dep (Phoenix/Ecto/Postgrex/Oban/Req/
Bandit family) is permissive (MIT/Apache-2.0).

LGPL is copyleft-lite: LGPL-3.0 attaches relink/replacement conditions to combined works,
and whether a BEAM mix release / escript (compiling the dependency straight in) satisfies
the "dynamic linking" boundary LGPL relies on is an OPEN COMPLIANCE QUESTION for this
decision to answer, not established legal fact — premise unverified, resolve it as part of
the decision (upstream guidance, Erlang Ecosystem Foundation / hex licensing discussions,
or counsel if it matters enough). harness is a PUBLIC repo, so this warrants a one-time
licensing decision rather than a silent accept.

This is a HUMAN decision task (not a code dispatch). Decide one of: (a) accept the LGPL
exposure with a documented rationale in NOTICE / THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES, (b) contribute to / request a
license change upstream, or (c) evaluate an alternative MCP library / vendor the minimal
surface under a compatible license. Whichever, record the decision so it does not resurface
each audit.

task.title: ResultStore.Postgres list/aggregate path fails whole query on atom decode — tolerant row decode like the File store
acceptance_criteria: list_run_records/0-2 on the Postgres store returns every decodable record even when one or more rows reference atoms not loaded in the current BEAM
Skipped/degraded rows surface as one aggregated Logger.debug line per scan, not a per-row warning and not a whole-query error
A regression test inserts a row whose jsonb references an unknown atom-like key and asserts healthy siblings are still returned
Live repro path re-checked: result_store-list_run_records MCP tool returns records against the dev BEAM instead of ArgumentError
task.body:
Observed 2026-07-14 against the live dev BEAM (store configured as {Harness.ResultStore.Postgres, []}):
`Harness.ResultStore.list_run_records()` — no filters, and every filtered variant — returns
`{:error, %ArgumentError{message: "... not an already existing atom"}}`, and the flat MCP tool
`result_store-list_run_records` surfaces the same error. The Postgres backend's read path atomizes
stored string keys/values (check_output/ratings/facets jsonb or filter translation) via
String.to_existing_atom, so a row referencing an atom not loaded in the current BEAM fails — and one
bad row (or field) kills the ENTIRE listing, exactly the File-store halt bug fixed for term files
(ResultStore.File tolerant read: skip + aggregate-log). Point lookups by run_id via SQL still work,
which is how the data was recovered (blockwatch tasks 2-22 reviewer provenance).

Fix in the File store's spirit: decode rows tolerantly — a row (or jsonb field) that fails atom-safe
decode is skipped (or decoded with string keys preserved) and counted in one aggregated debug log,
never failing the whole query. Audit ResultStore.Postgres for String.to_existing_atom /
binary_to_term(:safe) sites on the read path; the never-raise best-effort contract already holds
(error tuple, not raise) but an all-or-nothing error tuple is still an unusable query surface for
orchestrators and the dashboard.

task.body:
Add a Harness.AgentAdapter for Kimi Code (Moonshot's coding CLI, installed at
~/.kimi-code/bin/kimi, v0.26.0, docs https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/).
Parallels Task 52 (pi.dev) — thin adapter, uniform OTP Port, raw output captured
verbatim, reviewer AI is the gate.

Known CLI facts (verify again against the installed binary before coding; authority order:
live CLI > current official docs > this body): headless mode is
`kimi -p/--prompt <prompt>` with `--output-format stream-json`; `-m/--model <model>`
pins the model. Installed v0.26.0 and the current command reference disagree with the old
task premise: prompt mode cannot be combined with `--yolo`, `--auto`, or `--plan`, and
already uses autonomous permissions. Do not emit `--yolo` on the prompt path. Probe
`kimi provider --help` and its catalog subcommands for this installed version before
choosing the model-list command; `provider list` may list providers rather than models.
`-c/--continue` resumes the working directory's previous session and `-S/--session <id>`
resumes by id — pick only combinations the live CLI accepts. Kimi consumes AGENTS.md
(its system-prompt template embeds a KIMI_AGENTS_MD block), so
`:codex_ephemeral_file` is a hypothesis; prove the discovery semantics (cwd walk-up vs
explicit) before choosing the channel.
Kimi-specific extras (--skills-dir, --add-dir, --plan, acp/server subcommands) stay
out of the four-callback contract per the Pi precedent. Auth is subscription-style

auth_env_scrub declaration, and cite the doc or observed behavior either way.

acceptance_criteria: review.json schema gains an optional proposed_tasks array (title, body, suggested scores/markers, evidence); Run.Result carries it and dispatch-verdict_detail exposes it
Reviewer prompt/rules instruct the reviewer to propose discoveries via proposed_tasks and to never edit roadmap/tasks.toml, roadmap/data.json, ROADMAP.md, or CHANGELOG.md in the worktree
Run staging excludes roadmap/tasks.toml, roadmap/data.json, ROADMAP.md, and CHANGELOG.md from the deliverable commit (same mechanism as the .harness/ exclusion), so a run diff contains only code
A run whose reviewer proposes tasks lands cleanly with the proposals readable from the persisted record after worktree teardown

Docs updated: skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md and priv/includes/harness-workflow.md describe the proposal flow and that the ORCHESTRATOR files proposals through its own task-writing gate (dedupe/merge against the live pending set) after the land; sync script run
out_of_scope: Harness auto-filing proposals into any roadmap (judgment about filing stays with the orchestrator AI, per the mantra)
Changing how the lander advances the dispatched task's own status (done --shipped-in stays)

task.body:
Observed in ccxt_client dispatch (2026-07-19): reviewers file discovery tasks by
editing roadmap/tasks.toml inside their run worktree. The worktree forks from an
older base, so the reviewer assigns the next task id of ITS fork while origin has
moved on — producing id collisions that block the lander (task 433 land blocked:
its reviewer filed id 437, already taken on origin), orphaned data.json-only
renders, and singleton tasks that never pass the one-session=one-task merge gate
because the reviewer cannot see the live pending set. Roadmap and CHANGELOG files
are also a universal write-set overlap that defeats write-set-disjoint parallel
dispatch: every run touches them, so "disjoint" waves still conflict at landing.

Fix the channel, not the judgment: the reviewer keeps proposing tasks (that
judgment is valuable), but as structured data in the verdict artifact instead of
roadmap commits. Harness mechanically carries the proposals through Result and
the persisted record; the driving orchestrator files them centrally after the
land, where it can dedupe, merge, and gate them against the real roadmap state.

task.title: Coalesce-dispatch: run N small same-bundle tasks as one implementer run
acceptance_criteria: A dispatch surface (dispatch-bundle option or new tool) accepts an explicit list of task ids and runs them as ONE Harness.Run: one worktree, one implementer invocation with all task prompts, one reviewer gate, one land
The reviewer verdict records per-task outcomes so the lander can advance each coalesced task's roadmap status individually (all done --shipped-in the same sha, or the run fails as a unit)
Write-set union of the coalesced tasks is what enters wave serialization
In-flight idempotency still holds: re-dispatching any member task while the coalesced run is live returns the existing run
Docs: harness-driver SKILL + harness-workflow include describe when to coalesce (small tasks sharing a bundle/surface) vs parallelize; sync script run
out_of_scope: Automatic selection of which tasks to coalesce (the orchestrator picks; harness executes)
Partial landing of a subset of coalesced tasks (unit semantics for v1)
task.body:
Pipeline fixed costs (worktree fork, deps bootstrap, cold checks, reviewer boot)
are ~20-40 min per run regardless of task size, so a D3 task pays the same
overhead as a D7 one. Observed in ccxt_client 2026-07-19: several sub-hour tasks
each consumed a full run's fixed costs; the operator called for bundling. The
one-session=one-task rule catches this at filing time when one author sees both
tasks, but reviewer/sweep discoveries arrive as separate valid tasks whose merge
window has passed. Give the orchestrator a dispatch-time coalesce primitive: one
implementer session lands N small related tasks under one review, matching what a
human session would naturally do.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1784509159980-54c2a6b7, aacf879fe4e55668a905cd83020e116be025943a).

task.title: Lander fallback: mechanically resolve additive-only tasks.toml conflicts by renumbering
acceptance_criteria: When the landing rebase conflicts ONLY in roadmap/tasks.toml (plus its data.json/ROADMAP.md renders) and both sides' changes are purely additive [[task]] blocks, the lander renumbers the branch-side new tasks to the next free ids on the target, re-renders via rmap, and completes the land
Any non-additive conflict (edits to existing task blocks, code files) still retains the branch and blocks as today

String references to the renumbered id inside the same branch diff (CHANGELOG lines, code comments, test names) are either rewritten with the renumber or the land is left blocked with a report naming them - silent broken references are not acceptable
A test covers: clean renumber, non-additive conflict left blocked, and in-diff reference rewrite/refusal
out_of_scope: Semantic dedupe/merge of the added tasks against the target roadmap (orchestrator judgment)
Conflicts in files other than the roadmap render set
task.body:
Sequential integer task ids plus parallel worktrees make additive tasks.toml
collisions structural: two runs filing discoveries both claim the next id, the
second one to land conflicts, and today the lander retains the branch and blocks
the task - a purely mechanical repair (renumber the additive block, re-render,
push) that currently costs an operator/orchestrator session (observed ccxt_client
task 433, 2026-07-19: reviewer filed id 437, origin had taken it; hand repair
took cherry-pick + renumber + reland). Renumbering additive blocks is counting,
not judgment, so it belongs in the lander per the mantra.

Note: the reviewer-proposals task (same date, agent-gate bundle) removes the
MAIN source of these conflicts by taking reviewers out of tasks.toml entirely;
this fallback covers the residual class (operator or parallel-session filings
racing a land). If that task lands first and the residual rate is ~zero, honor
an honest re-score downward instead of building on momentum.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1784507322519-810e046e, 2f3ed81476802c8fade2fe480f78902737aab44d).

task.title: Settle-persist must survive schema/DB drift: never silently lose a run record on a failed insert
acceptance_criteria: A run whose settle-time run_records insert fails (e.g. Postgrex undefined_column from a pending migration) still ends with a durable record: the payload is spilled to a durable dead-letter (file or table) and replayed automatically once the insert path works again, or an equivalent no-loss mechanism
The failure is surfaced loudly to the operator (notification sink / dashboard warning), not only a log warning
Pending-migration drift is detectable: a boot-time or persist-failure-time check names the unapplied migrations in the warning
Test covers: insert failure -> record recovered after the schema is fixed; lander landed_sha writeback failure on the same run does not crash the landing
Integration evidence: reproduce the undefined_column class against a test schema and pin observed error semantics
out_of_scope: Auto-running migrations on the live node (operator decision)
Read-side tolerant row decode (task 365 owns that)
Reconstructing historical lost records (operator judgment)
task.body:
Observed 2026-07-20 on the harness node itself: task 367 auto-landed a migration
(add_review_proposed_tasks_to_run_records); the long-lived dev node hot-reloaded
the new schema module via code reloading while the DB was still unmigrated. From
that moment every run_records statement failed with Postgrex undefined_column
(pg_code 42703): the settle-time insert for run-1784509159980-54c2a6b7 (task 368,
reviewer-approved and successfully landed at aacf879f) was dropped after a single
attempt, the lander's landed_sha writeback updated zero rows, and the status view
went blind — while the land itself succeeded. Result: an approved, landed run with
NO persisted record (dispatch-status not_found), which breaks the recovery
primitives (reland/rereview read the record), KPI rollups, and the token ledger.

Best-effort persistence is fine as a policy; silent single-shot loss is not.
Under dogfooding this drift class is structural: harness lands migrations into
its own running host, and nobody has run ecto.migrate yet. Keep the fix
mechanical per the mantra: spill-and-replay plus loud drift surfacing, no
auto-judgment about the migration itself.

Evidence: node log 09:15:19-09:27 2026-07-20 (+08) — failed INSERT with full
payload, failed landed_sha writeback, repeated status-view failures.
